Fran Bow is a game I was looking forward to playing forever and I recently got a chance to sit down and finish it, but was it worth the wait or my time was wasted ?
In Fran Bow we play as a young girl named Fran. One day her family is brutally murdered and she is put in an asylum so she can cope with the loss of her parents, but she finds out that there is a dark force behind the death of her parents and she has to find her cat and find out the true reason her parents died.
First of all I want to start off the review with everything Fran Bow does right.
The gameplay is a simple adventure game where you go around environments and pick up stuff, combine and use the things in your inventory to solve a bunch of puzzles, but this game twists this sort of gameplay into something different.
Early on in the game Fran is given pills which reveal a second world to her which is filled with all sorts of monster and death. The second dimension is there to help you solve puzzles and pick up items you normally can't pick up in the real world.
Atmosphere plays a big part in Fran Bow. Early on in the game and even in the later chapters of the game the atmosphere is always creepy and it never stops even in the calmer chapters of the game. The second world which is accessed by the pills Fran can take is insanely creepy and most of the things in this game is really disturbing.
The sound design is also really well designed, but in some chapters it's weirdly executed. In some screens there's music and in others there's only the nature effects like owls hooting and crickets chirping which helps set the mood.
Now for the puzzles. Most of the time the puzzles aren't easy even going to the point of classic adventure games where they don't make any sense. The first few chapters of the game are fairly simple, but still challenging, but later chapters get incredibly tedious, due to how complex the puzzles get.
After some chapters you also get mini games like a jumping across gaps game which is similar to endless runners on mobile phones (but this one has an ending) and a frogger type game.
It took me 8 hours to finish the entire game and get every single achievement. After the game is finished there's no replay value whatsoever.
One of my main problems with the game is that the mood of the game changes way too quickly and even in the darker moments of the game which I loved are ruined by comedic moments which are ruin the mood. This starts to happen in the mysterious kingdom chapter where the chapter disrupts the flow of the game.
In the end did I enjoy Fran Bow ? Yeah, I did. It's a great adventure game, but it has flaws which I can't overlook and in the end I suggest checking out the game on a discount and not at full price.
Final Rating:
7/10
Pros:
+ Great Art Style
+ Atmosphere is amazing
Cons:
-Non logical puzzles
-Later chapters disrupt flow of the game

Neon Drive is a retro obstacle avoiding game with a heavy 80’s theme going on. The game looks so awesome...i mean ‘radical’. The game will test your reaction time, your twitch reflexes and your timing as well as memorization of where the obstacles are in a level.
As it’s name “Neon Drive” and being an 80’s inspired theme, everything is neon, the car is neon, the road is neon, the obstacles is neon and it looks EPIC. I mean when i started this game I literally said out loud “woah!”. Superb graphics. The game is pure eye candy. I was constantly getting above 100 FPS with V-Sync off. Game is smooth as silk. Such type of game requires the smoothest gameplay because timing really matters in this game. Even the start menu is really nice and the level selection screen are a bunch of arcade cabinets. The backgrounds in each level also look amazing, from city skylines, to abstract art to night skies. All of them look beautiful and pleasing to the eyes.
Totally awesome 80’s techno music. Each level features it’s own track and all of them are equally good. I especially like the 1st and 6th level tracks. It’s got awesome sound track and I don’t even lick techno music that much but this music was really cool.
Game is basically different modes e.g one is where you’re in third person and you have to avoid obstacles coming your way. Another mode is top down view where you have to avoid cars. There is also modes where you get to go on a plane and even a 2d robot scrolling mode etc. There are 4 lanes which you can move in, the timing of your lane switch matters as if you do it too soon or too late you will crash into the obstacle and die. Once you die you restart the game from beginning of the level or if you have reached the checkpoint, you’ll start from there. Usually the checkpoint is at 50% through the level. Level 7 is quite unique as in that level you’re on a dynamometer and 2 robot arms are producing blocks in different lanes and you must avoid those. That said there is a lot of variety so you won’t get bored doing the same thing over and over.
There are 7 levels total and you can play them in any order. I highly suggest start with the first one as it’s one of the easiest, later levels are extremely hard. There’s 3 difficulty modes in every level, normal, hard and insane. The normal and insane difficulties are locked and once you beat the level in normal mode these will unlock. The hard and insane difficulties will increase the speed of the car. This game is very hard and will test your reflex, reaction time, timing and short-term memory (and patience :P )
There’s also an endurance mode which lets you play all the 7 levels in order back to back. So you can even beat all the levels in one sitting if you’re skilled enough.
Levels 1-3 will give you the same car but in different colors, the last 4 levels will give you a different car in each level. You can also customize your car number plate with upto 4 letters. Just scroll to the left in the main menu and edit the number plate.

I have a concern: why is Fran Bow not as popular as Undertale?
Here are some of the possible reasons I've come up with:
1. It's a horror game, unlike Undertale, which is allegedly suitable for all age (and I believe we all agree).
2. It came out 2 weeks before undertale came out. Undertale captured gamers' attention so much that no one paid attention to great games like Fran Bow.
3. There are many similarities between Fran Bow and Undertale (which, if you play it, you'll see my point), including the design of the characters, the way the story is told, and so on.
4. The soundtracks aren't as immersive as the ones in Undertale.
5. Some puzzles in this game are simply too hard to solve without using the community guide, which significantly slows down the pace of the game.
Despite such odds, I would have to say that this game is not a bit worse than undertale, considering its strong narrative style, special perception of different realities, and a very disturbing cue that is essential to the development of the plot.
One improvement that could be made to make this game even better is to make the ending more philosophical and less abrupt. In comparison with the intriguing narrative throughout the whole game, the ending was kind of abrupt to me. There are lots of things left unexplained on purpose, but I feel like the producer could have explained a little bit more just to clarify some fundamental facts of Fran Bow.
I strongly recommend Fran Bow to anyone who likes horror games and puzzle games, and the combinations of both. The story of this game is extremely outstanding for a horror game, and is extremely disturbing for a puzzle game. Believe me, most of you will love it.

This is one of the best games i've played. a good sequel to Doom 1 and 2, maybe not as fast paced as those, but still a great sequel that keeps you on your toes and bridges the gap between classic and modern day shooters... It has all the elements of a classic shooter like great level design, backtracking, medkits for health regen and a very fun corridor shooting mechanic, and the graphics that easily pass for a modern day shooter with the help of some texture mods..
I strongly advise u not to play the vanilla bfg edition but mod it with HD Resolution pack version 2.7 (as of 12th March 2016) and it's updates 2.7b, etc, or if you're feeling lazy just use the Ultimate Mod pack that's not fully updated, but still an easy way to get most of the good features like good graphics, improved A.I, where the imps are a menace and the zombie marines take cover avoiding your fire... yes the imps are a big threat as opposed to the original Doom games. They jump at you if u miss a shot close range.... And the mod improves gun physics as well..
The guns are the same as classic doom.. You have everything from the oh-so-brutal chainsaw (easy to use against melee slow walking zombies) to the plasma rifle to the ultimate B.F.G. Headshots are of prime importance in this game, more so than most other fps shooters, because it does 2-3 times more damage than a normal body shot, and you have to manage your ammo consumption of each gun just like in the classic old shooters, which by the way was such a great mechanic to have (god damn you you stupid lame military shooters) ...
Ultimately why this game is even better than most shooters out today is, it keeps you on your toes all the time, u are surrounded by enemies everywhere and the enemies are an ACTUAL threat, where they will jump at you each chance they get, unlike most games now where you are given targets in front for "shooting practice" and there is no point in backtracking in most games. either the games are like linear Call of Duty , or they are open world like Far Cry where backtracking doesn't matter , its all plain open grounds, whereas the level design in Doom is just FAN-TASTIC, just like classic Doom. You are given limited ammo and health , and u have to "manage" them by saving the larger medkits for later , especially on higher difficulties. and again, unlike most modern day shooters, when you backtrack for a large medkit , the game spawns extra enemies for you behind. I, who have played too many modern fps games, while backtracking, assume everything behind me is dead, and happily tend to reload all my guns only to be surprised by another IMP running straight at my face. so i basically take 10 damage out of nowhere just to get that 25 health medkit. oh well , atleast its worth it... Mostly....
And to top it all off, Doom BFG edition includes the classic Doom games as well, which again, is as good as Doom 3, and even better to some,  and DEFINITELY not outdated . I played all Dooms with mods in the last month, and i personally rate Doom 2 > Doom 3 > Doom 1.. THE most badass game series of ALL TIME.

Fran Bow is a difficult game to review.
From a standard point-and-click perspective, the game delivers wonderfully. The game manages to avoid the common problem many point-and-clicks face; ridiculous solutions or situations (kind of). Every solution to a problem you encounter throughout the game logically makes sense. The situations you come across are sensible in the way that it’s understandable when you cannot surmount a problem initially and have to find a solution. To try to explain more clearly, I’ll mention something I’ve seen plenty of times before in other games; Something is blocked by spider webs. Logically, you should be able to just move them out of the way with your hands, or even any nearby object that isn’t too large. However, the games would make you find a specific object, such as a brush or stick, to finally be able to pass an obstacle that should have been easily passed. Fran Bow manages to avoid having any of these fallacies. When I mentioned “kind of” earlier, I meant that while it achieves this, the situations are really anything but logical.
You play as a drugged out 10 year old girl with a mental disorder and a devastating experience. With this comes a story that goes further and further from reality. While it leads to a story that is unpredictable and exciting, it also loses cohesion and sense. What further hurts the story is that this lack of cohesion leads to it being very open and confusing. Instead of containing and bringing in the story at points to help the player with understanding what’s going on, it’s allowed to freely roam and becomes convoluted. It’s alright to have a story presented like this, don’t misinterpret me saying that’s a bad form of storytelling. However, there has to be understanding from the player. Maybe not initially, but eventually. There is no understanding. It’s never made clear even what’s going on. Things are abruptly introduced, and then just as abruptly dismissed or never brought up again. As mentioned before, there is absolutely zero cohesion as Fran jumps from one point to another. In the end, nothing is solved or answered, and no loose ends are tied. It was an ambitious way to tell the story, and I believe it fell completely flat.  The story was a mess.
Much of the appeal of the game to me was Fran. I greatly enjoyed seeing how she interacted with things, with her thoughts drawing conclusions that would have never have drawn myself. The creators did a fine job in capturing the idea that the girl was not mentally sound. I hope to see more games try to capture the type of character she was. It was because of her that I enjoyed the game.
So, to round everything up, I’ll have to say that I do not recommend it. While the game had many good things (I did not go into the graphics, but the hand-drawn 2D graphics are appealing), the story is essential to a point-and-click game. Bad storytelling that, quite frankly, never really ended is too large of a mark to be ignored. Reading through interpretations of the story, some of them are so vastly different from one another that you’d think it was never meant to follow a specific storyline.
On a minor note, I never got any achievements after the first three despite finishing the game. Not a big deal, but something to look out for.

I may be a bit late with this review, but i had nothing else to do, so why not?
Let's start with saying that the game is absolutly beautiful!
The combat system for all three factions is solid enough.
The story is questionable but enjoyable.
The sound of killing your enemy feels like in the movies.. only better!
Now... if i sum up al these good things about the game, why does it feel so dull?!
Predator:
You play as a unkouwn predator who is send off to a planet wich is 'ruled' by the marines, you continue trough some levels of killing marines and aliens until you end up in the tempel where you fight a boss-alien.
There isn't a real story tied to this guy..
But it's the most fun to kill enemies.
Alien:
You play as a predator (number 6), you and your mates escape from the laboratory from Wayne industries.
The whole point of this species is to root out all the other spieces on the planet and ultimatly number 6 to become the Queen of all xeno's.
You can see your own tail wich is cool,
you can walk on walls and ceiling, pretty fun!
combat is sometimes a bit strange.
You can hunt down harmless civilians and kill them in an awesome way!
The shadows are your friend!
The marines don't stand a chance if you play it smart!
Marines:
You are a marine wich you team has left you to complete their objective and you are guided by a fellow marine.
I didn't put much hours in this one because it's pretty boring at times.. it's the greatest challenge in the game and this playtrough has some horror elements.
You just use your rifle and pistol to kill all the Xeno's and predators..
that's a bit of a overview over the factions you can play.
Each faction has 5 levels each, wich is pretty low..
The levels feel all the same because you pass with each species trough the same levels but in a different order.
The levels become boring if you play for an hour trough, because yeah, everything you do is the same!
if you are looking for a game to stun you by it's awesome gameplay, then i can say that the first 2 levels give you such a feeling but after it's nothing more then just a straight line with some bumps here and there.
Game in overall feels dull and boring at sometimes and probably not worth the full 14.99€ instead go for 10€
I'll just recommond it because it isn't that bad!

Summary
------------------------------------
Things that I like in game:
-music (its rock/metal, im not fan of those genres but it goes well with game)
-visual effects
-idea
-funny moments in story mode
Now things that I don't like:
-sometimes is hard to spot next attack
-missing F12 for screenshots
-hard to play (even on easiest difficulty)
-can be irritating
-can't precalculate custom music
Would I recommend? Well if you can live with bad things in game, it can be fun. And in that case buy it on sale.
I voted "Yes" , but I wish that I can stay neutral.
Details
----------------------------
I watched videos about gameplay, and it seemed to me interesting.
When I started to play, tutorial was fine, explains nicely. However, when I started story mode (it has anime movies), even on easiest difficulty game was hard (first two levels especially). You need to watch where are enemies comming (you can't rely on music), and often is not clear who will first attack. Sometimes they both attack at same time, and in that case you need to use specific combo in order to not get kicked.
Most irritating thing for me is that once you miss, and get hit by enemies, it is really hard to stand up and continue (in fast music rythums, thats the case in 2nd level).
I can't imagine how it would be on harder difficulty.
Thing that I like in game is music and there are some good visual effects. Oh yea, you can't screenshot with F12 (which is shame, I missed some good shots).
Another bad thing is that when you put your own music, you need to press Space when you feel rhythum (for begining, middle and end of song). It's not scaling well (for example if song changes beat often). While this might be good thing for someone, I like more precalculated things.
Overall, I would say that concept is interesting, but it needs good tunning.

Is this game any good? Yes, yes it is, but it's definitely not "great". I still recommend it. Here's why:
Pros:
- Engaging story and characters (for an action RPG) with enough humour and charme to keep you entertained
- Interesting setting (It's a mixture of the industrial revolution with magic and monster hunters), with interesting enemy design etc.
- Gameplay is good enough
- Diverse skill tree
- Lots of items
- 3 distinct classes (I think the other classes were in VH 1 as DLC). The traditional hunter, a flamethrower type guy with advanced weapons and a mage
- 4 difficulty settings
- Ability to import chars from VH 1 or create an "expert char" at lvl 30
- "Endless mode" apparently
- Low price point
- Base of operations
Cons:
- The campaign is pretty short. I've beaten it on "Casual", because I'm not that interested in spending 20+ hours on this, in about 9 hours with every map fully explored. The story picks right off after Fulmigatis death from VH 1. This time you are up against General Harker, who takes over where the other villain died...well, eh. It's definitely necessary to view the VH series as a 3 episode game, because that's what it is. You're pretty lost without having played VH 1.
- The story has 2 major problems:
.
- The setting is still cool, but there is little new to it. I think a snowy peak and a spider level are the only new settings being used. The rest is typical wilderness and city...disappointed.
- The gameplay isn't bad, but it's also not entertaining for long, unlike say Diablo 3, where you have several active abilities and augmentations that can be switched around for lots of combinations. Here you basically get a limited amount of skill points to use 6 active skills (of which I only used the heal for the hunter, because honestly, weapon skills seemed more important) and also, theoretically, 8 weapon skills (4 melee and 4 ranged). I say theoretically, because you can only unlock so many skills that seem useful in 1 playthrough, because you also have to level them up 10 times to get the ultimate augmentation for it and to improve its damage. Since I barely made it to level 28 in my first playthrough, I didn't have a lot of diverse skills, because, frankly, there are just so many of them and so many seem redundant. You can't just pick up a new skill and try it out, because it might be completely useless without the augmentations or without levelling it up, which makes the system rather pointless in my opinion. Again, Diablo 3 for example does a much better job of just giving you skills to play around with, without forcing you to invest loads of skill points that you can only get back through a respec which costs a lot of money.)
- The crafting system: It's frankly very boring and apparently you cannot use the rune system until level 30, because items below that level can't be disenchanted for materials you need for runecrafting...that is seriously ♥♥♥♥♥♥.
- There are lots of items. Unfortunately, maybe 5% of the items that dropped were actually useful to me, which makes the experience rather dull...for example, if your campaign is only 8-9 hours long and your players have to use the same weapon for 3 hours then you failed in making the loot system interesting...also dropping loot that a player can't even use, because he is level 10 and you drop a level 38 sword is supremely dickish...I still have that sword in my stash.
- The game is imho not unique or interesting enough to play through again...so that is also a problem. There is no longevity.
- Even on the lowest difficulty setting you can get killed very easily, repeatedly, which is also kind of frustrating, for example when you are facing 3 mighty enemies and can barely pierce their shields, but get instagibbed by their non avoidable ranged attack, that is bad game design. I don't mind a challenge, but the hordes Van Helsing throws at you are ridiculous at times.
- The "base" gets annoying pretty quickly, because you get radioed frequently to return to base and complete some mission or whatever. Thankfully you do not have to do that...at all I think, dunno, you can also let your soldiers do the missions, but it interrupts the game flow pretty annoyingly and constantly.
- Money does not seem to be an issue in this game and I have no idea what to even spend it on...save for resurrects.
- The sound clipping is STILL present and is extremely annoying. Try a char who doesn't shoot with guns...*sigh*
All in all Van Helsing 2 does not improve in any way upon Van Helsing 1. The only new addition I can think of is the base and that's really a minor feature. The story is less engaging, the novelty has worn off. There are still funny moments, but they are less interesting in general. It feels rushed out and as I said like episode 2 of the same game, which it apparently is, since now we have Van Helsing 3, which I will be testing now, and which probably doesn't have any changes in it either. It's a bit sad, because I think you could really expand upon the game's crazy setting, but eh...maybe 3 is better.
Why do I still recommend it? Because it's a solid enough ARPG for almost no cost...it's cheaper than most games are even when heavily discounted. And for that it's good enough and entertaining for a short amount of time, especially if you want to continue your save from VH 1 (which I didn't have anymore, because not Steam and uninstalled, blah).

Doom 3: Console Remaster
That's exactly what this should have been called. To start off, let me say that the "BFG" edition of Doom 3 is worth $20 if you don't already own Doom 1, 2, 3, and RoE. It has all of those plus a new extra campaign. You can take the wad files and download a sourceport and have a good time with the older ones (as far as I've heard, I used the wad files from the other Doom releases). Doom 3, however, is a different story. It's undergone a lot of changes, and none of them are unquestionably good.
Among the changes are:
-"Updated" textures (most look worse than the original PC version)
-A LOT more health and ammo pickups (as well as modified values for said pickups to make the game easier)
-You no longer have to equip the flashlight to use it. For me, this neutered the horror aspect, but I honestly never had a problem with it in the original. This might be a positive to some people, though.
-No mod support. This is probably the worst thing about this edition is it isn't compatible with the already existing Doom 3 mods.
So...it's kind of a hit and miss. Yes, you get a ton of stuff in this package. All of the games are in one place for you to play. They all play fairly well, and the package is cheap.
BUT
They are all inferior to other versions. If the "BFG" edition had actually made the game look better, or changed some of the gameplay designs for the better, then I would recommend it completely. However, since there is no mod support, you're stuck with the "updated" textures.
6/10 overall for me, but if you have the other versions, don't bother. I mostly play the BFG edition out of laziness because I don't want to click a few more executables...so there's that I guess.

It features Doom 1+2 (all expansions), Doom 3 + RoE and Lost missions. I will cover all 3 games in this review so expect it to be a bit long.
Doom 1:
Seems like a HD version of the old MS-DOS game. It runs smooth and the gameplay is fun and fast paced (just like we remember it from the old times). Doom 1 is the shortest game in the series with 4 episodes where each episode takes place on different settings with new enemies. The map design is good, but I feel you can get lost sometimes. It takes time to get them keys and find hidden doors etc.  I think the soundtracks are what makes Doom so good. You hear bit-music in form of hard rock and heavy metal which fits perfectly with the setting. I had a lot of fun with Doom 1.
Doom 2: This one is a lot harder and longer than Doom 1. Runs smooth and looks good. It features over 30 levels (- the expansion), new enemies, new weapons and new soundtrack. Textures are different, the level design is so much better and we have more enemies at once. It took some time finishing 1 level, but damn it was fun exploring every inch of the map. I quickly understood that this one was harder since I struggled a lot on different places. The key is to get them secrets and strafe/dodge them pesky fireballs. The game starts where Doom 1 ended. I recommend you to just enjoy this one because it nails everything Doom 1 implemented and takes it to a whole new level. The expansion (no rest for the living) is even more fast paced and with tons of enemies at once. You need to be prepared for the Hell Knights and Barons, because they are everywhere!
Doom 3: This one takes the horror aspect as a main focus, while Doom 1+2 was more about the run and gun. The vanilla version of Doom 3 was really dark and you had to equip a flashlight to see most of the time. The graphics are improved in the BFG edition. I have to say it has aged well to be a 2005 game. The BFG edition is not so dark as the vanilla version, since you now have a flashlight mounted on your armour. It takes away the horror aspect, but I'm completely fine with it. It's more run and gun now with more ammo lying around etc. Doom 3 is more story driven. The story is exciting and explains the whole thing about how demons gets unleashed on Mars. Think I completed it at around 8-9 hours. It got some replayability where you can find hidden vide-logs and PDA's. The enemies are for the most from the previous games, but they have also added some new ones. They are all well made and scary to look at. Weapons are also almost the same, but here they have also added some new ones. The problem is that the weapons in Doom 3 does not feel powerful at all. I'm for the most thinking about the shotgun, which is super weak. Such a shame. Bosses are fun to fight and some of them needs to be taken out on a special way. The expansions continues the story and gives you some more hours of playthrough.
All in all Doom 3: BFG Edition is a great bundle of games. I recommend it to everyone who is a fan of the franchise. Can't wait for the reboot!!

KickBeat is a rhythm game that's almost good, but doesn't quite hit the mark.
For starters there are only 24 tracks, and they're pretty much all either what wikipedia defines as 'Industrial Rock'/'NuMetal' or the 6 electronica/dance tracks from Electronic Super Joy.  This ultimately leads to a pretty low amount of genres.  There is an option to make custom tracks out of your own songs, and while you can set the BPM, you cannot add true custom tracking as far as I can tell, leading to a sub-par experience there.
As many other reviews have noted, the notes don't really match up with the rhythm that much, so you will primarily be relying on the visuals to know when to press buttons.  This leads into another large flaw of the game - the visuals are incredibly noisy, often making it a strain to know when the 'enemies' are coming.
Another mechanical quirk of the game are the 'power up' orbs.  These primarily just give you bonus points or multipliers.  There's also a shockwave (clears nearby enemies) and a shield, but using those actually grants less points than not using them.  The quirk is that you have to doubletap the button in order to pickup the orb.  On the higher difficulties, missing an orb counts as getting hit.  This is problematic because it can quickly grow incredibly tiresome to doubletap orb wielding enemies in succession.
The game was initially designed for consoles - as such I used a controller for it, but that brought its own slew of problems.  On expert/master difficulty, there are often enemies coming from three directions.  As almost anyone who plays on a controller is aware of, pressing an opposing pair of buttons (example: A+Y or X+B) on a controller is incredibly awkward.  Combine this with needing to doubletap, and getting punished for hitting extra buttons, leads to a frustrating setup.  I imagine this is much easier with a keyboard, but it does raise the question of why the game was designed this way to begin with since it initially launched on console.
Finally, I just wanted to point out the silly unlock system the game uses.  You're stuck with playing as the male character until you complete the game's story as him - then you can use the female.  Despite being given seperate 'stories' they both play the exact same songs, and have the same gameplay.
Oh - right, this game actually has a story.  It's, as to be expected, absurdly terrible.  This isn't a problem in itself, except for the fact that there are a couple brief unskippable cutscene parts associated with the 'boss battles' which are painful to sit through.
Anyway, despite all my whining, I did finish the game - which is saying something in itself.  There is potential here, and if you picked this up in a bundle, it's worth giving a whirl.  Ultimately however, I cannot recommend actually buying this game by itself.

At first I was nervous to buy this game, with the negative coments and no personal references for opinions. But after owning this game for 4 days and putting in 48hrs worth of game time. I can say that it is well worth ignoring the ney sayers and spending the $15.
The main complaints I've heard coming into Starbound was that there was too much lagg and that it was hardly finished. While I have noticed a few times what you would call "lagg", it really only a second or less of slowing down (nothing that ever caused any problems). However, I would suppose that if you played on the "unstable" version of the game (When you purchase starbound it comes w/ stable & unstable versions) then you may experience more issues...but then again they warn about that in the Developers note "The [NIGHTLY] branch is updated automatically every night, and is for players who want to track progress or simply can't wait to check out shiny new features. :D Play at your own risk, though, as these builds are not tested and bugs/crashes are likely."
As for its content, within 48 hours I was craft the highest level armors, fully upgrade my ship, and fully upgrade my matter manipulator and all tech upgrades. Partially because I was lucky and found good planets with abundant resorces but, also because I powered through it as fast as I could and looked up guides. Even still, this game had more than enough content to be worth the price. And as for endgame content, there is still the option to build and grow colonies (that have even more side quests that pop up in them), exploration can still yeild great rewards such as rare weapons and gear, there are lore books to collect, challenge dungeons, and regular dungeons to fight through (or capture and turn into your own colonies).
Really this is almost enough for me to call it a finished game but I'd still love to see more and where they can go from here. But if $15 won't kill you and you enjoy building/exploration/RPG games, then I'd say that Starbound is definitely worth a shot.

Well, as you can tell, I enjoy playing Fallout 4. It's a really great and fun game to play! Yes there is no doubt that this game does have it's fair share of issues, but I'd like to borrow a movie term here, it's a beautiful mess!
Story: I'll be frank, the story is kinda weak. It's pretty similar to Fallout 3's storyline, though instead of a son/daughter seeking his/her father, it's a father/mother seeking his/her son. And the ending... well it's not like previous Fallout titles sadly.
Despite the main story being weak, the side stories for characters and companions are pretty good and interesting. And a lot of the lore you can learn about what happened after the bombs fell is interesting!
Graphics: The graphics are pretty good if you've got a rig to handle high settings. There are many mod's available that can help improve them too!
Crafting: Crafting is straight forward and simple, but also helps players adjust their weapons to their play styles! It only gives you a bit of experience, but if you've got a lot of extra resources, take the time to craft guns that adds to their value is a good way to make a lot of money. It's also a helpful way to get that extra dozen or so exp needed to level up fast.
Settlement Building: I'll be honest, you're either going to love it, or hate it. Early on, you're limited on what you can build due to lack of resources and that some very good settlement items are locked behind perks. But as you advanced, and unlock perks necessary, you can create some amazing settlements! And thanks to Bethesda releasing their Vault add-on, you can even build your own above ground vaults! It's really amazing what a lot of people have put their minds too, so check out settlement building videos on youtube to see some amazing and creative people!
Combat: Compared to Fallout 3 and New Vegas, combat has really gotten better! Gun play feels much better than in the previous games as well. And as mentioned above, thanks to crafting, you can craft guns to fit your specific play styles.
Voiced PC: I'm only bringing this up because I know a lot of people have an issue with this. And my response is, I frankly don't have an issue with a voiced PC in Fallout. I know a lot of people whine about how it ruins "their" game, and if that's really a game breaker for them, but that sounds like a personal problem. I don't think the VA work is bad, but I do wish that they'd have hired a few extra VA's to give us alternative voices to choose from.
Finally Creation Club: Another thing that I'm bringing up solely because so many people are whining about it so much! I actually like the idea of the Creation Club. Gives some modders the chance to actually make some side cash on their mods. But I do agree with those complaining that prices are ridiculous! I mean seriously, the armor mods (IE Enclave; Buttercup; Morgan's Space Suit) cost as much as a story DLC! Honestly, I think if they were rolling out with the Creation Club, they would've been better served coming out with a story mod that gave everyone several hours of game play either in or around Boston, or in a new location similar too Nuka World. But it's completely optional, so it's not going to affect your game if you choose to have nothing to do with Creation Club.
Well, I recommend this game, because it's fun, it's interesting, and you'll lose yourself in building your settlements!

The core gameplay is that of an "action platformer" (very little actual platforming, but it controls like one, including the dash-cancel and air combo), with a decent light/heavy attacks for combos, and enough variety in the attacks (once you unlock them for 50 each) to keep it interesting.
Add to this a narrator guiding you through the story.
Although the narration is in chinese with english subtitles, it really works because the lines are well delivered, instead of a bland monologue.
It also helps that the translation is of good quality, as far as I can tell (I am not proficient in chinese at all, but the english lines seem to work).
With just this though, the game doesn't take too long to beat, as long as you don't die too much to enemies and bosses, but with this price tag, it's already ok for me.
But that's not all the game has to offer (don't spoil yourself by looking at the achievements), because nearly every time the narrator tells you to do something, you can choose to not do it, or to do something else, and it will continue to be narrated, but by an increasingly♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥narrator (sometimes he makes fun of you instead).
The best part is that all of this "meta" is completely optionnal, some of it leading you to zones earlier, some of it being an "ending" of sort.
Not only are (most of) those parts funny it likes to talk about some informations that are more related to the development of this game (and games in general).
As you can probably tell by reading this, I really enjoy playing this game, and the "meta" is just right for me to add on top of an already nice game.

If you love horror, suspense, imagination, puzzles, a beautiful soundtrack, a challenge, and a depressing yet amazing plot, then this game is for you.

Cleared this game on the PS3, got it on Steam anyway because I hadn't gotten any of the DLC.
Gameplay-wise, Sleeping Dogs is for the most part far from original. The combat in particular is clearly heavily inspired by the Batman: Arkham Whatever series (heavy emphasis on countering enemies) with some influence from Ryuu ga Gotoku/Yakuza (environmental finishers). Aside from that it's the usual sparsely-populated sandbox dotted with uninspired mini-quests.
None of this matters, however, because the game is GOOD. The combat being similar to the Arkham series' means that it's good, and when it sparingly gives you firearms becomes even more ridiculously fun with the ability to activate bullet time. Car chases are the best I've ever experienced, what with the game giving you the option to jump out of your vehicle and hijack another in the middle of a chase, or open fire on a vehicle you just jumped out of in slow motion and instantly cause it to explode in an impressive conflagration. While the story is nothing new- I-won't-say-his-name who dies near the end is basically the EXACT SAME CHARACTER as the guy who died in Ryuu ga Gotoku 3, or the Japanese drama Double Face (which has the bonus of also being about an undercover cop infiltrating the mafia)- the setting certainly is something I'm pretty sure has never before been explored in a video game, and the experience of being able to explore a Hong Kong gangster action flick is a pretty refreshing one.
This game is certainly something special, and really worth checking out.

There is a health container which will raise your maximum HP by one. However, it's not carried to the next stage.
Because you'll mostly just dodge the enemies and kill the boss, you'll get bored of this game quicky.

Cons:

This is just a ton of fun, and I don't know how I had never heard of it.  KickBeat is a DDR-style rhythm game with a holistic sensibility about the beat, jumping among drums, guitar, and vocals as they become prominent in the song.  It doesn't feel like you're playing the drums with your keyboard; it feels like you're conducting the whole song.  The mapping of the built-in songs is precise and joyful.  The songs themselves are way more industrial-metal than I usually prefer, but in this game they work perfectly, and you'll agree with me even if it's not your genre.
Apart from gameplay, one thing that really stands out is the unexpectedly hilarious writing of the cutscenes.  Honest belly laughs.  It's baffling how writers with such good instincts could name their game KickBeat, possibly the most forgettable name for a video game I can think of, right up there with the equally underappreciated Defender's Quest.
The upper difficulty levels sometimes require three simultaneous button presses, and some keyboards -- including both of mine -- have an issue with "ghosting" that prevents them from registering all three.  This is not a game bug, it's a hardware bug, but it's still something to be aware of before you buy.  The lower difficulty levels are still plenty satisfying and offer lots of replayability.
Full-throated recommendation.  This game deserved press and didn't get it.

This isn't really a review, more of a counter-argument against the negative reviews in regards to the timing of the game.
I must say, at first this game is a little confusing, since most rhythm games of this style normally have you pushing buttons in time with a particular aspect of the song, ie Drums, guitar, where-as this one has you pressing the buttons in time for all parts of the song, one minute you are tapping along with the drums, the next you are following the vocals, and I think this is what is throwing a lot of people off when they are trying to play, saying that it is out of time and what-not.
I can assure anyone that is put off by the negative reviews, that it isn't off at all, and by my third song, I had the hang of it, 5-Star-ing pretty much every song. Yes, it can feel unfair at times, switching what part of the song you are playing along to, but as you learn the songs, you get used to it and know what is coming. I found I did better on songs that I knew.
Oh and also, I wouldn't bother trying to play with your own songs, it just doesn't work, not for me at least.

This game is a lesson in bad management and bad design practice.
You simply do not promise features in a game if you cannot deliver them.  You can publish a list of features that you desire to add if possible, but you only promise the core elements.  And then once in production, you do not just abandon the project to start a new game, especially a sequel.  It is an unwritten contract between the dev and the buyer that you will deliver a working game with as few bug as possible.
As this game exists, the dev simply wasted to many development hours on a single feature.  The ship designing options in this game are hands down one of the best that I have seen.  You have so much control within the constraints put in place.  However, the whole purpose of a ship design is to utilize it in its function, typically combat.  And while combat is decent and some what fun, you need an economy to support it, and Stardrive simply does not have a well working economic model.
In fact, the game ends up punishing you for the 1st 30 min to hour of play.  1st by making you feel like you need to grind a bunch of base technologies just to be capable of performing the basic functions of a 4x game.  You will need new planets to expand you economic abilities, but you will feel you need 4 technologies before you can successfully colonize a planet: a food tech, a production tech, an income tech, and the ability to expand on to prohibited terrain.  However, if you focus on these techs to quickly start expanding, the AI comes and smacks you around because your military is weak.  So lets say you focus on military techs (like guided missiles and armor; yah, no armor before this tech), your units are capable of carrying a basic fight, but the AI has now colonized any half-decent planet on the map.  But then you say to yourself, I've got a big military I will just invade a weaker AI.  Welp, hope your like rebels suddenly poping up on your worlds with no prior indication of unrest because your income rate cannot support even a half decent fleet unless you colonize new worlds.  But wait you say, I'll just build a smaller but higher tech fleet; nope.  Not enough fire power to successfully invade a AI held world because unsuprisingly the AI has a fleet just as big if just a bit smaller but like 3x the troops you were able to build.  And all of this early game will determine whether you will win or loose late game.
However, this is not to say you cannot do well.  If you get lucky, the random map has placed habitable planets as neighboring systems, given you one of the less aggressive races as a neighbor, and not block those systems with hostile drones.  If you can survive this early game, the game can be a good bit of fun.  At least up until some late game bug or unfixed feature ends your fun.
A game should not punish players for trying to perform the tasks the game demands or make them slog through a list of Techs that can make or brake their game just to successfully perform those tasks.

Fallout 4 is an excellent game.
But that doesn't mean it isn't without its faults.
Mechanically, it works great. The gunplay is excellent, the visuals are great, the sound and visual effects are better than ever. But it fails to do well what the previous games did great.
New vegas and Fallout 3 were in a class of their own with character interaction, class progression, interesting quests, and a world that was artfully portrayed.
This one felt devoid of any real and meaning interaction, a few speech checks were all you need in most situations or a quick few shots to the head.
Previously you could bribe, blackmail, pursuade, murder, or try hilariously to manipulate people. And helping people felt meaningful and genuinely game changing at times. In this one, it felt like a chore.
As for the settlement system, it was an intereting integration, but felt way too overplayed, leaving the player to create the important and interesting locations in the wasteland, rather than already having them to explore and interact with. It just feels lazy.
The DLC is sound, other than additions to the settlement system, which felt forced. Far harbour and Nuka world are excellent additions to the adventure.
The modding community is always adding amazing stuff to the game, sometimes stuff that felt like it should've been there anyways.

Bastion is really really pretty to look at, but it's not fun to play -- not with a mouse and keyboard at any rate.  It's isometric and everything is on the diagonal, to top it off it's all done on floating platforms.  Going everywhere diagonally using WSAD is a total pain, especially since one wrong step and you fall off the edge into the ether.
The mobs tend to be overpowered, fighting is repetitive.  You end up with an impressive array of varied weapons to choose from, and they are all upgradable, but you can only chose two before you enter a (floating) dungeon with no idea what you will be fighting.  You can also buy permanent buffs, but you can only have a few active at any time.
You have an inventory, but it is minimal and based purely on furthering the game.  There is a story, but in the time I played it never grabbed me.  I was too concerned with getting from point A to point B without falling (while wondering what was off the screen shooting at me) to ever really *care* what the protagonists problem was or what NPC's wanted me to do for them and why.  For me, it ended up all about getting to the end of the dungeon with little joy getting there.  I did not finish the game.
Pros:
Truly gorgeous to look at
Varied upgradable weapons
A choice of upgradable buffs
The narrator
Cons:
Being forced to walk diagonally on floating platforms, or fall off
Choosing weapons blindly
Mobs and gauntlet running (on the diagonal)
This game is playable on a PC, but definitely wasn't made for PC

Before I start: I didn't play the Resurrection of Evil Addon (yet) so I will only review the main game and lost Mission.
Sooo, what are the pros and cons to Doom 3: BFG Edition?
+ Good Weapon System: Like in the classic Doom games you're able to carry all weapons you find during the campaign with you. There are a lot of different ones, from pretty standard assault rifle and shotgun to more futuristic weapons like the palsma rifle and the BFG itself. Each weapon fills its specific role. Also the game doesn't have iron sights, you can (have to) fire every weapon from the hip.
+ Good Enemy Diversity: From your standard rifle dude to plasma ball hurling, giant hell knights and skeletons with rocket launchers mounted on their shoulders this game has it all. A lot of the attacks in the game can be dodged (plasma balls, rockets, enemies jumping at you...) which adds an element of skill to the combat.
+ Health and Armor System: The game has the classic HP + Armor system where the armor absorbs part of the damage you take. Health doesnt regenerate and can only be refilled through Medikits, Health stations
The only problem i found with the system is that armor doesn't drain that much which means you'll be always topped out on armor.
+ Lost Mission DLC: It's definitly better than the main missions. More open, brighter areas and less spooky moments (aka monsters spawning behind you or jumpscares outta nowhere) make this DLC fun to play.
+ You get Doom and Doom 2 so you have actually good games to play. (Note: the .wads can be used for sourceports, tested with Zandronum)
So why the negative rating?
- Too much focus on spooking the player: Doom 3 ditches the fast Run'n'Gun of the original games for a slower, darker gameplay. The fights/skirmishes with monsters are somewhat fast, but moving from fight to fight is slow. A lot of dark areas, the constant fear of getting jumped by a random imp hiding in a closet behind you...
- The game requires a lot of backtracking: You fight your way to a console to activate just to go back the same way over and over again. The backtracking wouldn't be so annoying if the levels were a bit more open but going down the same corridor several times is boring as hell.
- The enemy AI is stupid: Even though the game theoratically has enemy diversity, these enemies just don't do much. I had Hell Knights walking away from me after throwing one plasma ball, revenants doing nothing when I was in melee range or mancubi not following me after i moved out of their line of sight. Basically the game has two types of enemy AI: zombie soldiers rapid firing at you and demons throwing a fireball now and then.
- Too much ammo pickups: I don't how it is in the original Doom 3 (I read ammo wasn't that plentyful there) but in the BFG edition it's pretty hard to run out of ammo. This isn't something you'd expect from a horror focused game (which Doom 3 wants to be) as managing ammo is a major gameplay element in most of these games. Even for a Run'n'Gun shooter sitting on loads of unused ammo isn't that good.
- No secrets or powerups in the levels: This may be more or less important for some of the players but I'll mention it. The original Dooms had a lot of secrets cleverly hidden in the levels. Finding these awarded the player with strong weapons and powerups most of the time. Doom 3 has no real secrets, most of them are just a bit off the main route, up a ladder or they lay just in plain sight behind some bars / behind a fence just to picked up later on the way. Ammo for stronger weapons like the rocket launcher or the BFG isn't really hidden, most of the time laying in plain sight.
The other issue I had that there aren't any real powerups during single player (I know they somehow return during RoE with the artifact), the only thing returning is the berserk pack. 2 times. One time to fight some zombies and the other time during the hell level but that's it.
For whom would I recommend Doom 3: BFG Edition? Horror shooter fans.
For whom wouldn't I recommend this game? Doom fans, because this package has nothing to offer except maybe the .wad of the No Rest For The Living Episode of Doom II.
Side note: A problem that has been mentioned in a lot of reviews, but I'll include it in here too: Apparently taking screenshots via Steam (by pressing F12) is registered as cheating, locking you out of achievements (if you're into that).

A well done action FPS game that seemed to slip through without being noticed by most people. Play as all 3 species, each with thier own story and goals.
The gameplay feels fluent and smooth. FPS drops were very few and far between on my medium end PC on high settings. You spend most of your time traversing through mostly linear levels completing objects along the way. In some areas objectives make you kill waves of enemies or solve puzzling problems such as figuring out how to enter a room, which helps keep that game a little more interesting rather than traveling through from place to place shooting everything in site.
Where controls are concerned, each species plays differently with thier own style of movement and controls and some are better than others. Playing as the marines feels like your typical FPS game, basically shoot your way through the level with a variety of guns. You feel more vulnerable as a marine as well as Aliens are very quick and come in hordes, and predators are much more powerful.
Playing as the Alien and Predator is where this game stands out from other FPS games. The predator has a variety of gadgets such as the laser cannon to fight from a distance as well as a spear and claws to tear your enemies to shreds up close. You are able to jump high and far using an ability, this allows the predators to have alot of verticality to combat. You can also go invisible to catch your enemies by surprise, however get to close and the humans with see through you camo. The Aliens are very quick and agile, while playing the Alien you are able to crawl up walls and leave very far. These contols are hard to get the hang of at first but once you get the hang of them you feel pretty deadly. You are quieter but all these perks come with a price, and that is your health. As the alien you will need to learn to be stealthy on your approach to clear rooms as well as know when to run and hide. Both of these species have special instant kill stealth moves and grab kills, however for as cool as they look, they also leave you very vulnerable to attack, their is also no way of cancelling this action and they take a few seconds to finish. If you are attacked during thease few seconds you will most likely die or barely get away.
On high the graphics looked really good, they felt like real areas and fit the setting of the Alien/Predator universe. The levels are pretty well designed, and their is a variety of settings to traverse through as you go through the story such as the forest, ruins, structures and a few others. The gun fire flash looks good in dark rooms and the lighting is done very well adding to the spooky theme of some areas. The design and animation of the Aliens and Predators look well designed and look like their movie counterparts. The animation looks good, especially the Alien looks like it had a lot of work done to it to make it look and move realistically as it crawls over the walls. The animations during the stealth/grab kills are very well done and look badass and gory the way they should be in this style of game.
The audio is decent, although some of the guns sounded terrible and wimpy. The sound design during the levels does a pretty good job of making you feel on edge and adds a little bit to the suspense. The aliens sounded like the aliens from the movies however nothing special, same with the predator, you hear his significant and unique sounds but its nothing really special or new. The marines are terribly voice acted and their likes sounds cheasy.
For the most part the audio is decent and will add to the feel of the setting but nothing special.
The story are different and each species has their own goal in mind however their is crossover between each story. As a marine you are trying to fight back the Aliens and find out what happened after a problem occurs in a research facility your goal is to find out what happened, where they are coming from, and how to stop it, but end up crossing paths with the predator down the line changing some of your objectives.
The Alien story line has you playing an Alien captured by humans and tested on. When the queen calls you seek to find her, only to be restrained by the humans, however after an issue arises during an experiment you are able to break the shackles that bind you down, allowing you to fight back, escape, and find your queen to learn why she is calling you.
The Predator story arc has you playing as a predator needing to prove himself to the elders to earn his right to be a hunter. This has you traveling through multipul areas killing Aliens in trials from the elders, through your trials you will cross paths with the marines leading for some objectives to become skewed as you destroy the resistance.
Aliens vs. Predator is a decent FPS action game that goes off the path from your basic FPS game. Being able to play as all 3 species with thier own unique abilities, movements and story arcs is fun and helps the game feel fresh. The story is decent, with some being better than others. They did a good job of balancing the characters out with thier own advantages and weaknesses making each species feel like it should. The world looks good and well designed. The controls feel good and tight, the only one that took a while to get used to was the aliens movements because of its quick pace and ability to climb on walls and other surfaces.
This is a good game that would be good to get on sale. Fans of first person shooters may enjoy the originality of playing as all 3 characters in this game, however if you are looking for a horror game, this may not be it. While it seems to try to be one, it doesnt seem to commit to the idea as the game progresses, at most this game may hit the creepy feeling at some points but thats about it.
I can not comment on the multiplayer as I never tried it myself, but for the most part from what I've heard is that its fun but almost always dead. So maybe with a few friends it could be fun for a get together.

I'm not very good at fighting games, but I usually enjoy playing them, and SFV is no exception. In fact, I'd say it's probably my favourite fighting game of all time.
So what's so good about the game? Well, for starters, the game mechanics are really fun (which is the most important bit, IMO), and it's pretty easy to learn the basics of each character thanks to the demonstrations mode. The singleplayer content is also more extensive than I'd anticipated: the story mode especially is better fleshed out than I would've expected from a Street Fighter game. Online works well too, and I haven't experienced too much lag online in spite of what some other people seem to be reporting here on Steam.
Of course Street Fighter V is not a perfect game. It lacks an arcade mode, the button prompts are all Xbox controller icons even if you're using a keyboard, and you are not allowed to rebind keyboard controls without third party programs. The game can also randomly crash if you have Wacom tablet drivers installed on your PC.
A lot of the game's content has been locked behind DLC, including new characters, stages and alternate character costumes and colours. Most of these things can be purchased with in-game currency called Fight Money, so you don't necessarily need to pay to get any of the characters. At some point you will likely need to either grind for Fight Money or buy them with real money, but I personally find that a fair price to pay since Capcom has promised there will not be a "Super Street Fighter V" or other game upgrades like that. Just wait for a likely sale during EVO or something if you want to avoid grinding, so you can get away with paying less.

I don't usually play driving games, but when I do, I tend to favour arcade racers. Back in the day, I played the heck out of 'Lotus: The Ultimate Challenge' and enjoyed 'Need for Speed II'. I even found 'Test Drive III: The Passion' quite fun because of the driving freedom that it gave me. 'Burnout Paradise' combined everything I love about these games, with the added bonus of some vehicular mayhem.

'Burnout Paradise' is set in Paradise City. This fictional city is a fully realized one, designed specifically for racing, stunt driving, vehicular mayhem, exploration, as well as pushing and experimenting what your vehicles can do. New cars are unlocked upon completing challenges, which are plenty and spread throughout Paradise City. Collecting vehicles can be addictive, but useful and almost necessary as they give you advantages that can make completing the increasingly difficult challenges easier.

Finding shortcuts, making insane jumps, smashing gates, destroying billboards, and driving recklessly aren't just fun distractions in the game, but they also increase your car's boost, which come in handy during challenges. The game doesn't give you any hints or explicit visual cues as to where to go and what to do, so familiarizing yourself with the city is crucial. This lack of handholding makes discovering bonuses more gratifying.

Unfortunately, despite being called "The Ultimate Box", this version of 'Burnout Paradise' does not include prominent DLCs like access to Big Surf Island and Legendary Cars. This is really unfortunate as I thought I would have these DLCs available to me. I was also hoping for the option to create my own custom music playlist, but there isn't. Still, 'Burnout Paradise' ends up being more fun than I initially expected, and still earns an enthusiastic recommendation from me.

I like how there are events in every intersection and you can jump from one event to the next very quickly without entering a menu.The other events (race, marked man, road rage) are good, but not quite as fun as the older burnout games. The audio/visual presentation seems like a step down from the other games however. Even though the graphics are technically very good, the color palette is washed out with lots of grays and browns, which is surprising to me because the older games had a more fun and colorful style. Also the soundtrack is definitely worse than the old games and the announcer DJ atomica is very annoying. The game also feels pretty easy.
If you have never experienced a burnout game, Paradise is a great place to start and if you're a fan of open world racers you definitely owe it to yourself to give it a try. Its a shame EA had to kill the Burnout series and switch their focus to the slowly dying need for speed franchise.

I know it's tiresome to hear complaints about the lack of quality control on Steam, especially since we're clearly at a point where there's no turning back, but I'll say I do miss the days when a game had to be an actual game in order for it to get on here. Endorlight is nothing more than an asset flip, a few cosmetic changes tacked onto a base engine that is itself a ripoff of Spelunky. This is a bald-faced attempt to make a few bucks while putting forth the absolute bare minimal effort. As such, Endorlight lacks any semblance of substance. It's just a bland, repetitive trip from the top of the screen to the bottom, collecting gems that do nothing and killing enemies with three weapons that are effective from varying distances but have no damage scaling to make any one of them more useful than the one with the most range. Occasionally, a bomb will blow out a portion of a wall and you'll find yourself unable to climb out of an area, forcing a restart. Even if the developer's bad practices don't bother you, the fact that it's a bad game should. Don't purchase Endorlight at any price.

Let's be totally up front here; Zombie Pirates both looks and feels like a game designed by someone who has never made a video game before.
When it opens, it presents a quaint little opening where pirates destroy a person's ship and steals the owner's woman. Then, he rises from the dead because his love is too strong. Nothing special, but I understand - sometimes, you don't want to be too heavy with story. You just want a dumb little love story, and I can side with that. Our character has come back from the DEAD to save his love, because it's silly and this is a game about pirates and *zombies*. And then when you load the first level... you're playing as the pirates.
Wait, we're against the zombies? We're the pirates? We stole that guy's love, killed him, destroyed his ship, and now we're Chuck McPirateFace, ruler of the Seven Seas, killing off hordes of zombie pirate ships? ...Okay... I guess? The game only told us that the one zombie guy came back. Where did all these zombie ships come from?
And the gameplay. My god, the gameplay. There's an implied grid, and you sail your ship around it. When you get close to enemy ships, you fire at them. If they get close enough, they fire at you. You can't dodge the shots the enemy shoot at you, so your only option is to stay in a sweet spot range. Each enemy drops an item which can be helpful, but ultimately it's extremely difficult to downright impossible to utilize and use an item (in which at least one of them involves getting another ship to control, giving you a strategic advantage) and also keeping yourself in the sweet spot you need to be.
And then, the game rates you on the *number of ships you've lost*. Are you trying to make a strategy game? If this were turn-based, I could understand punishing me for losing ships. But it's real time. You can't punish someone for losing ships in real time, especially if you're already expecting me to control my main ship in real time as well.
Sew it all up with having to hear your main ship spit out dumb phrases ("These dead men are telling tales!"? Really?) over and over every time you move your character, and it becomes so sickeningly cheezy, and you're left with a sickly, amateur game that couldn't even keep me occupied for a friggin hour for me to review it in a serious manner. I'm disgraced to have this game in my library, and it is barely worth fifteen cents, let alone the fifteen dollar asking price.
I find it funny that up above, in the game description, it seems to end with 'Zombie Pirates will send a shiver right'. The cut-off sentence just sounds like a question, and a good one. Will it send a shiver? Sure, but not from horror. Pastels do not lend themselves to horror. I shivered from the very idea that someone, somewhere spent the kind of money that could feed someone for a few days, or buy something objectively more interesting on this pile.
tl;dr Avoid this game. It is not worth either your money or your time. If real-time strategy or tower defence is what you're after, there are better, cheaper games (read: Plants vs. Zombies, Sanctum).

Superb little game and my absolute favourite at the moment!
There are so many planets to explore, so many items to craft, so many creatures to kill or capture!
When you've found the place where you want to live, you can build nearly everything you can imagine. Castles? Laboratories? Beach houses? Islands? Underwater Cities? Farms? 80's Clubs? Bunkers? Military bases? Pyramids? Tree houses? Asteroid bases? Japanese temples? No problem. The possibilities are virtually endless. You really can farm the garden of your mind.
And if you feel lonely inside your cities, castles, bases, etc., just buy some colony deeds and populate your constructions with some happy little NPCs.
The story is overhauled, it's interesting to follow the progress of the Protectorate and what you can do to save the galaxy. I played the main story for about 35 hours and had fun completing the different missions, exploring everything and defeating big bosses.
If you love the pixel style and spending hour after hour in crafting, exploring, mining, farming, cooking, relaxing (the soundtrack is extremely calm and peaceful), constructing and building your 2D-dreams, this is the perfect game for you!
It strives to be the next Stanley Parable, and at the end of the day, it might have even exceeded that goal. Well worth it.

Asylums and insanity tend to be a crutch in horror games, but Fran Bow manages to avoid the usual tropes of haunted hospitals and delusional psychos. It actually avoids a lot of storytelling tropes, forging off in an uncharted and often bizarre path towards its final revelations. You can be sure it's a beautiful and entertaining ride, but not one without a few bumps.
Fran Bow is the name of the spindly, doe-eyed ten-year-old you guide through this grotesque adventure. Her happy homelife was interrupted by her parents getting filleted and her cat vanishing, so the game opens in an asylum for children. What starts as a quest to break out and reunite with your lost kitty spirals into an insane journey across... I'm not even sure what nouns to use here, honestly. The story is going to go places you're not going to expect in the least, and the surprises never really stop coming.
The actual gameplay is plenty familiar for adventure fans, with clicks to move and a plentiful inventory to Use, Combine, and Examine. For most of the game you'll have an additional gimmick in the form of pills that warp reality (or how you see it, anyway) around you, essentially giving you two scenes to explore for every one you find. Chapter three of this five-chapter adventure also has an additional gimmick that's used to great effect in some rather clever puzzles. You'll come across NPCs to chat with as well but don't expect dialog trees or complex interactions, as your part in the conversation is usually a binary choice between "continue talking" and "bye".
As for the puzzles themselves, they're pretty logical despite the insanity blossoming around them. Items tend to have clear uses, explanations abound, and there's something of a hint system present for most of the game. There's even a few with multiple solutions that can earn you achievements for working out the less common way. As long as you have a modicum of patience you won't be needing a walkthrough. Scene transitions are often instant and can be double-clicked through if not so the quality-of-life elements are there to stave off frustration.
The only thing that might put you off a bit is the story, and in an adventure game that's admittedly huge. I mentioned before that the plot goes off in some bizarre directions, and if anything I'm understating the point. Fran Bow is ostensibly a horror game, and while there's plenty of gruesome scenery and creepy beings, the entire third chapter is something I never expected to see in a horror title. The chapters themselves are a bit disjointed in terms of tone, pace, and mechanics as well, so much so that the game might feel episodic at times. It all comes together in the end but does so in a very jarring, sudden way that still doesn't answer all the questions it raises.
Flawed though it is, the story is still an entertaining one and is carried on the backs of its charming cast. Fran is incredibly upbeat and pleasantly irreverent for being a disturbed orphan, and the people and creatures she meets often echo her childish exuberance. There's an excellent balance here against some darker and more serious characters, and Fran herself has a morbid streak that's used to great effect. It's a good pairing with the gorgeous hand-drawn graphics, giving the game a look somewhere between Tim Burton aesthetics and stop-motion animation. I wish I could say the same about the sound design but it's honestly pretty lacking, with little more than a competent soundtrack and some simple effects that don't always fill out the scene.
The adventure genre is a bit heavy on the horror side but Fran Bow does plenty to stand out. The look, the feel, and the story are all unique draws and come together to form an impressive experience. It might not always make sense, but you'll have so much fun chuckling at Fran's black humor and marveling at the beings she meets that I doubt it'll hold you back much. There's a full six hours or more of exploring to do in this dark and beautiful world, and plenty of reasons to dive right in.

Amazing game. Good lenght and dificulty level. Great gameplay and puzzles, equally great story telling and complex, characters we care about. Just what I want from a point and click game. Not too easy that you go through it in an hour, but hard enough that you're sometimes stuck and consider a cheeky peak at a walkthrough. Loved the subtle references to other games or fictional worlds in it as well.
Given the story and themes (childhood, psychiatry, alternate universes and the power of the mind...) the game could have been a meaningless sum of overused situations and objects, but Fran Bow totally delivers. All the expected elements are here (psychotropic drugs, a dodgy Freudian doctor, an a creepy insane asylum to name a few) but the way we interract with them as a gamer is smart and subversive. For instance, using the meds to jump to a different universe was actually awesome. It made the gameplay richer and more interractive without taking away from the traditional point and click experience. It also rendered the storytelling interesting: are the pills good or bad? Is Fran really mentally ill or is she just midunderstood and magical, or both? Is any of it really happening?
The Universe is rich and wonderful. The artwork is both enchanting and delightfully creepy. Amazing details in the diferent layouts. I loved all the characters. And how ambiguous someof them are.
I am just thrilled that a game exploring the themes of insanity and mental disorders managed to avoid clichés, or overused gory horror. Fran Bow is just the ticket, it doesn't just use madness and insanity as a catalyst for some stereotypical story, it goes right to the heart of the subject and asks serious question without making us feel the people behind the game are trying to push an agenda onto us. It's game which comes from the heart.
Only negative points is that the dialogues are sometimes a bit lenghty, but that's because they help explain the background story. I appreciated getting a peak into the complex universe and story behind Fran Bow, but it slowed the pace a bit. Also if you buy the game after having bought the demo you have to start again from the beginning.
This game really stands out. If you're going to try a point and click game which mixes innocent childhood and creepy madness, make it Fran Bow.

I found Stardrive ages ago and saw a lot of good things about it.  It was in alpha/beta though and Steam was nice enough to point me at the products webpage, because as handy as steam is they cant list all of a products features on their little webpage (I dont think it had the read more tabs at the time).  Looking at the developers product page and seeing youtube videos of what you are going to purchase is just good consumer behavior so that you know what you are purchasing.   It looked really interesting and offered things such as
Moo2 like but RTS 4x
Multiplayer
Create your own fleet designs
Special Missions in which you assume control of an individual ship instead of a whole side
A sandbox mode with an engaging storyline.
Neutral factions like remeneant and pirates
A variety of random Galaxy events.
Shortly after buying in the developer said he was temporarly removing multiplayer to work out the kinks. Of course the sandbox storymode wasnt finished yet but thats ok it was in beta and we saw how it was going to work with researching technologys and contacting a neutral planet and yadda yadda.  And watching the WTF is, along with other videos I knew what to expect with late game latency, so when people bashed on it I spoke up for it, telling people to give it time.  As a one person developer a 1-2 year wait for him to fix things up was acceptable.  Especialy for a game that had already been in development for something like 4 years.  But it was nearly done,  so we should hold on before making judgements.  I made guides, tried to help people out,and gave suggestions.
But the longer it went on the more sour it got.  A couple weeks out of its -short- Beta when we could no longer get refunds there was a 50% off sale.  A couple months after that we were told Multiplayer would never make it to the game and that maybe in a stardrive 2 we would get it.   Special missions were abandoned all together.  The Galaxy events were restricted to simple planatary shifts for fertility/richness.  The Remenent story-arc was removed (and then later reintroduced in a shoddy manner).  Some of the AI's were just left in a crippeled state.   And then afterall of that there was a Fertility/abundance nerf across all difficultes (that the AI ignores) that you cant disable... Why nerf fertility/abund in a single player game?  A -lot- of players got banned from the message boards for silly things and it was a pretty rage induceing time all around.
But thats ok I thought,  I decided to give him more time.  He said development would 'slow' while stardrive 2 was in development but we could expect improvements.  I decided to wait for SD2 to get finished before looking back and seeing what has changed.
So this last week I gave it a try again.  And I have to say i am not very happy with it.  I enjoyed the game more during beta and after 'release' with the late game slowdown then I do now.  Sure some small bugs were fixed with fire arcs and its a little bit smoother.  But several AI's just sit there and let other AI's conquer them with out putting up a fight, several races just refuse diplomacy of any sort (usualy the ones that are conquering other ai's),  and the AI still cheats up the wazzoo building fleets it cant possibly support.  And overall it feels really bad fighting over a 4 population planet with a 1.2 fertility and 1.1 richness because thats the best there is out there.
In the end the game currently (may 2015) feels unfinished (even more so then during beta), and in need of a good AI patch, a balance patch, a few new galaxy option sliders to combat what was done post release, and maybe a gamemode paid DLC.
I'm gratefull for the 33% discount on SD2 for SD1 owners,  its a nice gesture.  And I really do hope SD2 turns out well, and can compete with other games in the turn based strat genre. But in the end this game also made me deicde to hold off on SD2 until its cheep as dirt.. because no matter how good it looks 'now'  it could be a lot worse in 6 months.   And thats just not something I ever really expected to say about a game.
