It's not that I disagree with all of your assessments, but pretty much all ARPG's have problems with items #1-3 throughout in some form or another.
I usually play a melee character, and other games usually treat melee badly (vanilla Diablo 3 comes to mind, at least compared to my experience with Barbarian vs Witch Doctor).  I was pleased to have a pleasant experience in Van Helsing 2 using a melee character.  I can't speak to mage balance because I balanced my DPS with plenty of defense/resist as a melee theme (no mana shield though).  I would sometimes get gibbed pretty quick, but I would usually see that there was dangerous stuff I didn't move out of (kinda my bad).  Plus, this game has a perk that lets you get a "free life" every 3 minutes where you turn into a ghost on the spot so that little mess-ups aren't such a big deal.  There's a trick that lets you vanish from all aggro as well.
To touch on difficulty:  I played the game on Hard, but you can change it on the fly (which is nice) and you can get these unique trophies that modify the difficulty of the game in very specific tradeoff style ways (if you so choose).  My favorite was a trophy that gave +100 magic find, but mobs have 20% more HP.
Van Helsing's storyline #3 is waaay better than almost all other ARPG in my opinion.  The quests, dialogue/voice acting, and story progression are probably only matched by Diablo 3 in quality.  Torchlight, Path of Exile, and other ARPGs barely have a useful story aside from framing mob slaughter.  It's not as good as every other game I've played, but it's top notch for ARPGs.  I see this as a highly subjective evaluation though, so I'm not as adamant about this as the other items.
Endgame for #4 I can't speak to, because I usually just play through games once usually.  I haven't tried multiplayer #5, but I can see that would be a frustrating experience.
In my experience with the hunter on hard for one play-through (no multiplayer), I would definitely recommend it.  I see that you had problems with the mage and maybe the gibbing gave a bad taste in your mouth playing at heroic difficulty.  When comparing it to other ARPGs, it's hard for me to see how a fan of the genre wouldn't enjoy experiencing Van Helsing and thus recommend others to "give it a go."   I really thought the unique elements of this game were refreshing and want to see a third one.
I don't use WASD
the time to move and attack, but it helps tremendously when kiting and in place of a "move here" hotkey.  By the way, they need to add a "move here" key, I was looking for it when I saw I could configure WASD (they currently have it defaulted as the up, down, left, and right keys.  You can also do another advanced move where you can use your mouse for things on menus (character/inventory, etc) while at the same time moving around precisely (where normally if you want to move, you HAVE to have clicked with your mouse on something).  Although I wish there was an option to make make the base keys move diagonally.  W should move the character up and to the right, the S key should make the character down and to the left, etc.  This is because most paths in top down isometric ARPGs like this usually have main paths pointing diagonally.  This default diagonal movement keeps the player from more often having to hold down more than one WASD key.
In the "Ink Hunt" DLC I just saw two goblins in a Titanic-esque pose fall off the front of a boat in the air, embracing each other throughout their death fall.  Sadly, I was so stunned I didn't take a screenshot   :(
When comparing gear, by using a special option in the menu, you can see two different gear comparisons.  One comparison of base stat changes, and one comparison with all enchantments together.  This way, you don't always think, "Wow I rarely get a decent upgrade!"  When, in fact, you've been comparing the gear using the enchantment and infused essences together in most games.
The bosses usually have some kind of special addition that I haven't seen.  Like in the Ink Hunt DLC, this boss shoots a fire beam out in an arc as one move, slams down from above with another move, and draws you in with a third move.  This is just one example, but at least the bosses aren't, "They just take longer to kill" (although they do take longer to kill).  Luckily there is also an aura that dramatically increases your proficiency (by 25%) when taking on elite mobs.
For instance, there are some mobs that have wind up attacks in front of them that can easily be avoided using direction WASD.  Other mobs will have a front facing shield (some of the mobs literally have a tower shield with a peeking window) that you must get behind to score more damage.  Other mobs will visually look heavily armored in the front, and you must move behind them and they turn slowly.  And I know what you're thinking, "That'd be annoying to tell if the mob just has a buncha armor up front, that's a subtle tell..."  and you're right!  That's why they also add the front-damaging-reducing quality to the mobs description bar as well so that there's no confusion.  I like how the game rewards me for paying attention to positioning and taking full advantage of WASD + point-n-click synergy.

[18/05/2017 Update] Keeping the review negative because the developers have not changed what I was criticizing in the review. However, I do recommend the game and the developers have made some good efforts since this review. First, the developers have decided to give extra silver/merit-points for owners/buyers of the steam version of the game. Second, they have introduced a new reward mechanic inside the game which rewards you with a random item every week (if you connect once a day, so 7 times all in all). This reward can be a pet, a taunt, a death animation, a house, a character, a scroll... anything, I guess. It doesn't seem rigged as I have received pretty cool rewards so far. And 3rd, the developers have announced a big and promising add-on to the game (called Town of Salem : The Coven) which will be released in early June. The buyers of the steam version of this add-on will have 50% off its cost (5 $/€ instead of 10, so 5 $/€ discount, basically almost the price of the steam version of ToS).
The new currency system is a bad idea and I can't recommend the game to a newcomer for this reason. Sure, ToS is a fun little game at its core but now you can't buy all the available cosmetic content in the shop with ingame money. Bad practice from the publisher.
What happened : before the update the only currency system was town points (yellow coins), that you earned by playing games. After the last update (21/11/2016), the town points have become the "premium" currency and they added another currency in the form of silver coins.
After this update, you earn silver coins by playing and the only way to earn town points is through the shop in exchange of real money.
Problem is, after the update, in the shop, some cosmetics can be bought only with town points. You could get these cosmetics simply by playing, now you can't anymore.
A shame, really.

I would recommend this game to anyone that doesn't mind the old style anime appeal and a text based adventure that you play a part in. My ony major complaint is that at the end of teh game, the Daughter says how she felt in Japanese with no translation! I even used a translation app to try and get the gist of what she was talking about, but it couldn't hear her clear enough. Also, I'm not sure if this is a glitch or whatever, but my Daughter, kept failing doing the Inn job, even though I spammed it until I reached max cooking. As everyone mentions, the translation can be bad, but I haven't found it to be distracting at all. But in spite of the downsides, I really loved this game! The girl, seeing her age from 10 to 18 really pulls at your heartstrings and makes you feel like you bonded and raised this (hopefully) great girl thats now a woman. I felt proud knowing that my little girl turned into a noble soldier.
So in short:
Pros
Fantastic music
Engaging classic RPG fighting/adventure
Many Endings
Diverse ways to play
Truly endearing
Pacing feels great (8 years to see things unfold)
Cons:
Certain Stats feel a less useful (ie temperment)
Translation (Average player shouldn't be too annoyed)
Daughter's Life Summary words not subtitled (God this is the worst! Please fix)
Wishes:
More clothing would have been awsome. /thnking about all the playthroughs I could do, seeing the few thats present is kind of dissappointing. The could even have the same stats as clothing already present.Think of them as "alternative" outfits.
An "Ending Vault" so that I can view the Daughter's Life Summary after I unlock it. This would be cool, as the player would feel like even like their Daughter is gone but not forgotten.
The other Princess Makers! I saw that Princess Maker 5 was created in Japan. I'm thankful for this one we have, but I would expect Princess Maker 5 to be even more incredible. I would even be happy if we got 3 and 4 first within quick succession.
I hope my horrible review helps someone decide if this game is worth their time. If you enjoy life simulation, I think this "schedule" style simulation is a good approach. I orignally had this game on the PS3, but I have since sold the console and have purchased it for PC.
Burnout Paradise is one of the few racing games that I have seen that offers so much freedom. The game takes place in a giant open world map populated with objective challenges like races, stunt competitions, and road rage (take out other cars) competitions. Additionally, the world incentivises you to explore by making you search for hidden areas, big jumps, and billboards to smash through. There are many billboards that seem impossible to access, but after looking around, you'll finally find the hidden jump needed to access it.
The game features very satisfying driving mechanics that allow you to drift around corners with ease. At the same time, the game has over 100 different cars that all have a very unique handling behavior and charm. You will gradually unlock faster and more resilient cars as you complete challenges across the map. Even after unlocking the late game cars, I still like to drive around in the earlier cars from time to time for their appearance and driving experience.
The online mode of the game is also really entertaining. You can freely roam around and the city and chase after your friends to try and take them down. Alternatively, you can team up with your friends to try and complete online challenges. Some challenges are quite difficult, as they require a specific number of players and require you to complete a task under a time limit. However, the reward for completing all of the online tasks is a very exclusive (and dapper) car.
Overall, one of my favorite car/racing games I have ever played because of the freedom, exploration, and online activities. The downside to the game is it is no longer updated, so there are many patches needed for minor bugfixes and stability fixes on newer operating systems.
As many have said, "The Ultimate Box" does not include the DLC of Big Surf Island, the legendary cars, or the toy cars. Despite the exclusion of DLC, this game is definately worth the buy during a sale.

Bastion is the first title from Supergiant Games, and it’s an impressive first release. You play “the kid”, a young boy who wakes up after a terrible accident that has shattered the world. The kid then tries to rebuild the world, by going from city to city and collecting the needed pieces.
Gameplay-wise, Bastion is a dungeoncrawler where you fight your way through set levels and enemies. It’s simple and straightforward; Right click for one type of attack, left click for another. You can also collect potions to be able to perform a limited amount of special attacks. There is no inventory system, but you can switch through weapons when you return to your base, to where you return after each finished level. I found the gameplay quite easy and it was a casual and relaxing experience.
However, the greatness of this game doesn’t lie in the combat system: It lies in the beautiful audio, graphics and storytelling. Bastion is a work of art.
When you start the game, the first thing you will notice is the narrator. A sooth voice that tells the story about the kid as you are experiencing it. As you start walking, you will see the floor and walls being created around you as you move forward. And finally, the soundtrack is gorgeous. I am listening to it now, weeks after I finished the game.
The game has a good length – I finished in around 8 hours all in all. But it’s also the kind of game that you may want to return to and play again. I warmly recommend it.

Fran Bow is a surreal, engaging experience best enjoyed alone in the dark. The game left me questioning whether or not what Fran sees is reality, her imagination, or even a combination of both. As the game progressed I became more and more engrossed in the story and the characters and I felt a wide range of emotions while playing, anything from sadness to anger to joy and the transition between moods was at times instantaneous. If you're a fan of story rich games and macabre humor I cannot recommend this enough.
Pros:
+Wonderful soundtrack that is both joyful and creepy, very fitting with the game.
+Engaging story that kept me wanting more at all times.
+Interesting characters and Fran's reactions to things are hilarious and adorable at times.
+Intuitive puzzles that rewards note taking and in the majority of cases make sense as well.
Cons:
-Some event chains made no sense and I had to look at a guide for these, but they were few in number.
Neutral:
=The end feels a bit abrupt but in my opinion the ambiguous nature of the ending fit the game thematically. YMMV.
=Lack of voice acting might be a negative for some, I personally didn't mind.
Conclusion:
I bought this game on sale, having never heard of it but this game is definitely worth the full price as well. The story for me took about 12 hours to complete and I enjoyed every minute of it. I felt like there could have been more to the ending but I understand why the creators would choose to end it the way they did. Overall Fran Bow was a wonderful game and my greatest regret is not having heard about it sooner.

Sleeping Dogs is a sandbox crime action game that's much like any GTA clone, but set in Hong Kong. The setting makes a key difference, as the story makes for an interesting almost modern Kung-Fu movie in the cops vs Triad vein, and guns are uncommon due to national gun laws. The majority of the combat is done hand to hand as well with environmental actions (and unofficially cars if you can get one in a fight). The combat is comparable to the Batman Arkham games, but not nearly as fluid, varied or rewarding. Main missions are scored by how well you balance yourself as an undercover cop and a rising Triad gang member - you want to be as brutal as possible to gang members with the least collateral damage to civilians as possible. The gunplay is standard fare for games of this type, which in my opinion is generally not great and nowhere near as satisfying as a real shooter, but it serves it's job and features the bullet time system which I think comes from the True Crime series this game is an extension of - though more skilled shooters will find this largely useless (tough, guns aren't as accurate as they would be in something Like Uncharted or Warframe). You get a pretty well interpreted vision of Hong Kong, though a disappointing foray in it as you don't get to really explore any of the skyscrapers which HK is known for.
I played the game for a good bit and was going to stop playing it for a while, as it was another crime sandbox game and I could already tell I would tire of repetitive side, race, "collect dozens of X" missions. I nearly did, before I realized I put some hours into the story, so I might as well finished the Story missions at minimum. I got more intrigue with the story of seeing how the Sun On Yee gang you're involved with changes and evolves and seeing how Wei Shen would deal with the battle of being both a genuine officer of the law, yet a violent criminal - while there are plot holes in the situation, I enjoyed the story enough to actually be interested in the sequel, which is a surprise to me as story is rarely important to me, especially in sandbox games, and I knew halfway through the game I wasn't interested in the story until I got deeper into it. There seems to be quite a decent selection of tracks on the radio stations which unfortunately I didn't hear much of as much of the cars I drove were among the same 2-3 stations by default (and I didn't care to bother changing the stations since I was racing through story missions.
If you are already the kind of person that loves these games, then you are more than likely going to enjoy this. If you're more of a person with discerning taste and/or less time to deal with "not interesting" games, then you aren't really getting much here that you haven't seen in similar games before it beyond the setting and the plot. While those two aspects are generally the least important parts of a game for me, they were the two things that kept me interested enough to finish the main mission thread, though not the side mission.
At the time of writing, this game is on Summer sale for $9.99 and likely cheaper later. While I can say that I'm perfectly fine if I never played this game, I'm also glad I did, and that price is fair enough for what I experienced. And while I like complete content, I would not bother with DLC unless you expect to play this game to the fullest.

M.E.R.C. is a game where you manage a mercenary company. Every missions, you can deploy 4 differents characters (2 in alpha squad, 2 in bravo squad). You can't control each unit individualy but rather you give command to each squad. You have 4 different classes: heavy, assault, sniper and engineer, with 4 possibles sub classes, such as medic and hacker (the only ones i've seen as of yet). There is coop where you can do a mission with a friend or random person and everybody control theirs alpha squad, which looks like it could be fun to play with a friend (havent found a coop mission yet, the lobby was always empty).
If you have read other reviews, you might have seen many comments comparing M.E.R.C. to XCom. While I do find a ressemblance in certain aspects (main map where you review missions, the barrack where you can see your units, etc.), I really wouldn't compare to that myself, meaning don't buy this game because you liked XCom but don't pass on it because you disliked it either.
The game has many strong points and many flaws aswell, but given that it is in early access, I have strong hope that the flaws will be corrected and worked upon. Here is a list of the points that I like and what I feel the game should improve.
The good:
-4 differents classes and 4 subclasses give many different options but I feel they could have more than 2 active skills per classes (example: The assault class has grenade and a firing supression skill, and that's it. There are a few passives that modify skills, like the poison grenades, but I feel in the end, every assault is just the same).
-Seems to have many different pieces of chest armor, leg, helmet and weapons that you can find and buy. Weapons are restricted to classes but they have various stats.
-Armor you equip does show on your character (there are no customization like you had in XCom to choose a character's appearance yet, not sure if they want to add that).
-Combat is fast and animation are fluid. It always feel satisfying to watch a squad of ennemies explode when you shoot barrels or throw grenade at them.
-Graphics looked good enough for me (I started playing video game with the first doom on MS-DOS so I dont care too much about that. But they look nice enough).
-I think the story for the game is interesting. Not sure how much it gets developped as I've only finished the first few 'storyline' mission but I felt it was worth reading instead of skipping all the time.
The 'will require more work in the future': As I said, I'm sure it will be worked on at some point, but if you find those would ruin your experience, then you can decide to delay your purchase until they've had a few more updates in the game.
-I feel the music is very repetitive. I felt like turning it off after my game session.
-AI is extremely dump. They will take cover on the side of barricades that are facing you (meaning you shoot them in the back), they will start running at you and get insta killed all the time. Once I threw a grenade at a patrol over a wall, almost killing them all. They fell to the ground, stood back up and continued their patrol like nothing happened. Sometimes ennemies will shoot at the wall with rockets, not even damaging you, instead of moving to another cover.
-Talking of cover: If your guys have no line of sight to the ennemies, they'll just stand there and do nothing when you ask them to fire. Moving to the nearest place with a LOS would have been nice.
-Your guys will often stay idle while you have ennemies running around them at almost melee distance. They do fire back when fired upon though.
-Opening a container makes your character stuck there until you close the container manualy (if there is an item you cant take in it). if you dont see it right away, you get into fights with only 3 guys realizing that the other one is still at the box, 100m away.
-When you recruit a new unit, you cant know what his subclass is. In fact, if you try to see its skill tree, it cause other bugs that you need to reload the game or go do a mission to fix.
-There is no difficulty setting. I found myself instantly killing any ennemies as far as the edge of my screen after the first few missions where I bought assault rifles that deals more damage than the best sniper I can buy.
-Sniper class feel very underpowered. Even their headshot ability wont kill enemies in 1 or 2 hits (you have only 2-3 uses of it per mission unless you find more as loot).
-Ennemies can detect you from outside of your screen or sometimes from the other side of a wall with no LOS.
-Many many more (even though I listed quite a bunch of things, those werent harsh enough to make me want to refund this game).
I have found no game breaking bugs at all so far.
Conclusion: I would still recommand to buy this game, as I am sure it will only get better, with more features and bug cleaning. Game might be more fun if you have someone else to play with.

I see a lot of reviews comparing this game to XCOM, which isn't really accurate at all (I blame the cover shield icons). There are definitely some similarities on the macro scale re: squad management and mission selection, but the minute-to-minute gameplay is much closer to a squad-scale loot-based RTS like Dawn of War 2. I liked the focus on small, discrete engagements rather than constant run-and-gun action - it definitely feels like the game rewards smart play. Catching some fools out of cover and mowing them down is very satisfying, but if you get cocky and try to rush a fortified position, you are probably just as screwed.
Being an early access game, there are definitely some rough edges, especially around the character loadout and skill tree UIs, but so far I think this game has a lot of promise.

At first I was very reluctant to buy this game, and I will tell you these reasons:
1. Not a fan of the whole "escape the room" games. Where you have to find objects and use them to continue on with the level, its not like you get any hints or anything so if you are stuck without a walk through you could be there for hours wondering what to basically do, especially if you are convinced you picked up and clicked everything in the area.
2. Graphics were iffy to me, normally I cant get into a game unless the graphics are a certain way. At first I originally disliked character design but after buying it and playing for the very few hours I have, it kinda grew on me.
Lets get to the actual review.
Fran Bow is quite the experience which doesnt throw in any spectacular new elements to these kinds of games, the mechanics play very well like an "escape the room" game in which you pick up items, use them, combine them, examine them etc to make your way out of a room and towards the goal. To progress the story basically you have to pay attention to every item you can possibly collect and logically figure out a way to get to certain areas, keeping this goal in mind.
What is interesting is the "dimension" twist they put on the game in which Fran can freely switch between the real world and her demonic visionary world to solve puzzles. Which again, the mechanic isnt a new concept with these types of games but it does make the game very enjoyable. My favourite thing to do was swap too and from the dimensions just to see the difference in the room, even if logically I didnt have to.
The story itself is rather straight foreward at first, and only gets more skewed as you play, the game tries to make the first chapter as logical as possible with the items you pick up and you only realize the more you get into the game that the whole "logic" to escape a room has slowly turned into something of creativity. For example: (skip the next line possible spoilers below)
(((((((((((((((((SPOILER: The door you make for the tree trunk to get through.)))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))
When the story progresses you can half assume what happened to her parents in the begining, the story pegs a "bad guy" but something seems really off about it.
The story itself makes you paranoid and unaware of what is real, and it may feel like the developer isnt even trying anymore to be realistic, he just randomly makes it fiction after awhile. Which is what it may feel like, but then again it works with Fran's mental state.
Being a little ten year old girl with a mental issue you begin to question her actual morality and sanity, if I were ten I'd be screaming and freaking out seeing a head explode or feel very hesitant when it came to death and gore. Which Fran does not really show. When it comes to examining certain visions she would say stuff like "Wake up silly!" or "Oh no that baby is on the ground.."
At first I thought the dialogue just wasnt real, not for a little girl seeing so many visions and gore. Then again after reading so many dialogues of apathy/naivety towards death, it really made me understand her mindset and truly see how "not all that there" she really is.
The games ending is an "open to interpretation" sort of ending, which I will not spoil. (My curiosity spoiled it for me honestly) The tasks by some of the "demons/Ghosts" you will have to do are a little corny, and to really enjoy this game you will have to focus on the main story: Who killed Fran's Parents? What is Fran seeing and why?
I recommend it for a relaxed simple puzzle game, there is some gore but its not that bad. Music is fine, I didnt get tired of it. Try not to use a walkthrough for increased difficulty, it isn't too hard but it's still not super easy. Its a short game, it has 5 chapters but its still a fun story to get wrapped up in. Definitely a good buy when on sale. Especially if you enjoy these types of games.

Well I bought it while it was on sale and never played it until two weeks ago. It instantly got me. The story is so captivating that I didn't even collect all shrines and statues just because I wanted to continue the storyline, which doesn't happen that often when I play games like this. It is this new situation, not being a gangster like in GTA and all those titles but rather being an undercover cop, always fearing that your cover might be blown up. I will just make a list here to point out what points are outstanding and which are not that great.
Pros:
-Action Hijack. Holy. Really cool thing, it allows you to hijack someones car just by jumping off your vehicle onto theirs, like in action movies.
-Pretty big city.
-"Minigames" like picking locks, hacking codes, tracking handys and so on. Not really challenging but it is a nice gimmick to have in an action game.
-The combat system. It's really easy but it still looks pretty cool when you're doing your combos to defeat those 20 triad members.
-Not too much shooting. Weapons are pretty rare, you mainly use martial arts to fight foes.
-Different culture. The setting is authentic, the voice acting well done, just the traffic sucks.
-Very cool characters. Reminds me of Mafia & Mafia II.
-The captivating story. Wei Shen (you) gets a bit attached during the story and you can understand him due to what you and the characters go through.
-Nice graphics. Nothing outstanding but they fit well. Not comparable to Mafia II though.
Cons:
-The driving. Meh. Not really dynamic, but it doesn't affect the gameplay too much.
-THE TRAFFIC. Who the heck drives on the left side. 10/10 would crash.
-The physics. Some things just look really weird especially when you're driving through everything but you suddenly crash because you hit a sidewalk.
-Not enough to do besides the story. You don't have that much sidequests but that's totally fine since the story is so good.
Conclusion:
If you like games like Mafia, Mafia II and GTA Vice City then you're gonna love this game (at least its story). It just feels like a good thriller.

It's a neat idea to have a remastered version of 2004's Doom 3, which also contains RoE and classic Doom games, but i don't think it's that good as i thought. You know why? Because of the changes to Doom 3 and RoE and classic Doom games:
1. Game being brighter. I know a lot of people thought that original Doom 3 was TOO dark, but making it brighter reduces the atmosphere that this game has. Even with lowest brightness setup, the game is a little bit brighter than max brightness in the original.
2. Mounted flashlight - probably THE MAIN reason why a lot of people prefer this version over the original. Makes sence for console versions (PS3/XBox360), but PC - not so much. I like that vulnerability situation when you hold a flashlight in the original game and there's an enemy in your face. In this version: Enemy in front of you in the dark room; flashlight on; shotgun to the face with flashlight on. Also the flashlight is limited, unlike the original 2004 game.
3. Ammo. The game quite literally feeds you with an ammo. In Level 4 of Doom 3 campaign i ended up with full shotgun and machine gun ammo. Even on Veteran, it's easy with all that ammo. I think it makes sence for console versions to feed you with an ammo, but for PC - not at all.
4. Level changes in RoE are just stupid in my opinion: Waste Tunnels have been changed by removing the gas in the tunnels and the helmet in this kind of an airlock, so you don't have to kill Hazard zombies to get their oxygen tanks, well you need to kill everyone you see, but you get the idea. Entire section in Hell, where you need to use an Artifact to puch out a bunch of Mancubi, Hellknights and Imps, is completely gone, The Maledict fight is easier because 1. He doesn't spawns Lost Souls, and 2. The rocks (or meteorites or whatever the hell they are) do less damage.
5. If you think it's enough of changes? No, because the changes to classic Doom games are even worse: Wolfenstein levels after Map 15 are just "naked", 2 changes to Nightmare! difficulty involves the speed of Demons being reduced to UV speed and the speed for fireballs being reduced. The red cross in Medikits, Stimpacks and Berserk packs have been replaced by red'n'white pill, which is lame. The music sounds weird and awkward, can't: change controlls, open the console, use cheats, play multiplayer. Just, why?
The Lost Missions are fine, but they're too short.
Conclusion
Doom 3: BFG Edition is a good way to remember the horror of the original Doom 3, it's still enjoyable, i would recommend it if not for changes, but no. I would say, if you own original Doom 3: Phisical copy or Steam, stick with them, and if you really want to play the remastered version - "Go 2 It", it's up to you. 6/10

TLDR version: this game has potential, but still needs a lot of work.
Long version:
For an Early Access game, this isn't bad. No bugs, or at least none that I really noticed. I've seen much worse from fully released games that were created by well known studios with huge conglomerates behind them. Even the 'Work in Progress' Axe throwers and the accompanying building, seemed to work fine. The graphics are lovely as well.
That said, there is as yet not that much content, and the AI was not much of a challenge, at least not at the normal setting. I hope loads more content and an option for even bigger maps will be added. But if they keep it up like this, this could turn into a great game. I just hope it won't turn out to be an utter disappointment, like so many games, that are abandoned somewhere along the way, or at least never live up to anything even close to their full potential. I also hope the AI will be improved, to be more of a challenge. One of the AI enemies seemed to be stuck, possibly never progressed beyond the first building, although it somehow acquired about half of the map.
After that first game, for some reason, I have been running into trouble. But not from the AI, but from the game mechanics. There aren't many buildings in the game yet, but you need several of them to keep going. However, you can only build a few in each territory. Pretty soon, you get into trouble. You either run out of resources, building space, villagers, or something else. Sometimes everything seems to be going fine, then an earthquake hits, or your food gets eaten, and suddenly the situation seems beyond recovery.
As yet, I can't really recommend the game, as it is nowhere near finished, and I've been burned by pre-orders for games that absolutely had no excuse for being as disappointing as they turned out to be. You never know with Early Access games. All I know is, I hope they continue the way they have been going, they seem to be on the right track. Since I am forced to make a choice between recommending this game, and not recommending it, I sadly have to choose no. But it makes me feel a bit guilty. I hope that, when the game is developed further, I will be able to update this review and change my recommendation.

Just played my first playthrough. I must say... I really enjoyed it! I've never experienced this type of game before so it felt a bit strange. I would recommend this game to anyone that doesn't mind the old style anime appeal and a text based adventure that you play a part in. My ony major complaint is that at the end of teh game, the Daughter says how she felt in Japanese with no translation! I even used a translation app to try and get the gist of what she was talking about, but it couldn't hear her clear enough. Also, I'm not sure if this is a glitch or whatever, but my Daughter, kept failing doing the Inn job, even though I spammed it until I reached max cooking. As everyone mentions, the translation can be bad, but I haven't found it to be distracting at all. But in spite of the downsides, I really loved this game! The girl, seeing her age from 10 to 18 really pulls at your heartstrings and makes you feel like you bonded and raised this (hopefully) great girl thats now a woman. I felt proud knowing that my little girl turned into a noble soldier.
So in short:
Pros
Fantastic music
Engaging classic RPG fighting/adventure
Many Endings
Diverse ways to play
Truly endearing
Pacing feels great (8 years to see things unfold)
Cons:
Certain Stats feel a less useful (ie temperment)
Translation (Average player shouldn't be too annoyed)
Daughter's Life Summary words not subtitled (God this is the worst! Please fix)
Wishes:
More clothing would have been awsome. /thnking about all the playthroughs I could do, seeing the few thats present is kind of dissappointing. The could even have the same stats as clothing already present.Think of them as "alternative" outfits.
An "Ending Vault" so that I can view the Daughter's Life Summary after I unlock it. This would be cool, as the player would feel like even like their Daughter is gone but not forgotten.
The other Princess Makers! I saw that Princess Maker 5 was created in Japan. I'm thankful for this one we have, but I would expect Princess Maker 5 to be even more incredible. I would even be happy if we got 3 and 4 first within quick succession.
I hope my horrible review helps someone decide if this game is worth their time. If you enjoy life simulation, I think this "schedule" style simulation is a good approach. It really makes you feel like you're raising a Daughter in an anime styled world. I imagine the playthroughs feel uniquely different as you don't have time to make some "god" character. Can't wait for tomorrow since I will be making my second Daughter!
If the Developer's see this review. Please fix that subtitle problem! I felt so disconennected from my Daughter at that time. It was almost sadder then knowing she has grown up and left her Father...

Unlike a Tamagotchi, your daughter (probably) isn't going to end up dead in a room full of nothing but poop. I can't confirm since I haven't gotten all 70ish endings, but she's a lot more likely to grow up to be the queen of all poops. Or a dancer, which might be worse--I didn't spend
and tens of thousands of gold on a top-notch education just for you to become a
sweetie.
Now you, too, have the opportunity to probably be a terrible parent without risking permanent damage to your delicate lady parts or 18 years' worth of child support payments. In real life, careless parenting is pretty much limited to leaving your child unattended for hours in the nearest Walmart. In Princess Maker 2, your precious daughter can literally marry Satan when she grows up. Next time, don't let her work at the cabaret and partake in underage drinking, Dad.
You're (probably) not going to hell after playing this game, despite the old DOS version’s greatly exaggerated reputation. And if you do, at least you have a shot at marrying the supreme ruler of Hell--if your poorly raised daughter hasn't married him first. The only thing removed from the original game is the cheat/debug mode, so you have to actually raise your child and force her to work or explore and fight in the RPG sections if you want a steady supply of cash.
As I pushed my daughter to the brink of exhaustion and forced her to work on the farm for weeks at a time, I realized I didn’t care enough about her dreams and feelings. I cared about
: getting her the best marriage partner, raising her to be the strongest combatant in the realm…okay, and the actual game achievements. Right now, some of them are kind of buggy, but they’re all legitimately attainable. I assume they’ll be fixed in a later patch.
As others have mentioned, the current translation is a bit rough around the edges and your daughter’s speech at the end of the game desperately needs subtitles—unless you’re fluent in Japanese. I am glad for the added voice acting, though it can get repetitive after a while. Setting the text to instant (or “Without wait,” as the odd translation puts it) helps a lot if you’re speeding through to get different achievements and endings. It’s a shame the Steam overlay doesn’t work, but it might be unavoidable considering the age of the game.
Despite the minor issues I have with PM2, I’d love to see Princess Makers 3-5 on Steam someday, so I can continue to accidentally torment my innocent blank slate of a child as I try to shape her into what I failed to become in my own life. But as
they say, it's never too late to become a queen of darkness.

Alright so, this port isn't quite as good as the original DOS version. The graphics while better aren't as charming, the music is a bit buggy and the translation has weird moments ("Your daughter has been defeated by" being your victory screen for example) but at the same time, its just as fun as the original game. I wouldn't go as far and say the port is terrible, but take it as a warning.
Now onto the actual game. Its great. You ever play Long Live The Queen? They're fairly similar games. The main difference being that Long Live The Queen being more focused on political and militaristic aspect of castle life, this game is more of a general life simulator set in a castle. You can do so much with raising your daughter, its pretty insane how much content their is in that regard. You can train her to be a soldier, a priestess, a teacher, a dancer, a singer, an artist, a witch, any blend of those and so much more. The game has over 40 endings too!
The game also has a combat system and dungeon exploration if you chose a more offensive route. They're extremely simple, but they get the job done and are pretty rewarding. I do wish the dungeon exploration had more to it, but its still fun for what it is. On another note, the soundtrack of the game is pretty underrated. While its not the best, the tunes in the game are very relaxing and make me feel at ease.
This game isn't without its flaws however. My biggest gripe is that your daughter can get extremely overpowered relatively early in the game. I'm only in Year 2 (out of 8) and I'm already one-shotting dragons and winning the Harvest Festival. I think they did it to try to make your daughter proficient at several task at once but its still a bit wonky. The game can also get weird sometimes. You can feed her breast-expanding pills as early as Year 1 and one of the endings involves you marrying your daughter. Weird stuff..
Overall, a great life simulation game. Probably my favorite, even better than Long Live The Queen in my book.

First off I've played very little of the versus mode of this game, my first forte into Left 4 Dead period was on the Xbox 360 and even then I mostly stuck to the campaign so this review is specifically about the campaign.
When Left 4 Dead had first come out I had very little experience with any zombie games and at least as far as I could see the insane zombie craze that is now all around us hadn't blown up so big. Left 4 Dead's campaign can be both a hectic and amazing experience with or without friends. The AI Director is nothing to gawk at and is much more challenging in my opinion on the PC version than on the Xbox 360, it shapes the way the Special Infected act and how frequently they spawn and when a horde is going to rush you out of nowhere. Controls are tight with mouse and keyboard and feel really good, the music is beautiful and the little changes and noises that play to alert you of enemies or a crescendo event are very well done. All weapons and items feel useful and viable and even if you have a preference and choose to use the same weapons over and over you'll find little downside to keeping what you like. There's no real "spoken" story to say but the little bits you hear from the player characters, the well crafted environments and the writings you'll find in each safe house and even occasionally out in the world add to the sense that you know about as much the characters in the game do and I like that feeling. It feels good, it's like your in the characters shoes.

Bastion came and went with its artistic style - the narrative is refreshing in that it doesn't conform to the tried and true typical setup:

Sprinkle on top of that a fun enjoyable action game with levels, equipments, techniques... and you have a jewel of a game: fresh, beautiful, unique.

Bastion is a beautiful game from start to finish. Every location, every character, every sound is just full of life and color. The combat is exciting and rewarding, with many different weapons to mix and match to fit your play style. The level design is simple, yet well-done. The story is linear, but every step unlocks a new piece of the world, literally and figuratively. Your character will find these mementos of the world before the disaster which starts the events of the game, and each of these mementos helps paint a picture of the peaceful world of the past. The music in this game is incredibly beautiful. I feel like every part of this game was designed down to the smallest detail. It is quite an amazing journey. There was not a part of this game that I did not thoroughly enjoy.

I don't get what's so special about this game. Is it the gameplay? It's average at best, I've seen more exciting gameplay in Flash games. You can choose between a few weapons, walk around smashing enemies and objects. That's it.
Is it the incredibly innovative art style? Yes, that must be what everyone loves. And it's also the thing I like least about this game.
If this review is too long for you, skip the following 4 sections.
You play as some young guy called "Kid" who drinks spirits in a saloon to gain buffs. Also, you constantly have to listen to a narrator who sounds like he comes directly out of a really cheesy spaghetti western. He has a pseudo-cool voice and a fitting accent which just gets on your nerve after a while because it's so extremely stereotyped.
Sometimes, the narration gets pushed too far. I see a collectible and without thinking I run straight to it, the floor under my feet going down. "Kid thought twice about getting [whatever it was]", the narrator says. Wait, what? Sure, you can comment what's happening, but when I'm controlling a characterless guy such as Kid who is only defined by my own actions, you can't just act like what's on his - on MY - mind.
But let's get back to the art style. Alright, I could live with that cheesy spaghetti western feeling. But the game takes place in an extremely colorful fantasy world. You have these bright colors, carry a bright red oversized hammer while walking through the bright green grass, fighting comical enemies. And in the background, you hear that narrator with that deep voice, telling you how bad everything is and how screwed you are. Seriously, this feels like Teletubbies suffering from depression.
And if this wasn't already unfitting enough, the developers had to push it even more and add some weird oriental trip hop soundtrack which fits neither to the western setting nor to the fantasy setting.
Well, as it's neither the gameplay nor the art design which makes the game exciting for me, maybe the story is good. Let's take a look:
The world is ending. Kid has to collect some crystals to rebuild a monument in order to save the world. Not special, but not bad - yet. During his journey he finds some nice survivors who then live in your homestead. After about 30 minutes you collect the last of the few crystals, but suddenly, absolutely incredible unexpected plot twist: One of those nice survivors gets into an argument and in his rage he destroys the monument which ultimately seals the end of the world. Seriously, what the hell? Did the developers go out of ideas? This is by far the most illogical action of any character I've ever seen. So, instead of collecting 5 crystals, Kid is now supposed to collect 20 crystal shards.
I stopped playing after collecting the fifth shard because the game just didn't change. The story didn't progress any further, the gameplay stayed the same, the narration was still annoying, Kid still lacked character.
Innovation can be good, but instead of focussing on a good idea Bastion is just a mixture of multiple incoherent art styles with average gameplay.

So here's my angle on this game: I bought a PS4 just in time for me to go off to college, and my sophomore year saw me playing it some, but only first person shooters. I really hadn't bought a fighter since DBZ Budokai Tenkaichi 2, so I was like "Hey SFV is coming out, it looks really good, only 5 days from my birthday, BET!" So I got it Day 1. First mistake, I HATED the game. No content, lacking/simplistic mechanics, not many characters, no central plot, etc etc. I'd never hated a company as much as I did Capcom while I had it, even when more characters where added oh so slowly. I traded my PS4 back for an Xbox 1S. Now, I bought the game for my PC for $20, which was fair as there's more content now, a story, working servers. The fighting is great, and with season 2, I like damn near all the changes it brought to combos, frame datas, etc. I feel now there's alot more room for different, equally viable playstyles, similar to USF4. But these good changes are WAY too far out from release to really sweeten it to me. If you haven't bought this game, I'd say don't buy more than do, but $20 is a  fair price if you do. But ABSOLUTELY don't buy ANY DLC (w/ real money). ♥♥♥♥ CAPCOM for overpricing, undercooking, and underdelivering to their fans! There's still no arcade mode, the story was GARBAGE, there's no real single player content outside of the tedious survival mode and VS CPU (which didn't even come at launch). Nothing has real replay value, and there's no innovation. Just look to MKX for how much content and interesting takes on modes can enhance the experience. The DLC characters costumes and stages are ridiculously overpriced ($5-10 anyone?), and regular♥♥♥♥♥character colors too. And fanboys will say "You can earn it all for free with fight money" but fail to realize that the grind to get fight money after the initial playthroughs of story and survival is PAINFULLY slow, making it a chore to get stuff that in yesteryears would unlock from simple, fun gameplay, not an arbitrary currensy system.

Ive been on a pixel-graphics horror binge lately, and finally got to play uncanny valley
Apparently this game was supposed to be much much bigger, but wasn't funded enough, not entirely sure.
so heres the basic scoop, trying my best not to spoil anything. You are a guard meant to patrol a facility every night for 5 days, and during those days you have almost unlimited freedom, dont go to work, kill your boss with a fire extinguisher, go to work every night like a good fellow, play this game the way you want, but be warned, its a one-button interaction game, so theres no "Yes, do this, no, do that" If you can do something and click E next to it, the game does it, period.
As for how the game feels? The first playthrough you will probably feel incredibly confused most of the way through. The basic plot bits you can get from the trailers are made apparent very fast in the game if you just snoop some, but the big picture is harder to see, and if you accidentally trigger an ending early, you may be completely confused.
Some more details, this is not a game where you get to explore a town and do shifts of work, the towns you see in trailers are
, this whole game consists of the complex you work at and the apartments, along with a generator station, nothing more, all of your choices and the impacts of them take place in those zones and those alone. there are also a total of 2, yes, 2, other characters in the area when you begin, thats it.
Despite the "totally free to choose" theme, the truth is you are basically on a path to fate and you only get to choose how you come at fate. That is not meant to be a spoiler, there are many ending and they are all unique, but they all are just the result of you coming at events differently. Many of the exploration, and even combat sequences, you see in trailers do not affect the ending in any incredible way.
The last bit of bad i have to put out on this game is the simple fact that, any human being behaving normally would never, ever, ever get anything but 1 ending. This is not a game you can come at as a person and behave as yourself and see what happens, because nothing will. The only exception to this is if you are a moron like me who forgot his apartment number and slipped into the wrong one, and even then by staying or stealing from it we are behaving very unrealistically. In essence, achieving most of the endings requires you to behave like you know you are playing a videogame and just want to break or maim things until some new ending is unlocked.
For all the stated downfalls, this game has a gorgeous pixel art style and an interesting, if predictable, story. I cannot say much on the "Combat" because honest to god you can play for many of the endings and never even get the gun that the trailers depict, and I never bothered getting it.
At the end of the day, trying to stay positive, this game is an example of a fantastic concept that was executed by a creative team with a small budget. It is not a massive game, nor is it jam packed with choices, locations, or tools to use. The voice acting is simply bad, but thats because it's a game that was underbudget, and they did what they could. If you like horror and games about making choices, with replayability dependant on multiple endings, then you very well may like this game, however I strongly suggest you download the demo first and try it out, because I would never have guessed the content of this game from the trailers, they led me to believe it included daytime segments and other locations, as well as more combat, and it simply doesn't.
Try the demo, see if it still interests you, and if it does, try it out! I enjoyed my playthroughs once I understood what was happening, though that did take some time to figure out. The biggest issue i have with this game is that it is a choice based game where you have no idea where you are supposed to make choices or WHY to make them until after you have played it once or twice and see the overarching story some more, this leads to playthrough 1 and 2 being 5 nights of total boredom and looking around trying to find something exciting. And of course, since after play 1 or 2 you already know every hidden or dramatic thing, getting a great ending while the drama is still hot and mysterious simply won't happen.
Leaving review as positive because the game is not bad or broken to the point that I didnt enjoy it for the little i paid for it.

A man looking to escape his troubled past with the mob finds work as a night guard at an abandoned research facility in Uncanny Valley, a sci-fi horror game.
This game has a gradual build-up to the point where things start happening and the combination of settings and music really help to build suspense in an otherwise mundane setting. Depending on your choices for each day, you will end up on one of many storylines, each leading to its own ending. Careful exploration of the apartment complex and research facility in between doing your daily shifts will be mandatory if you want to get the best endings.
Replaying Uncanny Valley can get a bit tedious due to the fact that you have to repeat all the early beginning parts of the game including the dream sequences, so I recommend opening the game’s directory and copying the save.ini file out after clearing the first few days. You can then just copy it back for each “new” playthrough to make it less boring.
I liked this game even though it’s a bit short (probably my fault for save-scumming) and I clocked in about 4-5 hours to get almost all of the endings. Pretty good bang for your buck if you pick it up for the frequent sale price of $1!

So I am going to explain to everyone why Doom 3 is the worst game ever made. Why we have been brainwashed, tricked, backstabbed and got slapped across the face with this atrocity to mankind.

Now it's hard to say Final Doom and Doom 64 were the third Doom game for many reasons. This is mainly because Final Doom was made by modders and Doom 64 was made by Midway Games but Distributed by ID. So to be completely honest. It's hard to say which was the real third game. But in my honest opinion since ID Distributed Doom 64, it is technically the third game in the series without counting Final Doom's Plutonia Experiment and TNT Evilution. So Yes. Next is the actual presentation. The game looks awful for being released in 2004. The presentation is bland, moldy, uninspired and does not feature any good level design whatsoever. I have BFG and the original, I HIGHLY recommend to get the original instead although both are decent. The only reason you should consider BFG is for the 3D and occulus support if thats your thing. Read this before you decide on purchasing BFG edition.
TL;DR In BFG you should expect
Pros
-possibly more populous multiplayer? -3D support -Native Controller support
Cons
-Worse graphics -reduced difficulty -worse shadows/largely increased brightness -removal of most horror aspects -less mods/compatibility with current mods
--------Long form reasons for Original over BFG--------
- Gameplay mechanic changes. One of the controversial changes in BFG was the addition of the built in flashlight and removal of the flashlight weapon/item. It sounds silly to fuss over but you really need to experience the original masterpiece the way it was made to be played before bashing people for complaining about it. The game had many key scenes that were structured around that game mechanic. They pull off genuinely spooky scenes where the lights would go out and they time appearances or jump scares perfectly with how long it takes to pull out your flashlight. The flashlight mechanic was like a double edged sword, while equiped you were ready to proceed with full knowledge of your surroundings but limited on what you can do about them while gun equiped in a dark hall you might pass by a hidden foe ready to give you a surprise attack from behind!
-BFG is awefully bright in comparision to the Original, like horribly bright. Maybe it had something to do with making it for occulus rift? Perhaps 3D doesn't look good with pitch black corners so they filled all dark spaces with a light gray? Whatever the reason you probably wont even end up using the new flashlight mechanic on BFG with how visible everything is. This added to the flashlight mechanic you should expect BFG to be more of a run n gun shoot em up style game whereas Original Doom 3 will be leaning much more towards the sci fi horror. The amazing shading and shadows in original doom 3 are vastly reduced with the brightness in BFG thinning the line between "that looks amazing" and "those textures look 11 years old.." which brings me to my next point..
- There have been many custom mods created for original Doom 3 that are not compatible with BFG and make the game look better than even the latest and greatest titles out there. There are some good pre-compiled mod packs with multiple mods mixed in you can find with simple instructions with a quick google search. I recommend Sikkmod 1.2, Monoxead high-res texture pack, and Trent Reznor's sound pack. I have a 6 core CPU and AMD 6970 and some of the settings with shadows and shaders Sikkmod offers can really make a modern PC struggle, play around with it and find what works for your rig.

Aliens vs. Predator (2010) is a re-imagining of the '99 title of the same name. The game is focused on combining the Alien and Predator franchises in the same universe and having three seperate story lines, one for each of the races and for the Colonial Marines. The main selling point of the game is that each of the three races play totally differently. Only shared factor between the gameplay is the first person perspective and thus creates a nice amount of variety.
The Colonial Marines are your most basic race, the gameplay is similar to most other FPS games, you go around shooting hordes of Aliens and progress through the levels by doing different kinds of tasks. The gunplay is reasonable but not exceptional, it's nothing special and can't hold a candle to titles like F.E.A.R. but get's the job done fairly well.
Xenomorphs, (Aliens, if you're a noob.) are a beastlike species that can climb walls, move at extreme speed and use their claws, teeth, and tail to quickly incapacitate their enemies. The downside is that the Xenos are completely missing any ranged attacks, meaning you're required to take a more stealthy approach to the game as you would by playing the other two races.
Playing as a Predator lets you access a wide variety of different gadgets and advanced alien weaponry like the shoulder plasma cannon, thermal vision, optical camo and so on. Predators are extremely tough creatures and are the most powerful of the bunch, they don't have all that many weaknesses, but can still be defeated with a large enough group.
The game borrows music from the movies and has some soundtrack of it's own as well, it's pretty enjoyable to listen and fits the atmosphere very well. Especially if you're a fan of the films, then you'll get a nice nostalgia trip as well.
When AVP was released in 2010 it was one of the most demanding games by the time, (Along with Metro 2033) and looks still very good. The title was one of the pioneering DX11 games out there and supports tesselation and other basic DX11 effects as well. If you can stand some rather dated animations then you'll be fine, the textures are still better looking than in most games.
AVP also supports horde based survival coop against the Aliens, and few competetive multiplayer modes. The coop is easily the strong point of the game and is very fun to play with a bunch of friends. Competetive gameplay is most likely quite dead by the time of writing but can also be played if you happen to have enough friends for it.
In the end, if you're an Alien/Predator fan you already own the game. If you've just discovered the series and want to experience the older titles then look no further. This game is a very enjoyable ride that will take you around 13 hours to finish in single player, after which you still have the competetive and coop multiplayer to play.

Doom 3
While it's true this game is a departure from the series roots, doom 3 isn't a bad game. With a focus now on horror as well as gunplay the game widens its scope to many fans disappointment. However the graphical quantum leap from the original 1-2 lends its self to the horror atmosphere quite well. The scares may be few (if there at all) but the atmosphere is immesrive and the gunplay is fun (when dealing with the non human enemies anyway).
The game invokes total recall flashbacks from mars and even gives a nod to blade runners 2019 blaster. Keeping features from the original, doom marine still hauls a small armies worth of weapons including a chain, plasma gun and even the beloved chainsaw.
Unnecessary cutscenes occasionally pop up and temporarily break all immersion as if halflife never happened as far as the devs are concerned. Doom marine also appears to own gordons short battery flashlight which becomes crucial in darker parts of the levels... only gordon was never exposed to as much dark, thankfully it's quick to recharage and not much of an issue. Another trivial but noteworthy complaint is how quickly bodies disappear almost immediately after they hit the ground. as if the germs on the floor were more deadly than your bullets.
Doom 3 is fun just don't expect the same speed or intention of the originals. If you're a doom vet and long to zip around the halls like the glory days, this game's not for you (there's even a sprint bar now). As it stands alone though doom 3 is worth playing.

tl;dr - Far inferior to the unreleased DOS version.  I can only justify buying this to send a message that the west wants these games.  It's up to you to decide if you want to spend $20 on a worse version of a game from 1993 - along with my hesitant recommendation, I recommend reading into the history of SoftEgg's attempt at bringing the game to the US if you're on the fence.  I may not know how tl;dr works.
Like most of the other reviewers, I played the DOS version of this game a TON when I was growing up.  I consider the story behind that version's failed release to be one of the greatest disappointments in video game history - look into it, if you feel so inclined.  Had the release succeeded, we may well have seen official English releases for many more Gainax titles.  Titles I have never played, and would sorely like to.  The fact that this is actually getting an official release in western markets now, so long after the fact, is surprising.  However, there is one thing that is preventing me from fully embacing this release: the translation.
As others have noted, the translation is vastly inferior to the unreleased DOS version.  The opening text crawl, which you can see on the Store page, has some amazing Engrish (to be fair, nothing else in the game quite reaches that level).  There are grammatical and spelling errors abound, and in a game that is largely text based it's pretty annoying.  In addition, certain stats and skills now have names that don't really make sense.  Charisma has become Glamour, Refinement has become Elegance, and neither of those are really troubling.  But in a game where the religious symbolism is extremely western (crosses and nuns), why has "Sin" become "Karma?"  It doesn't even make any sense.  You actually GAIN karma for doing sinful things, and if I hadn't made the connection to the DOS version, I may have thought that was a good thing.  Also, and this is admittedly a minor point, Conversation is now "Speech."  The skill is basically tracking your daughter's ability to engage in witty conversation with people, so Conversation is far more appropriate.  Speech sounds more like she's learning to speak properly... yet, the only way to increase it is by working at the Bar, and proper speech is actually governed by Decorum.  It's silly.
It makes me sad that such an inferior version of the translation has seen a release that the DOS version never did.  I yearn for the days of the original's nostalgic, pixelized art, though I'm willing to accept that that's more about my own nostalgia - the art isn't really bad.  I think some of the art has altered your daughter's poses as she grows, but that may have something to do with blood type, and I've only played one game, so I can't definitively state that's the case.
Also, another minor point (not so minor?) - going full screen stretches the game's aspect ratio rather than retaining it via a border or something.  It looks terrible, so play windowed.  And why did my daughter stare lovingly at me and speak Japanese to me for 90 seconds upon completion of the game?  There was no text in that segment, which if I recall from the DOS version, was a letter your daughter wrote to you thanking you for all you've done for her.
Honestly, I'm not sure if I want to recommend this.  The unofficial DOS version is better in just about every way.  I don't condone piracy at all, but it's hard to justify paying $20 for an inferior version of a game from the early 90s.  I haven't looked into what the community is doing with this release - if smarter people than I are going to find a way to crack and fix this game, then buy it.  I bought it solely because I want to send a message to the Japanese makers of games like these that there is a market for them in the west.  They're fantastic and I want them.

I don't get what's so special about this game. Is it the gameplay? It's average at best, I've seen more exciting gameplay in Flash games. You can choose between a few weapons, walk around smashing enemies and objects. That's it.
Is it the incredibly innovative art style? Yes, that must be what everyone loves. And it's also the thing I like least about this game.
If this review is too long for you, skip the following 4 sections.
You play as some young guy called "Kid" who drinks spirits in a saloon to gain buffs. Also, you constantly have to listen to a narrator who sounds like he comes directly out of a really cheesy spaghetti western. He has a pseudo-cool voice and a fitting accent which just gets on your nerve after a while because it's so extremely stereotyped.
Sometimes, the narration gets pushed too far. I see a collectible and without thinking I run straight to it, the floor under my feet going down. "Kid thought twice about getting [whatever it was]", the narrator says. Wait, what? Sure, you can comment what's happening, but when I'm controlling a characterless guy such as Kid who is only defined by my own actions, you can't just act like what's on his - on MY - mind.
But let's get back to the art style. Alright, I could live with that cheesy spaghetti western feeling. But the game takes place in an extremely colorful fantasy world. You have these bright colors, carry a bright red oversized hammer while walking through the bright green grass, fighting comical enemies. And in the background, you hear that narrator with that deep voice, telling you how bad everything is and how screwed you are. Seriously, this feels like Teletubbies suffering from depression.
And if this wasn't already unfitting enough, the developers had to push it even more and add some weird oriental trip hop soundtrack which fits neither to the western setting nor to the fantasy setting.
Well, as it's neither the gameplay nor the art design which makes the game exciting for me, maybe the story is good. Let's take a look:
The world is ending. Kid has to collect some crystals to rebuild a monument in order to save the world. Not special, but not bad - yet. During his journey he finds some nice survivors who then live in your homestead. After about 30 minutes you collect the last of the few crystals, but suddenly, absolutely incredible unexpected plot twist: One of those nice survivors gets into an argument and in his rage he destroys the monument which ultimately seals the end of the world. Seriously, what the hell? Did the developers go out of ideas? This is by far the most illogical action of any character I've ever seen. So, instead of collecting 5 crystals, Kid is now supposed to collect 20 crystal shards.
I stopped playing after collecting the fifth shard because the game just didn't change. The story didn't progress any further, the gameplay stayed the same, the narration was still annoying, Kid still lacked character.
Innovation can be good, but instead of focussing on a good idea Bastion is just a mixture of multiple incoherent art styles with average gameplay.

If I were to sum up Fran Bow I'd say it was one part Wizard of Oz and two parts Nightmare on Elm Street. Right from the start there's a lot of creepy, messed up things going on and it's not all Fran. The art style is exceptional in adding to the mystery and unsettling situation we find Fran in.
Let's talk about Fran for a moment. An 11 year old girl whose parents were killed and she now finds herself basically an orphan in an insane asylum for children. Yet Fran doesn't really exhibit the angsty, f - the world, brooding personality we would expect. Instead she looks at all things happening with a positive sort of naive response. See a bunch of dead fetus' in a well she's happy it took it's umbilical cord with it. Head explode right in front of her she speaks to the fresh corpse like it might respond any minute with some extra twitching. Maybe it's the massive amounts of drugs or just her not being mature enough to realize something is wrong that she is such a tragic character. And you really want to give her a happy ending with all the trials she seems to be going through it's just a lot at any age. However, you're going into this knowing that Fran probably isn't all there.
Around half way through the game starts blurring the lines between what might be real and what might be in Fran's head. The story alludes to there being multiple realities that we're experiencing but you are left questioning what's real. You can imagine early on how this will end but I really enjoyed getting  there. It's not all doom and gloom the entire way through but the story never alludes to you getting to a better place. Even when you finally reach your destination what you uncover isn't quite what you expect. The ending does leave a good amount of room for interpretation.
The puzzle aspect of the game was thoughtful and well designed. Nothing was too difficult to figure out and solutions utilized both of Fran's mental states to complete. There was a journal that you received sometime during your journey that also alluded to another character's perspective of a journey similar to Fran's. In addition to being a companion for a few of the game's puzzles I wish it could have played a bigger role. It wasn't useless as an inventory item but there was a time when I just completely neglected it as some random unimportant item.
In all this was a disturbing but well thought out game. There were some parts that felt a bit boring but nothing felt like it was a grind or filler for getting through the story. It's a heartbreaking and disturbing tale but well worth the price of admission.

Oh boy. This game has so many interface problems it's basically unplayable. It's almost as if it's screwing with the player on purpose. Where do I start...
* I guess the worst issue is the timer. You see, you work as a security guard in Uncanny Valley, and there is a routine you have to follow every day. But I guess using a normal ♥♥♥♥ing clock would have been too much to ask. Instead of, say, clear instructions like "your shift starts at 8 PM and ends at 4 AM", you get a countdown of 6 real-time minutes whenever you wake up. Every time I showed up to work, my superior complained I was late, and I couldn't tell if he was just being an♥♥♥♥♥or if I was indeed late.
* The timer does not pause when you read memos, browse menu items or talk to people. That in itself is a♥♥♥♥♥♥move, but because you have to actually press (and keep pressed) a button to see the timer, you won't realize you're wasting time at first.
* You can't use your flashlight and run simultaneously, don't ask me why. Environments are usually pitch black, so make your choice between seeing where you're going and getting anything done in the 6 minutes you get every day.
* The flashlight turns off by itself on every screen transition, and there's one on average every 5 seconds. Environments tend to be pitch black, so I often thought the game was still loading the next screen, when in fact the timer was ticking and I had to turn the flashlight on again. And again. And again.
* There's a hidden timer when the 6 minutes go by. It reads "shift over", but if you take too long to get back to your apartment, your character falls asleep wherever he is. Regardless of whether I did or not, however, my character always woke up exhausted and with the same 6 minutes, and the boss complained of tardiness even if I ran straight to the office. Couldn't tell if I was doing something wrong, or if that's just how the game is.
* You never know what direction you're supposed to walk after screen transitions (and as I said, they're pitch black). I lost count of how many times I mistakenly exited an area immediately upon entering because I pressed left instead or right, or vice-versa. And the goddamn timer keeps ticking.
* Items will highlight on the ground, you press the interact button, nothing happens; you press the pick up button (yes, there's a separate button for interaction and picking up), nothing happens. You adjust your position a few times. No messages, no changes, nothing. AND THE %##%$%# TIMER KEEPS TICKING.
* On the other hand, my character is now lugging a freaking fire extinguisher he found in the kitchen around. There's no fire or any sort of emergency going on, but whatever floats his boat.
TL;DR: The interface is atrocious and the game is ♥♥♥♥ing unplayable as a result. Any artistic merits Uncanny Valley might have had are obscured by how horrendous and frustrating the act of playing it is.

I suppose I should preface by saying I got this game through the Humble Bundle for a different game, and only decided to try it for the sake of Steam Trading Cards.
I've played my share of Survival Horror games, but this one was very poor. After one of the slowest starts I've seen, combined with a very lukewarm 'horror' portion, you end up thrust into what I could only describe as an overly active point-and-click style game with the same lack of conveyance as a Sierra title. The game encourages you to play multiple times for different endings, since there are numerous flags that switch what in game 'path' you're on, but I would not be willing to sit through the beginning more than twice. Not only that, failing to live counts as an ending itself, which, coupled with the conveyance problems mentioned earlier, is very easy to do. After trying several times and repeatedly dying to androids while trying to sprint away with limited stamina, I gave up, because the story was quite frankly, not worth it. The dialogue is very shortform and I have trouble believing anybody in this game is a real character. Buck swears a lot, Tom has zero personality, Eve is literally a droning AI, and the entire thing comes off as bland. I cannot invest in these characters, so much so, that I ended up accidentally killing Buck with a fire extinguisher in cold blood during my first playthrough and literally did not care. When a survival horror game can't even make death an undesirable experience, it's failed.

This game is a good time. Stuck in that odd area between obscurity and fame, it offers a good single-player, freeroaming, sandbox experience. This game was released before GTA V, and yet manages to do some things better than it. (I'm comparing this game to GTA because, honestly, that's its main competitor. Some very obvious 'it-isn't-broken-so-don't-fix-it' aspects of sandboxes are kept here which may be misconstrued as ripping off GTA anyway.)
The story is... well, I won't spoil it, but you're in China. That's about all you need to know that isn't stupendously spoilerific. . .
The driving is a blast. It controls surprisingly well for having to steer the damned things using WASD (default), and there are plenty of things you can do with your vehicles. It's a trip driving on the left side of the road coming from GTA (Although the opposite might stand true if you live in a left-side drive country to begin with), but you get used to it after a while. As you drive in the sandbox-- you'll be doing quite a bit of that, I assure you-- various achievements pop up on the right side as HUD that will track odd(ly fun) things like how long you can drive without slamming into something while still following the laws of traffic (generally) but not stopping. That's
difficult, by the way. Driving in missions is proportionally more exciting as you'd expect; although it can be frustrating at times, it's extremely tense either way.
The combat is
a blast. The main character is fluent in kickass-- and I mean
says it builds up faster if you use a variety of attacks, but I never found that to be the case. Despite all of this bashing about its repetitivity, it's really not so bad as long as you don't play the game in 12-hour-long sessions.
Overall, this game is... well, a good time. I know I've already said that, but it's really the best way to describe it. The compelling story might keep you going longer than the fights and interesting-yet-limited three separate experience bars, and running someone over might be both more fun and efficient (read: broken) than using the already-rare guns, but the positives by far outweigh the negatives in this sandbox giant alternative.
