This game is great and for the first time in my gaming life have I come across a fighting game as epic as this. Control works perfectly given that you own yourself a controller (can't imagine playing this game on keyboard), sound seems a bit dependent on your audio codecs on cutscenes, graphics look briliant and the gameplay is very reminiscent to earlier games in the series with Babality making a comeback as well as gruesome fatalities.
The Komplete Edition comes with a host of unlockables that you can purchase using in-game points which can be easily obtained by playing the story mode. Some might be dissapointed by the fact that most of the characters are already unlocked in this edition. But what I love about this game is the new X-Ray attacks which look amazing though quite ridiculous making the game less gory and more comical at times.
One major problem with this port is the cutscenes. It appears as though hey are videos recorded from the console version which probably isn't far from the truth. It causes slight pausing/freezing everytime they start which is after fights and the drop in quality, graphics-wise, is very obvious, plus if you have audio codecs installed on your computer, you might notice a significant difference in terms of audio quality and, in some cases, volume. One can only hope that the developer would release an update where the cutscenes are rendered using the in-game engine thus eliminating all of the aforementioned problems.
Overall I highly recommend this game. The story mode is beyond epic and neatly tells the story of Mortal Kombat from MK1 to MK3 with slight adjustments making the story very clear and very movie-like. The gameplay itself is very entertaining especially if played online against strangers, better yet multiplayer with up to 4 players playing at a time. Looking forward to the next Mortal Kombat game and movie!

Gameplay footage of the first two missions -
M.E.R.C. feels very familiar to X-COM, and the older, tactical strategy shooter Syndicate. For an Early Access game M.E.R.C. seems to work in almost all areas. We have not come across any bugs or game breaking bugs (yet) which is often the case with Early Access games, but this ran really fluid and was quite enjoyable to play altogether!

Prepare your team and equip them in a whole host of gear with a massive repertoire of goods, more options are available than its biggest contender X-COM, which is good news. Another factor M.E.R.C. has over X-COM is when a party member dies you don’t lose them forever which was one of the most infuriating aspects of X-COM, but was an element that was essential nonetheless. It is just nice to not have to worry about losing your squad permanently in this game, especially when expenses need to be carefully considered with the in-game budget you receive, but whether any of that changes is obviously yet to be seen.
Co-Op play works well too. The setting up of a lobby is a little odd as you have to host a mission and then work out how to invite your friends. If you could just invite your friend via Steam invite that would make this game a perfect online shooter.
Overall this game has so much potential and at the stage it is at right now reflects that.

I am excited about this game!  The gameplay is solid and challenging, and the squad-based tactics are cool - only a few hours in so far and I can see how the Alpha/Bravo mechanics will really become important.  Looking forward to trying it in co-op.  The special abilities of each squad member are bloody fun too - not only do they add neat effects but they are game changers in a combat situation.  A lot of games just use a "boost" mechanic with abilities to just make you stronger or more resistant to damage, etc., but some of these MERC abilities really mess the enemies up.
satisfying.  And you get to pick them and build them out as your mercs level up!
What brings it together though is the meta-aspect of managing your squad.  It has a strong impact on how you play - the loss of even one soldier turns into a management problem that adds another strategic level to the game and really puts you into the "commander" role.  Buying armor/weapons, recruiting new mercs to swap out while others heal, training abilities, etc - lightweight management between missions, but important and well integrated.  Looking forward to seeing more armor and weapon content come along.
tl;dr - Really pleased with M.E.R.C so far.

At the beginning of this month, I gave this game a "not reccommended" review. Why? Because I'm a veteran player of this game. I got this game about a month after its release on Steam (Feb 9th, 2014). Back then, the game was totally different than it is today. As you look in a lot of the other negative reviews, most veteran players will say the same thing, about how the game took a total turn on us and became something we weren't very content with.
But I feel that's a bit biased.
Yeah, the game took a total turn on those who got it and loved it when it first was released. The game had features that so many people were looking for in a sandbox game. Back then, you used to have hunger, a reason to start a home on a planet, a reason to love a planet, take care of it, etc. The game was fun, extremely fun for someone who found the absolute perfect game for the longest time. It changed on us and most of us didn't like it, at all.
However, the game is still a fun game today. Although it took a turn, it's not right to give this game a negative review just because I don't like the changes that have been made. The game is still enjoyable once I look past all of the memories of what it used to be.
Yeah, I miss the insentive to farm, or the need for food or else you'd starve.
I miss the reason of having a home, a place that you built yourself, countless hours of gathering just to make it right for you, so that you can store all of your treasures and belongings in rooms full of crates and bins, while now everything can just go right into your ship as you keep upgrading it. I absolutely hate the quest system, being forced directly into it, when I got so used to being my own person on my own adventure with my own story, not some pre-made one.
To me, the game is now just:
> mine to the centre of the planet
> gather the ores you need
> beam up (Oh yeah, you had to be on the surface to beam up to your ship back then)
> finish quest
> head to the next planet
The game used to be a challenge, a huge challenge. You couldn't find overpowered weapons in just any random chest across the planet. You actually had to go through these giant enemy bases and clear them out to find something of high value. Now, it seems that you can find just about everything you need in a few chests laying around the planet.
The combat wasn't so clunky. Aliens constantly stuttering and lagging towards the player, enemies freezing up, going at about 1FPS, it didn't used to be that way for me.
I don't feel much as a
than I do a
, and that's not what I got this game for back when it was released.
But, it's still a playable game for those who are new, and for those who want to give it a try.
It's somewhat fun, functional, and a game nonetheless.
So I'm flipping my
to a positive review, because although I'm not happy with the way it changed, it still is an enjoyable game for those who don't know about the old Starbound.
, The development of Starbound completely turned from what it originally was, and ruined the game for the veteran players, but the game is still a game nonetheless.

People will tell you that Street fighter V is a bad fighting game, and they're wrong.
What they mean to say is "Street fighter V is not a GOOD fighting game" and they are right.
SFV has the fewest technical aspects of a fighting game that I have seen since mortal combat 3. It has combos, Cancels, Specials, juggles, and a V skill system that lets you use a separate resource for getting out of pressure or saving up for one bursty skill. And that's it. Those are ALL the mechanics.
Is this a bad thing? No, not particularly, but it certainly isn't GOOD.
So why am I putting this as a positive review? Because SFV is great at being your entry into the fighting game genre. It's got enough technicality to let you understand the concept of special cancels, frame traps, priority, combos, spacing, footsies, etc. The game is so basic that you learn a framework fairly quickly and get a foundation for future fighting games.
I can attest to this, as I have never been good at fighting games, but I'm rather decent at SFV. I rank in the mid/high silver, which for someone who has a rather poor track record with this genre is an accomplishment at least in my eyes. In a fairly short amount of time with a particular character you can get a feeling for what they can do, what they're supposed to do, and how to do it. You'll learn to spot overheads, understand what a mixup is and how to punish.
If you're looking for a deep fighting game with long combos that test your dexterity and give you a ton of options at your disposal, you'll be pretty disappointed here, maybe check out BlazBlue or Skullgirls. But if you're looking for a game to dip your toes in the genre I have to recommend it.

You wake up.  Stuff's falling apart.  An old guy starts narrating as you run around trying to figure out what the dink is going on.  This is the Kid's story about the Calamity.
While the actual storyline in itself has been done before, the presentation of it feels fresh and new as you discover what exactly is happening and everyone's lives beforehand and so on.  If I must make one qualm is the story is completely narrated to you during play.  That means while you're trying not to die fighting a boss or something, there is actual story being presented and it can be difficult for those who can't multitask to be able to pay attention and lose details.  It's also incredibly short, and you'll be able to do just the story in around 3 hours (not including sidequests) though the game has a New Game+ encouraging you to play a second time through with all your assets still in check.
Sprites are sharp looking, environments lush.  I think the Kid's ingame proportions look a bit off from his artwork design but eventually you get used to it.  The enemy variety was a bit lackluster, which is a fault of the game being rather on the short side unfortunetly.  Sometimes it could also be difficult to figure out what you could and couldn't walk on leading to a fall, but I could've just needed my eyes checked I have no idea since it happened to me three times.
This game was meant more for a gamepad I feel, as the keyboard just feels rather awkward overall.  You can get used to it but never feels nearly as fluid as the controller with it's precise movement.
I have to admit, blowing something up with a mortar or whatnot brings a shimmer to my eye.  Everything in the game feels organic, leveling your character, using materials to upgrade your (very large) cache of weapons and equipping tonics to your character instead of armor to grant special quirks.  Again as stated earlier, due to the game being so short it's necessity you need to play through the New Game+ just to be able to upgrade everything and even unlock the rest of the achievements since you can't play through any areas except Proving Grounds or character related arenas.  The Proving Grounds force you to complete a task using the specific weapon for each area.  My main issue is the difficulty ratios for each of them are wildly different, and sometimes you cannot complete a proving ground until you fully upgrade said weapon which is a tad irritating.  God help the Machete Proving Ground and it's stupidity.  If the game ever feels too easy, you can also add in Deities or Gods onto your person which grants you an experience bonus but adds difficulty and let me tell you, the game can be impossibly ruthless with those settings on.  The main flaw I feel of the combat system is the targeting, as you automatically target the enemy closest to you, but if you wish to switch to another target, any enemy between it and them will have to be manually cycled through leading to massive headaches due to the frequency of tons of enemies being dumped on you.  This also coincides with your shield use as you have to be facing the target to be able to use it and is just best left to dodge and roll then to block.
At first I wasn't too enthusiastic about the music, but it has grown on me over time and I enjoy it.  Is it the best soundtrack ever? No particularly though there are some choice tracks in there that are worth listening too.  The voice acting is also done really well with the Narrator narrating everything from what weapons you equip to if you slip off a ledge and fall on your face.
A highly enjoyable game that is unfortunately really short, New Game+ or no.  Some small tweaks here or there and it could benefit greatly.  It also has some sort of 3rd mode of play which I never attempted involving some kinda scoreboard, which indeed this game does have leaderboards that surprises me but hey, why not right?

Street fighter V has had an... interesting run over the past year.  the game was first released far to early, had various bugs and crashes come and go, as well as moving to the controversial "Always online" style of game. and if 8 months ago you asked me if i would recomend the game, i would say hell no. If you look at other reviews, you'll see a lot of varied opinions. But what is most aperent is there was a lot of anger with this game. and much of it for the time had grounds to stand by.  Allow me to put it out there that im new to the street fighter series. I only discovered it within the past 12 or so months, but i liked the look of this one. So when this game first came out, I bought it within its first week of release. and saw a lot that♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off. Right off the back the game had missing content. there were buttons that if you pressed them all that happened was a window would pop up with the words "Coming soon!" and it just♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off so much i refunded it for its predesessor (Ultra street fighter IV).
I kept this grudge till maybe may or so, i dont actually remember when, but around when balrog/ibuki were intoduced to the game. It was on sale so i gave it a second chance. It was annoying i couldnt change my fighter ID after my previous perchace, but I kept with it. and i can now say that the game is actually pretty good.
The game is now at 100% completion with the exception of anual DLC characters/costumes/maps/whatever, and it plays pretty fantasticly. The gameplay moves fluidly, looks amazing, and feels the way (i think) Street fighter should. True there has been plenty of bumps on the way, but the final product to me is a good buy. Although if you are new to the street fighter series, i might recomend waiting for this game to be on sale. As of writing this review (12/23/16) Its on sale for about 20 dollars, which is more than a rational price.
To break it down to pros and cons:
Pros:
+The gameplay feels fantastic, and thats the main part of any fighting game
+Online play is pretty stable
+Cross platform play! that should be praised reguardless of a games quality
+Story mode, it may not be perfect but its still cool to see new and old characters in an actual story.
Mixxed:
~Not all the roster is availible at the start, you start with 16 of the (currently) 23 characters, and you have to purchase the others as dlc. However all characters can be attained though determination and enough gameplay, though its an uphill battle
~this game has had a plethora of bugs, though most were with menus, and eventually fixed. I dont recal there being any actual bugs with the combat at least.
~This game may give newcomers of the series a sour taste of street fighter. So while i enjoy the game, i feel this is a bad starting point for the series.
Cons:
-DLC costumes cost rediculous ammounts of money. Six dollars for one costume is pretty steep to me. and most costumes are only atainible with real world money. Thats really annoying.
-The game came out too early and im still bitter about that, it was a full price $60 early release game, and while its fixed now i hate when companys do this.
-Kens hair looks like bananas and juris theme is trash.

So TLDR, the game was released far to early, but is now a funtional and good game. Maybe buy it on sale, and its probably a bad idea to make this your first street fighter, start with USFIV and see if youd be willing to buy a version with crisper graphics and gameplay. Ive enjoyed the game even though i sort of suck (still bronze rank after ~200 hours) but i would be willing to say give the game a shot

This is NOT Sanctum 1. If you are going into this expecting it to be exactly like the first, then be forewarned that it is not. Also, in this review, I am including all DLC in my considerations, and I am including into consideration what this game has set out to be rather than what I personally expect from a TD or FPS game.
That having been said to appease the die hard purists of the original and the two genres, this game is on it's own merrit absolutely awesome. It has it's highs and lows like most any game, although there are a lot more highs than there are lows. There is a little bit of pacing and balance issues when it comes to playing straight through as you will inevitably hit a point where you are forced to improve not only your skill but also your choice of armaments or when certain armaments or combinations that are just completely overkill for the level you are facing. With sufficient skill and sufficient experience with the different combos, there is no reason you can't make almost any combination work, but getting to that skill point will take a bit of time and some trial and error that you just wont nail down on your first play through or until you've played enough to cap out you levels. On the higher difficulty levels though, that skill and knowing the combinations is critical and on the hardest difficulty for the most part you will need to bring your A game and the best combos you can muster. That is all part of what makes a good TD game though; possibilities and choices in how you play, replayability without getting stale fast, and the flexibility of different difficulties that includes something for the casual to the hardcore.
The FPS element does feel light, and the TD element does feel somewhat simplified when compared to their pure counterparts, but the state of both is perfect for the sake of trying to play both at once without getting overwhelmed as a new player and in order to prevent requiring days of number crunching or rote memorization of patterns. At some point though, you will beat everything and then it will boil down to just survival mode and how many waves can you kill before it's impossible. When you get to that point after playing for many many hours, it will inevitably get pretty dull for most.
All in all, just considering Sanctum 2 and only the scope of the game, I would give it a 80/85 in terms of what it set out to do and how well it delivers (points docked due to lack of really long term replayability for completionists, and minor pacing/balance issues). I would give it a 80/100 when comparing it against all other games I've ever played of all genres.

If I were to sum up Fran Bow I'd say it was one part Wizard of Oz and two parts Nightmare on Elm Street. Right from the start there's a lot of creepy, messed up things going on and it's not all Fran. The art style is exceptional in adding to the mystery and unsettling situation we find Fran in.
Let's talk about Fran for a moment. An 11 year old girl whose parents were killed and she now finds herself basically an orphan in an insane asylum for children. Yet Fran doesn't really exhibit the angsty, f - the world, brooding personality we would expect. Instead she looks at all things happening with a positive sort of naive response. See a bunch of dead fetus' in a well she's happy it took it's umbilical cord with it. Head explode right in front of her she speaks to the fresh corpse like it might respond any minute with some extra twitching. Maybe it's the massive amounts of drugs or just her not being mature enough to realize something is wrong that she is such a tragic character. And you really want to give her a happy ending with all the trials she seems to be going through it's just a lot at any age. However, you're going into this knowing that Fran probably isn't all there.
Around half way through the game starts blurring the lines between what might be real and what might be in Fran's head. The story alludes to there being multiple realities that we're experiencing but you are left questioning what's real. You can imagine early on how this will end but I really enjoyed getting  there. It's not all doom and gloom the entire way through but the story never alludes to you getting to a better place. Even when you finally reach your destination what you uncover isn't quite what you expect. The ending does leave a good amount of room for interpretation.
The puzzle aspect of the game was thoughtful and well designed. Nothing was too difficult to figure out and solutions utilized both of Fran's mental states to complete. There was a journal that you received sometime during your journey that also alluded to another character's perspective of a journey similar to Fran's. In addition to being a companion for a few of the game's puzzles I wish it could have played a bigger role. It wasn't useless as an inventory item but there was a time when I just completely neglected it as some random unimportant item.
In all this was a disturbing but well thought out game. There were some parts that felt a bit boring but nothing felt like it was a grind or filler for getting through the story. It's a heartbreaking and disturbing tale but well worth the price of admission.

I got this fairly cheap and it was worth the price. It's a great casual car crash game with a wide variety of vehicles and licensed music. It takes place in an open world that feels varied and has missions spread out over intersections. This is a nice idea although, like all the interface, it makes things harder than necessary. If you have one more mission of a certain type you want to do you may have to drive all the way to the other side of the map to get to it.
The game is a lot of fun when it indulges in what it does best: destruction. The road rage missions are ideal for the way things work as target cars spawn all around the player, regardless of direction or location (here the game is respecting the player's time). They're aggressive and flip magnificently when crashed. The physics aren't amazing- subtly is lost and brute force is the way to win- but cars deform nicely when hit and the destuction wrought when going the wrong way down a highway at speed with 5 other cars all trying to kill each other is impressive. Graphical fidelity isn't up to the standards of recent games but it's not bad at all and performance is excellent. If you get wrecked or crash you have several more tries before you get totaled and can repair at a garage- since there's no predefined route, there's really no problem there. Unfortunately the game becomes much less fun when the player advances because the later vehicles are ridiculously overpowered to the point where you pretty much have to match them by driving the same ones... and they just aren't responsive enough to enjoy. The end game is frustrating and boring.
The game falters in two basic ways. First, the entire user-interface is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Even accepting that the game was made for controllers in mind, it's awful and takes way too much time to find anything or switch settings, from game settings to changing vehicles in garages. There is no shortcut to quitting a race other than the hit\miss method of just stopping and hoping the game will realize you want to end the mission- and you have no option to restart so you get to retrace your route if you want to try the same race again. The stupid EA sign-in BS was so bad that I almost gave up on it (a steam friend I wanted to play with DID give up on it)- once again, EA screws the pooch for what should be simple steam functionality so they can try to pull people towards their little "services" that do nothing but serve EA.
The second problem with the game is the races. Much of what I loved about 'road rage' mode goes away when the game tries to have actual races instead of the arcadey modes. Driving physics are not up to the task, for one. Second, when you have to get from one point to another instead of just driving around crashing, things get much less fun. Assuming you don't have the large city\rural area memorized, you're going to have to be checking the map for most races -especially in the rural area where the roads are a mess. I don't even think there's a way to do that on a controller so I have to try and hit it on the keyboard while not crashing into a wall. Inexcusably there is no way to set waypoints for yourself!  I started aborting every long race- they're nothing but a chore.
So if you're looking for a casual destructive car game I definitely recommend it. I wasn't able to try multiplayer thanks to the poor multiplayer system but I had fun even in singleplayer.

Fran Bow, a girl who suffers from a mental disorder after her parents were brutally murdered by something unexplainable, tries to find out who/what did it and why it happened. With the help of her medicine she can see and solve puzzles that are otherwise invisible to humans.
Fran Bow is a truly horrifying experience and manages to be a frightening experience, even for a puzzle point N' click game. The game is eerie and the puzzles are not annoying and you are not forced to backtrack all the time (Unless you suck and need a walktrough, like I did). All the while the creepiest things are happening around you, but Fran is a girl who takes things light hearted, since she is used to it and has the ability to talk to these normally invisible beings that haunt the alternate dimension. The game lasts around 8-10 hours and somehow still does not feel that long, which is good because of the rapid change in scenery that keeps me occupied, and more progress = better game feel (Personal opinion).
The game does well in the "horror" part of the game. Although not outright scary, it still manages to give you a disgusted and frightened gut feeling. Not to mention the artstyle of this, those creatures are not a joke, man. If the point of this game is to portray extreme mental disorder of a child, I'm convinced, thank you, Killmonday Games, you are true blessing.
The only issues I ever encountered were a few glitches here and there, but none that were gamebreaking in any way.
10/10 - You'll find the truth when you're ready, Fran, you're brave and I respect bravery.

This pussified version of Doom 3 brightens the game world considerably, removes the flashlight mechanic, and doubles the amount of available ammo, turning it into a cake-walk. I breezed through it on Veteran difficulty. If you've never played it before I'd recommend the original instead. If you have played the original, well, it's still Doom 3-- lengthy campaign, fun combat, runs like a dream on modern systems and the new achievements make it worth another go-around.
Also included is the first expansion pack, Resurrection of Evil: a quality add-on, but also simplified in depressing ways. Certain areas have been removed for whatever reason, and you no longer need oxygen to traverse the toxic sections, completely removing the suspense. There's the Lost Missions, a brand new expansion exclusive to the BFG edition, which is essentially the "Blue Shift" of the two in which you play a surviving Alpha Squad marine attempting to shut down the portal. Highly recommended if you can't get enough Doom 3.
Then there's Doom 1 and 2. These are both legendary shooters that have been modified to run on modern computers without the need for source-ports like Zdoom or Boom. Unfortunately, that means they also lack a quicksave function, crosshairs, or the ability to jump. The aiming system is also a little off. I did appreciate the new variety of monster dialogue, a healthy combination of remixed growls and grunts. Doom is far from perfect-- sometimes it takes one shotgun blast to kill an Imp, but other times it takes two. The second two episodes feel thrown together and pale in comparison to Knee Deep in the Dead and the more recent Thy Flesh Consumed . Lastly, the invisio-sphere is still the most useless powerup in the history of FPS. It causes enemies to miss-- sometimes. If you like to strafe left and right like an OLDSCHOOL FPS PLAYER this means that nine times out of ten you will sidestep DIRECTLY INTO ENEMY FIRE.
Doom 2 is a tedious bore and I could never understand the appeal of it. The maps are giant mazes that lack any sort of context. I only ever used it to mod levels with the new enemies and Super Shotgun. This version, however, contains another brand-new episode, "No Rest For The Living," that is stellar and worth the full price alone.

Several missions in and I can say Im really happy so far. MERCs metagame plays essentially like Xcom - missions come and go as time goes by, mercs need to be healed of injuries, equipment must be bought and divvied up, new mercs hired and such.
The tactical gameplay revolves around your two man Alpha and Beta teams that make up your overall squad. You can give orders seperately to both teams, or control them together as a whole - currently, unless I completely missed it, there is no way to control a single merc. Tactical play is real time with a slow time mechanic for when things get hectic - it boils down to proper cover usage, squad abilities and not letting missiles hit you in the face...
My only real gripe right now is the use of left mouse for some things and right for other. Some cover requires RMB, some LMB. All targetting is LMB - but I instinctively want to use RMB for that and often end up sending my squad running at the enemy instead of gunning them down.
Overall, for my hours worth of play and 3-4 missions Ive been thru - Im really looking forward to more. Its got a great cyberpunk setting (Im a huge cyberpunk fan so this is a big deal for me) and the gameplay and logistics are already enough to be fun and engaging. This confusing d|ldo wizard mess starts with some surrealistic insomnia theme with shadows jumping you at every turn. Then there's some fade to black sections, waking up somewhere else, blah blah blah. They're going for some Deja Vu/madness/you're a sentient being or android or whatever scheme. Which could have been okay, if this was a movie. However it doesn't work at all as a GAME.
You see, I actually played until one of the "endings", turning out to be a grotesque "Misery" equivalent. The pixellated gore I couldn't care less about; the problem is, I as a player, have absolutely no idea what I did right, wrong, or what I could have done differently. And I'm sure this is as it should be, according to the latest hipster game-dev bushido code.
Obviously, the goal of the game is to confuse you. However, taking away control and not giving the player any clear goals - you know, in a GAME - breaks all the rules of what a GAME should be. There's a difference between books, movies and games, and the difference is there for a reason. Breaking rules and inventing new stuff is great when the chef discovers that potatoes tastes great when fried - it isn't so great when he takes a dump on the guests plate and expect them to enjoy the "edgy invention".
As such, serving this game to people is akin to welcoming aliens to the planet by inviting them to a game of cricket - not explaining the rules to them while fully expecting them to have a good time. Just tell them "now you lost a point" and "now you did great, maybe", but don't let them now exactly what they did well or not. As an alien I think I would have just nuked the planet from orbit after that.
Adding to that, these are all some glaring problems that need fixing:
- Game freezing when entering and exiting closet at subway too quickly. Had to exit the game and restart.
- Controls are bad. When using a controller, you can only use the D-pad to move, but have to change to the stick to navigate your inventory.
- Game doesn't work with the Steam overlay F12 button to take screenshots.
- Menus only show keyboard button presses for action, not controller inputs.
And that's why this is a non-recommended from me.

Doom 3.
While a rather large departure from the series style, it's still a game I have always enjoyed. Pre-ordering it back in 2004 and being so excited to load it up the day it released.
I love the change in style. The slower pace, the horror themed to the hell invasion. Doom 3 always will be one of my favorite games.
But, the BFG Edition... how does it stand?
Well, in contains not only Doom 3, but it's official expansion Resurrection of Evil, and the new add-on the Lost Mission. And it also contains the Ultimate Doom and Doom II: Hell on Earth. That alone makes it a great package.
Doom 3 and RoE are just as great as they were before. But, small changes stand out that make this release not as great as the original.
For both D3 and RoE they've adjusted the lighting, making the games brighter. Which, while addressing some complaints, actually takes away from the game's original atmosphere.
Also, they've increased the amount of ammo present in the game world. The original releases already featured way too much ammo. You can have almost 200 shotgun shells by the end of the second level in Doom 3.
That combined with the fact that they've actually reduced the number of enemies in certain encounters, and made a few of the boss fights easier... what was already a pretty easy game has been turned into a cakewalk.
And, the Lost Mission... is awful. A cobbled together campaign made up of bits and pieces of levels from Doom 3 and RoE. It lacks the originality of the original releases, and the feel of polish and fun. A nice addition, but, ultimately... a wasted effort.
The BFG Edition is worth the price to have the entire Doom series in one title, but, if you already own the original releases... you've already got the better versions.

I hate DOOM 3.  It falls flat on its face as a DOOM game and it's also unable to deliver a decent shooter experience, let alone a decent horror experience. I guess.
Open a door.
Pick up a weapon.
Breathe.
At best, DOOM 3 is a below average-quality corridor shooter.  At worst, it's one of the most boring games I've ever played.  If you're thinking about getting the BFG Edition so you can be able to play a remastered version of this game alongside the two original DOOMs, don't bother. I've played the original DOS version and this new version - Refine.
What I liked about Refine:
+ New Japanese voiceovers.
+ The music sounds much better.
+ New text makes it easier to understand some of the courses/work easier. I first played this game as a child and had a difficult time understanding the terminology in the DOS version. As a result, a child may have an easier time understanding this.
+ The Art is less grainy and more refined; somewhat brighter. The flowers in the vase change by the season – which I thought was a nice touch.
+ 'Olive/Daughter' feels less sexualized in this version.
+ I liked that I could talk to my Daughter multiples times about various things. In the old version it greyed out after one conversation.
UPDATE 2nd play through:
+ The People with bounty on their heads were easier to find this time. In the old version I had to approach the same building multiple times in order to prompt the event.
What I disliked about Refine:
- I'm not sure it was necessary to change the main art for 'Olive/Daughter' in the main gameplay screen. It's not that I dislike the new art, but it felt out of place with the older art. The poses were also different which I don't know if I cared for. The Red Dress seemed rushed compared to the original.
- When I completed the game and had reached the results the DOS version had a letter that your Daughter had written about how she was raised. Refine has a new image with new art of Olive/Daughter and she was speaking in Japanese with no text. Which I believe is just a bug or oversight currently.
- I feel like the new art was made to portray her more as a Daughter and not a potential lover; which is for the better really. However, in the Vacation scenes she is still naked in various scenes and poses. If the art was updated why wasn't that updated as well? She also talks about her bust and butt too from time to time when you talk to her. In the old version she would ask: "Do you think my figure is okay?" from time to time instead of her butt.
- The font that was chosen for the text is not as nice as it was for the old version. It feels cheaper.
- The cheats were taken away. I personally prefer to play without the cheats but sometimes it's nice to mess around. I can understand omitting naked Olive/Daughter.
- The voice overs were repetitive. The P/T pawn shop girl Wendy shouts at you when speaking and it is unpleasant.
- I feel like this could have been an opportunity to add something new to the game play; such as a new course, job, new items. or adventuring area(s) - based on 2 full play thrroughs.
UPDATE 2nd play through:
- (BUG) Your Daughter's Faith reduced to 0 when you took off armor.
- (BUG) The Clown achievement unlocked when I was meant to obtain the perfect hunting achievement.
- The Adverturing areas were still slow moving when moving your Daughter as Day turned into night and back.
Overall, I think this game needs a few fixes but I am very excited and would like to try different routes.

I've previously played the DOS version of this game and liked it a lot. This version has non-pixelated art which, although not as charming as the original's, is pretty nice. The game also gives you a choice to use the original MIDI or WAV, and there's Japanese voice acting as well.
For people who've never played this before, it's basically a scheduling game. You select what your daughter does from month to month: Certain activities build up certain stats, which make certain endings possible, and the fun lies in finding out how your actions play out. There are also brief interludes with simple JRPG-style combat and exploration.
While I'm happy that the game is on Steam, the English translation is painfully sloppy. The introductory movie is full of substandard English, and the game itself is full of typos: Amourer instead of armourer, for example.
Typos don't prevent people from playing the game, but because Princess Maker 2 relies on the quality and charm of its writing, I urge CFK to do the right thing and improve the translation in a patch. As it stands, the typos make the game look like a quick and dirty port, which does CFK's reputation no favors.
Edit: Now that I've played a game through, I can see that there's another serious fault. In the DOS version, your daughter would write you a letter when she became an adult, either thanking you or criticizing you for your parenting. In the Steam version, she reads that letter aloud in Japanese, but there's no English text. If you don't speak Japanese, then, you're out of luck as far as understanding what she's saying. This means that what was a touching moment in the DOS version is now just going to leave a lot of English-speaking players confused. This absolutely needs to be fixed in a patch.

So the return of nostalgia. This is a cult favorite child raising simulator.
You are a sword man who defeated the demon leading an army to destroy the kingdom. Soon after that you encounter a goddess who tell you to raise the girl as your own daughter. From there you will choose how she dress, whats her diet, what she study, and what she do as a job. The game have a lot of little detail that are nice to see, such as if her diet is poor then she will have harder time work jobs that take more stamina. Or if she go to the beach for vacation, then she'll come back with a tan. You have 8 years to raise the girl (she's 10 when the game start) into a young lady. Really there a lot to do in this game and it will require many playthroughs to see many of the different endings and events of the game.
My one con to this game is that it doesn't really give you a tutorial or hints to let you know which jobs raise/lower what stats before you do it. So your first couple playthroughs will most likely be fumbling around to see what cause what effect, or what the best way to handle a problem (such as the daughter getting sick or becoming a delinquent). Heck it took me a while to figure out why everyone kept dodging my daughter attacks while she was in combat (yea you can send your daughter adventuring out and fighting monsters).
All in all, this is a child raising sim with an addictive play style to it. Be prepared to lose hours trying to raise your daughter into becoming something great like a princess or queen.

I got this fairly cheap and it was worth the price. It's a great casual car crash game with a wide variety of vehicles and licensed music. It takes place in an open world that feels varied and has missions spread out over intersections. This is a nice idea although, like all the interface, it makes things harder than necessary. If you have one more mission of a certain type you want to do you may have to drive all the way to the other side of the map to get to it.
The game is a lot of fun when it indulges in what it does best: destruction. The road rage missions are ideal for the way things work as target cars spawn all around the player, regardless of direction or location (here the game is respecting the player's time). They're aggressive and flip magnificently when crashed. The physics aren't amazing- subtly is lost and brute force is the way to win- but cars deform nicely when hit and the destuction wrought when going the wrong way down a highway at speed with 5 other cars all trying to kill each other is impressive. Graphical fidelity isn't up to the standards of recent games but it's not bad at all and performance is excellent. If you get wrecked or crash you have several more tries before you get totaled and can repair at a garage- since there's no predefined route, there's really no problem there. Unfortunately the game becomes much less fun when the player advances because the later vehicles are ridiculously overpowered to the point where you pretty much have to match them by driving the same ones... and they just aren't responsive enough to enjoy. The end game is frustrating and boring.
The game falters in two basic ways. First, the entire user-interface is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Even accepting that the game was made for controllers in mind, it's awful and takes way too much time to find anything or switch settings, from game settings to changing vehicles in garages. There is no shortcut to quitting a race other than the hit\miss method of just stopping and hoping the game will realize you want to end the mission- and you have no option to restart so you get to retrace your route if you want to try the same race again. The stupid EA sign-in BS was so bad that I almost gave up on it (a steam friend I wanted to play with DID give up on it)- once again, EA screws the pooch for what should be simple steam functionality so they can try to pull people towards their little "services" that do nothing but serve EA.
The second problem with the game is the races. Much of what I loved about 'road rage' mode goes away when the game tries to have actual races instead of the arcadey modes. Driving physics are not up to the task, for one. Second, when you have to get from one point to another instead of just driving around crashing, things get much less fun. Assuming you don't have the large city\rural area memorized, you're going to have to be checking the map for most races -especially in the rural area where the roads are a mess. I don't even think there's a way to do that on a controller so I have to try and hit it on the keyboard while not crashing into a wall. Inexcusably there is no way to set waypoints for yourself!  I started aborting every long race- they're nothing but a chore.
So if you're looking for a casual destructive car game I definitely recommend it. I wasn't able to try multiplayer thanks to the poor multiplayer system but I had fun even in singleplayer.

It's hard to describe Fran Bow.  It's disturbing, beautiful, heart-felt . . .  It's kind of like if you took Undertale, gave it a terrific art style, and made it gruesome (and took out all the passivist BS and "RPG" style).
You really get connected to Fran and Mr. Midnight (yes, you connect with a cat) and the many creatures they interact with on the way.  It's a disturbing and touching story.
The puzzles are for the most part, right in that sweet spot where you don't need a walkthrough, but hard enough you feel really smart when you solve them.  There are a few that are unintuitive, but I only needed a walkthrough maybe 3 times and even then, "need" is a strong word (impatient is probably more accurate).
It can mostly be paralleled with American McGee's Alice as far as atmosphere (which, funny enough there's one point where Fran is looking in her closet and there is a picture and she says "that's me and my best friend Alice!", so you know they got some of their inspiration from the book/movie/video game).
I highly recommend this game.  It was a terrific adventure which I was happy to play through twice, will probably play again at some point.
There's something ridiculously satisfying about a game with good physics, and despite being bare bones, this game is ridiculously satisfying.

An interesting game: It could be described as a mix between Max Payne and Devil May Cry. A third-person action game in which the gameplay constantly shifts focus between melee and ranged combat, though you're usually free to employ both (the effectiveness of "mixing it up" will, of course, vary with the nature of the engagement) as you see fit.
At first, the game makes it look like its melee combat will be highly nuanced, as if subtle negotiation of space and exquisite knowledge of enemy patterns will be required, but this illusion quickly falls apart. As you get acquainted with the game's systems you will learn that you can, for example, safely mash the action key whenever you're near an enemy, even as you hold block, and easily perform the contextual throw counter (which often allows for an easy instant kill on downed enemies) without ever really reacting to the prompt shown by the game (or to the enemy's movements at all). The game has, nonetheless, some memorable action set pieces, and some rather good boss battles (even if most of them involve QTEs at some point).
You begin the game with four main combos, one for each primary movement direction, and as you advance through the story you learn "super combos", which are enhanced versions of the regular directional combos. These are activated by timing the third hit of a combo correctly. These are much superior to regular combos as they have greatly enhanced damage output and often perform knockdowns - so after you acquire these, you will end up pretty much only using the old, "non-super" combos by accident. The very last super combo you learn, "dragon tail", deals so much damage and covers such a large area that there's almost no reason not to exclusively stick to it for close combat. As the game progresses, you also end up acquiring four different special skills called "energy blows", which can aid you in combat or in solving the game's simple environmental puzzles.
Regarding the plot, Collapse has quite a bit of radio chatter, including calls you can make to learn about the game's story and setting. On this detail: It has a "secret" (it is not actually hidden since you can see the missing call log after the point of no return - You can then simply revert to an older autosave if you so wish) fork in the story which involves making a radio call at a specific point late into the game. All it appeared to change was that a specific character did not die in a cutscene right after this "secret call" becomes available - The ending of the game seemed to remain the same. Speaking of the game's ending, there are some rather aggravating jumping puzzles to be found in the latter sixth of the game or so.
The framerate would sometimes inexplicably plummet despite my machine far exceeding the recommended system requirements. I had around five crashes total (Windows 7). The last two pieces of information (files you can find scattered about the levels which contain details on the game's plot and world) were apparently bugged - they were completely blank to me. I will cautiously recommend Collapse: There is some undeniable jank to it and its presentation (it does NOT look like a game released in 2008), but there are also more than a few positive aspects to it. In the end it is mostly a well-paced experience that was an obvious labor of love, even if it ends up coming off as more than a little derivative.

Well-designed authentic post-soviet cityscapes take turns with futuristic sci-fi environments which look unique enough to avoid inducing tedium of revisiting an overused theme.
Skies are done so well - they deserve a separate mention. Especially the one at chapter 3: that's the most beautiful sky I've ever seen.
Layouts of levels are done skillfully to take as much playtime as possible from each location without protracting it.
Checkpoint placement is done perfectly. You get a checkpoint after every fight and after every hard jump, so you will never find yourself in need to replay parts of the game due to save points being too far from each other.
The battle system will look odd and clumsy until you take some time to get used to it. When you do, it becomes pretty fun and similar to Painkiller: bunny-hop, fast movement.
Additional challenge comes from enabled friendly fire. Unlike many other games here you can hurt friendly NPC who help you, but don't worry: it is balanced out by their quickly regenerating health.
Swordfighting part seem lackluster: first your health drops faster than enemies' then you learn standard routine: use strong combo to knock down an enemy, then finish him before he stands up. Don't expect to find depth and variety here. There are many moves to use, but it seems like only difference between them is animation.
QTE during boss fights also don't seem like a good idea: they make you too concentrated on pressing keys to enjoy animations and camera movements.
Following the story is interesting. Characters are charismatic. Writing style and voice acting are done exceptionally well.
Strong atmosphere, originality and variety of the environments, great writing style and acting, soundtrack and combat similar to Painkiller will keep you immersed in the world of Collapse and eager to keep going farther, wondering about what will happen next. It's a huge pleasure to explore beautiful locations and solve challenging puzzles. Do not miss this game, because it is just what you need.

Hell is your playground.
Some kids had Disney princesses, some had hot wheels and the like... I had Doom. I remember playing this glorious nonsensical fun before I could even walk properly. It was one of the first games I ever played as a kid and it was one never to be forgotten. I had spent hours playing this throughout my childhood and watching it 'mature'. Doom was one of the first main milestones for the game industry, one that so many old time gamers remember with glee.
Not to sound like one of those typical old time gamers who do nothing but bash new shooters and such, but Doom really set the bar for the completely outrageous games that we came to enjoy so much. They made you feel smart and really made you think to find all those secrets or even just to complete the levels because they were so well designed. It's why so many people still go back to it and disregard the newer games as they seem to have brought a little too much realism into the mix.
Where the first and second Doom had the iconic enemies, soundtracks and weapons, the new ones fail to bring out those unique characteristics about it. The enemies don't look anything like their aged counterparts, the weapons don't feel or look as satisfying, it looks like just another generic FPS shooter and that makes me sad. Though I don't completely trash new games, quite frankly it's remarkable that we have come so far in so many ways but I wish the things that made Doom 1&2 so unique were put to used more often. The main games that come to mind that have some of the crazy, senseless fun was Postal 2 and Saints Row 4.
Now don't get me wrong, it's not to say I don't love and enjoy -serious- games, quite the opposite, I just miss games like this. There really isn't anything more that can be said on this that has not been said before.

Absolutely do not listen to the few low reviews of this game that say it doesn't have a story or misogynizes women.   Or, you know, do; you have free will.
However; this fighting game is one of the best I've ever played; on par with Soul Caliber and Virtua Fighter.  It is the best of the MK series that I have seen, and I've seen them all.
Misogynistic?  Any game in which a woman can eviscerate a man and rip him asunder, limb from limb, seems fairly pro-suffragist to me.  Do they show too much breast?  Maybe, but they show a lot of Liu Kang's chest.  You never hear people call that sexist; objectifying the man.  So, if the test of universality fails, I think you can pretty safely disregard the 'sexist' slur.
As for having no story, have these reviewers every played Tekken?  Maybe Virtua Fighter?  Soul Caliber?  Most fighters have absolutely no attempt to even try to have a story.  Mortal Kombat, out of all fighting games, seems to stand brightest in its mythology and background.
Is it a deep story?  No.  Is it cliche?  A bit.  Is it there, do they try, do they give it a unique flavor?  Yes, yes, and yes!
In short, buy this game if you like fighters with blood, gore, violence, and sexy people; man and woman.

I felt a need to write this review because some of the other reviews almost convinced me not to buy this game. This is not me saying those reviews are wrong because I think a lot of those people have been playing this game for years so they know what they are talking about. However, I don't have years of experience (and disappointment) with this game. I didn’t play it when it focused more on survival, and I have no clue what the developers have changed and removed over the years. If I did know all of that stuff, I might not like the game either. However,  I bought this because I love Terraria and I wanted to play something similar, and this game more than fulfilled that need.
This is not a Terraria clone. In fact, it seems like they tried hard not to copy too many things from terraria. Sure it focuses on building, mining, and combat, but this is no more a copy of Terraria than Terraria is a copy of Minecraft.
The gameplay was familiar enough that I wasn't too overwhelmed, and the more I play the more I realize how much content this game has. I could spend hours on one planet alone and not even scratch the surface of what it has to offer, but there are also plenty of missions that give me a feeling of progress and help point me in the right direction.
I love the way cooking and farming have been implemented, the scenery is beautiful, and this game truly feels like something I will be playing for years.
If I had one complaint, it would be that there is almost too much going on. I find that I have to force myself to focus on one task at a time and not get distracted, but that  means I always have the feeling that I am missing something. There isn’t quite enough information given within the game, and since it has changed so much over the years it’s hard to find information online that is valid for current gameplay. Hopefully once 1.0 is released, it will be easier to find valid information.
If you like Terraria, you need to give this one a try. Don't let the negative reviews scare you away like I almost did. Like I said, I’m sure those people know what they are talking about, but I honestly think this game is well worth the fifteen bucks. I have played games that cost much more and they didn't come close to having this much content and enjoyment.

One of the lucky; few apparently immune to the sickness, you, unfortunately, are also trapped in a city crawling with thousands of the bloodthirsty Infected. Together with a handful of fellow Survivors, you must fight your way to safety or die alone. Thanks to a brilliant marriage of gameplay mechanics with cinematic genre, L4D creates genuine fright while not only enabling, but forcing cooperation between four players fighting for their survival. It has everything i want in a survival game exciting and realism; i rate this game Top and will recommend it to anyone who is in to FPS survival games.
There are games you want everyone to play, just so they can experience what i've such a good time with, and Left 4 Dead is one of them. It's unlike any other game I've ever played and demonstrates the true power of cooperative gameplay.

The game looks good both technically and aesthetically but the levels are linear, feel small and and despite vertical movement abilities for the Xenomorph and Predator, the action still happens mostly on level ground. At the very least the human campaign has you actually fighting the xenos more often than other humans/androids this time around.
The combat can become formulaic, almost flowchart like, especially for the Xeno and Predator who rely on melee combat and constant lengthy takedown animations. The weapons apart from the sniper rifle stay true to AvP canon but in doing so are few and uninspired.
The story doesn't even try to bring anything new to the table and all the races lack any clear goal or motivation beyond "move to the next area and kill everything that moves".
Again, it's not really broken in any way but I still can't recommend it to even the hardest of Aliens versus Predator fans.

How Northgard is different from other strategy games:
Northgard has incredible visual charm and features slower-paced strategical gameplay, which prioritizes anticipating and planning ahead compared to typical realtime-strategy-games, in which you are usually only competitive if you maange memorize build queues and are able to perform lots of "actions-per-minute" (basically clicking fast is mandatory to win those other games). Northgard games are very different because they advance at a very chill pace, which doesn't get boring because you're constantly thinking about how to adapt your strategy to what you are seeing. Read more about it below [...]
Northgard basically made me realize how much other real-time-strategy games stress the hell out of me during the entire ride, while a Northgard game typically slowly but steadily builds towards a peak at the end and gets more and more intense as you bring about the game's end or try to deny your opponents victory.
Gameplay in a nutshell:
Northgard is about slowly exploring a randomly generated map and learning how to "read" that map and its unique opportunities as well as challenges well. You need to combine the strenghts of your unique clan and research your technology-tree based on your map-circumstances in order to eek out a living, survive harsh winters and eventually colonize and win the map by several economic-ish victory conditions or simple conquest. A match typically lasts around 40 minutes.
Multiplayer:
With the recent multiplayer update micro-managing combat units has become a lot more fun and enjoyable, new unit types were added and the balance as well as the flow of the game have already vastly improved. There are a lot of multiplayer options to choose from - toggle any victory conditions and play team maps in a 2vs2vs2 or 3vs3 format. You can also switch in AI's. While the AI is not super-strong yet, it is fairly competent when playing on hard and managed to surprise me. It even seems the AI coordinate their attacks if two AI's are in a team.
Summary:
I'm super happy with my purchase and I can recommend it to any fan of strategy games. I'm looking forward to experience an entertaining campaign mode, while the multiplayer keeps getting balanced along the way. Northgard already offers really great value for its very moderate pricetag, so make sure to pick it up now in Early Access before the price is raised. Moreover, the developers are very receptive to intelligent feedback from the community and are quick to incorporate suggested changes and thus I have a very good impression of Shiro Games and they should be supported!

If you're looking to get into the Street Fighter franchise, or any 2D fighter, this is the game for you.
The gameplay is absolutely solid, it's easy to pick up and even the more experienced players have room to improve. There's a diverse cast of characters that play and look differently so everyone can find a character they like.
Positive:
1. The game runs smooth as butter on a decent machine. No dips in performance.
2. Easy to learn basics and hard to become a master of a character.
3. A training mode full of features designed specifically for it. Everyone can simulate different scenarios to get better.
4. Smooth online play 99% of the time and an active community.
5. Crossplay between PC and PS4.
6. Rich cast of characters with more to be added in 2017.
7. Awesome soundtracks.
Negatives:
1. Long loading times (performace may vary on different machines, but it's slow nonetheless)
2. No option to sort players in online lobbies based on their region.
3. Few single-player modes.
4. Kinda overpriced DLC costumes.
5. Low in-game money gains to make you purchase costumes/alternate colors/stages with real money.
Despite the above flaws, this game is worth it for every Street Fighter fan, for every 2D Fighting fan and for everyone new to fighting games in general.

I played this back in 2014-ish and at the time this game was fun for a few hours then eventually got stale afterwards. So, after 3 years has this game improved? I can't tell much of a difference between 2014 and now, the game is still fun and I really enjoy the base game...But there just isn't much to it other than the combat and guilds. No expansions, no new classes from what I can tell, no further RPG depth added to it. It's basically the same bullet hell MMO I played back in 2014.
Oh, and everything costs real money. This might have already been a thing and I just don't remember, but it's still a lazy business model regardless. The game appears to have been bought out by a company named Kabam. Here is what I have gathered from my search:
Kabam (formerly Watercooler, Inc.) is an interactive entertainment company founded in 2006 and headquartered in San Francisco, CA. with offices in Beijing, Vancouver, Los Angeles, and Austin, Texas. The company creates, develops and publishes massively multiplayer social games (MMSG’s) such as Kingdoms of Camelot, Star Wars: Uprising and Marvel: Contest of Champions for mobile devices. Before expanding into gaming, Kabam established itself as a social applications developer with entertainment and sports communities totaling more than 60 million users. Kabam markets freemium games for mobile devices, and social networking services,. The company's investors include Alibaba, Canaan Partners, Google, MGM, Intel, Pinnacle Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Warner Bros. and others.
The company has focused on developing "real games," or games with immersive gameplay mechanics akin to more traditional MMOs with an emphasis on the spending and gambling of virtual currency. In late 2009, Kabam launched Kingdoms of Camelot, one of the first successful strategy games on Facebook, but in June 2010, the number of players began constantly shrinking.[1]
As of April 2015, Kabam has announced a shift in its focus to developing AAA mobile games.[2]
Source:
The information above should give you a good idea who you are dealing with if you plan to shell out cash.
And yes, you can unlock classes for free, and I honestly don't mind how the current class unlock system works. You level your starting character to 20 which will then give you access to the next class. You can continue with the current starting class and gain fame, or kill him/her off to get access to the character you just unlocked. Now that right there is what I have a problem with. You cannot keep your character, you either have to buy a new slot with money or kill them off (they deleted my maxed out wizard when I got back, the only thing I had left was my level 8 Warrior). 2 slots to start off with I think would have been reasonable, but after seeing the terrible business model here and Kabam's history, these give off the impression of a very desperate company. Which could spell out the doom for Realm of the Mad God.
TL;DR: Other than the ignorant company behind this game, there really isn't much to talk about. RMG is a very generic free to play game that's fun with friends for a couple days and will run on a potato without any problems. However the servers are crap so be prepared to die a lot more to lag than the monsters you are fighting. My verdict? 6/10. It has something you could definitely build on but due to the nature of the situation this game is currently in I doubt you will see much in the way of future content.

I love this game. That's most likely the best way to describe it. Yeah... I guess
Fran Bow is a psychological-Horror Point-n-Click games by Killmonday somtime in August 2015. The story is about the little Girl Fran Bow (guess how the game got it's name :3) which is kept in an Insane-Asylum for she "witnessed" the killing of her parents. The plot follows Frans way to find out why her parents were killed and to find a save haven where she can "live on". To get there though she needs to flee the asylum and find the way to her last relative: Her Aunt Grace.
The pure plot might not seem that interesting to some players (though it's a fricking insane-asylum love it god dangit xD) but the gameplay parts and especially the art design overshadow this more or less standard plot start (In Chapter 3 the story really starts to "kick in").
The Gameplay is your standard Point-n-Click formular (klick on stuff, text, klick on more stuff, get some items, klick on even more stuff, funny commentaries, use item on stuff, profit!), some Mini-games here and there and the personal twist from the Developers: a way to "travel through twisted realities"/
.
This last part of the gameplay is most likely the best part gameplay-wise in the game. It binds the gameplay to the story, which should be always a given though is found in it's best way in the Indie-Community.
The Mini-Games are mostly easy to control and aren't that much of a nuissance (+ they're skippable) though in the last Mini-Game [end of Chapter 3] the collision and jumping feels kinda odd. Nothing really game changing though.
And now to the part which really surprised me in Fran Bow: The music.
Im a huge sucker for slow, dark, melancholic music. In fact if anyone loves this kind of music hes BOUND to get the soundtrack for this game. Mostly all of the songs are beautiful in their own way and while I personally don't like to hear the Mini-Game-BGMs I totally adore the song "Driving", which is played for I think 3 times through the whole game but hit me hard. In my opinion it's by far the best track on the OST.
Well I guess that's everything I could say about the game without spoilers (and even that didn't work 100% :/ )...
The best parts of this game can only be explained through spoiling crucial parts for the story which in my opinion would ruin the game.
I highly recommend to check Fran Bow out even when the genre might be completly out of the way for some.
The story though at the beginning a bit cliché is one of the best I've seen (in games at least) and the more or less endless ways of interpretation are constructed in a genius way.
I kinda feel like this game should have gotten a bit more exposure though it might've been overshadowed by the overexposed games last year.
So at last I would say that Genre-lovers can savely spend the 20 Bucks for Game and OST while others should test the Demo first and make out for themselves if they want to buy it at full price or on a sale!

Uncanny Valley, a retro-graphics styled 2D horror game developed by Cowardly Creations, presents itself as a return to the atmospheric horror of yesteryear when a third-person action wasn't the name of the game. This is a mouth-watering promise for those of us who miss the foggy streets of the first Silent Hill, or the ominous, blocky terror that was the original Alone in the Dark. But, as many reboots and sequels have proved (I'm looking at you, Resident Evil 6,) that's a really hard itch to scratch, and I'm happy to say that Uncanny Valley succeeds where many have failed.
Making a truly unnerving horror game requires several things: an engagingly spooky story, well-paced exploration, and an insurmountable terror threatening to catch you unprepared. UV has each of these ingredients, though there are some potential caveats depending on your play-style preferences:
Pros:
+ Gorgeous art direction and animations
+ Intriguing stories and decent writing
+ Multiple playthroughs are actually worth it
+That old-school survival horror revived!
Cons:
- Some graphical bugs could us squashing
- Inventory system is a bit cumbersome

I have been a long time fan of the Fallout franchise. From the first time I saw the Fallout 3 box on the shelves at Gamestop, I knew this series was special. Then after spending many days at school talking with friends about lore, and afternoons into the late night playing the game, I discovered Fallout New Vegas. Many people in the Fallout community say that NV is the greatest in the series, and while they have a valid point, I still prefer 4, and heres why.
Fallout 4 does something that no other game in the series does, and that is allow the player to, albeit breif, experience life in pre war America. Fallout 4 also introduces voice acting for the main character. This element is highly criticized as taking the 'voice' away from the player, which is completley wrong. As the character, you still have dialog options, and you can still decide which factions to join and / or ally with as well. All the other main characteristics of the series are present as well.
This has been a brief review, and I didn't cover the entire game, as I am pressed for time. But all in all it's a great game with a great story and a one of a kind world and atmosphere. So please give it a shot and you won't regret it.

In Aliens VS Predator you are able to play three different Stories as three different species, the Humans, the Aliens and the Predator. It took me not much more than 3 hours to finish each of their own stories on the Normal difficulty without looking for every collectible the game has to offer. Considering it’s a game from 2010 I was really satisfied with the visuals. The forests look dense and the water looks crystal clear. Light and shadow look good considering it’s been awhile since the game was released. If you are an Alien movie fan from the very first movie when it was released in 1979 by Ridley Scott then you may find more enjoyment in Aliens VS Predator then, say, in Aliens: Colonial Marines.
The Marine Story was the first one I experienced and among your typical FPS shooting action and objectives, I managed to find some tense moments where light could be as useful as bullets. Setting a proper mood when playing can improve your experience quite a bit so a darker room with some sort of surround headphones can be a big changer. Some of the weapons were accurate when portraying the sound from the original movies, yet, there were many times I felt overpowered against such terrifying enemy.
The predator Story was my favorite from the three. Right from the start, as predator, you will have to proof you are worth to join the most elite soldiers. Hunting and stealth tactics will be your best weapon. Divide to conquer is the best strategy one can find while trying to get your precious human trophies. Some may find an extreme satisfaction by taking their time to caught the enemies by surprise while finishing them off with a decapitation while others may prefer a more direct, ruthless approach. It’s up to you how you play, just remember that it’s a good idea to adapt as you play different species.
Playing the Alien story was the most hard for me. While it took me some time to get used to the controls by climbing the ceiling, walls and so on these missions gave me some harsh motion sickness, turning the experience really different and less enjoyable from the other two. After (if) you get used to the fast walking and crawling between walls, floors and ceilings you will feel the horror is about to arrive to those poor Marines. Waiting and stalking the prey when they less expect feels amazing and I found myself to avoid killing all the soldiers if it was not required. The notion of panic from the Marine soldiers is well noted and if you are spotted they will try to find you and terminate you, hence why it makes such a difference to wait in order to deal the final blow to the enemy.
In the end I had great fun with the game and I still believe it holds up in this time and day. If you are an Alien or Predator fan I’m sure you already played this game, if not, I think it deserves a good chance, for the right price. The Online portion of the game may be absent considering nobody still plays by now but either way the three different campaigns remains a solid experience that may be worth your attention and also your time.

Reminds me tremendously of Offworld Trading Company in that it is unique among RTS titles (more ways to win than just destroy all of your opponents) and you need to either balance your victory approach (and risk being beaten in a particular area because someone got to that condition first) or specialize going for something and risk being beaten because someone countered your approach... when this is balanced you have a really engaging RTS game.  Northgard promises just that.  Simpler gameplay than the Endless series and choices seem as meaningful without being diluted. Edit:  there is some keybinding implemented so far (you can ctrl-bind buildings, single units or groups to number keys, hugely helpful) and there are multiple military units (just not finished- but you can recruit 3 types as of now: a well-rounded ax warrior, a tankier shield guy and an ax-throwing dps)- so these are now pros not cons
