I saved the path with
for last, which I think was the wise move - she's a better choice to end the game with, I think.
There were interesting treatments of asexuality, which kind of hit me out of the blue, as well as familial death and mourning, parental abandonment, anti-LGBT bullying, and other issues that often get glossed over in dating sims. This is definitely for mature audiences, even if the art is suggestive rather than explicit.
The art is actually something I need to single out for criticism. The girls had few facial expressions, although I understand that expressions can be expensive. The biggest problem with the art, I think, is that two of the characters are drawn with chests that are not just large (plenty of busty women out there), but *grotesque* - at least in some scenes. I actually burst out laughing the first time I saw the main character; those things just didn't fit.
That said, this is a charming story with some interesting characters, and even though I got the game discounted, I think it's definitely worth the modest asking price. I look forward to the next project out of this tiny studio.

TL;DR Fantastic value on par with the orange box, will keep you busy for 30-40 hours. Doom 3 and its expansions can grow repetitive, but Doom 1-2 are still among my favorite classic first person shooters. 9/10
The Doom 3 BFG edition includes all the main games in the series as well as their respective expansion packs, it is essentially everything you could want from a Doom package. The lack of total support for mods is a little confusing, but there are ways to get most of the mods working within the game. Since this package includes the three different Doom games I will break them down by game.
The original that started it all, still very fun, but obviously shows its age and lives the shadow of its superior sequel. The secrets are still very fun to find with the creative level design and the game was practically built for speed running. Once again, the environments, weapons, and enemies all fall behind the sequel. Both Doom 1 and Doom 2 feature one of the best soundtracks in gaming, with 8-bit renditions of classic metal songs ranging from slayer to megadeth. 8.5/10
I love this game! Classic gaming at its best here, so many classic levels and weapons. The levels sprawl in comparison to the first game, sometime almost becoming too maze like if you are not familiar with their layout. I found the middle section of the game to be my favorite as the last few hell levels can get lengthy and confusing. The level design is a very minor complaint as "lengthy" for a doom level is only about 10 minutes. Definitely the best game in the pack. 9/10
This game was pretty controversial when it came out as some absolutely loved it while others felt it to be extremely repititive. I fall somewhere in the middle as I believe the game has its moments of awesomeness, but features now where near the varied levels of the second one; the space base environment really does grow old. The moments you spend in hell, which I believe the coolest environment in the game, is far too short. This is especially true in Doom 3 and its expansion RoE. Lost Mission features the best hell environment out of the three. Doom 3, to me, was also far too easy of a game with Lost Missions and RoE offering much more of a challenge. RoE offers an artifact which you upgrade through boss encounters throughout the game that start compunding abilities such as slomo, invunerability, and power. This and the grabber gun (Doom's answer to Half-Life's "gravity gun") made me feel like a badass throughout the game, even if it did end up being extremely over powered by the end. Lost Mission cofusingly does without this artifact and ends up being a harder chapter, unrelated, Doom 3 chapter. At certain points in these games it did feel like a grind to get to the next interesting part, but overall I remained pretty entertained though the 18-20 hours it took me to beat all of the Doom 3 content. 8.5/10
(NOTE: Doom 3 was not beaten on Nightmare mode, as I feel it has zero replay value; this would obviously probably change my complaints with difficulty however.)

This game is a package deal with the first two Doom games and Doom 3. It is not a perfect package, however. Doom 1 and 2 are censored, removing the red crosses on the medikits and re-skinning the Wolfenstein-themed secret levels in Doom 2 to remove Swastikas (presumably to sell the game without issues in Germany). For this reason, I recommend finding a de-censoring patch tool to restore these elements. The package includes a new 9-level campaign for Doom 2, No Rest for the Living, which had previously only been available on XBox 360. The Final Doom campaigns and the Master Levels for Doom 2 are not included, so you will need to purchase them separately. The WAD files for Doom 1 and 2 are compatible with most source ports and mods.
Doom 3 is almost identical to the original 2004 version, except the awkward "no duct tape on Mars" problem has been fixed. You can use the flashlight with any weapon equipped, making the game much faster and smoother to play without needing to switch weapons every time you see an enemy in the dark. It includes a new campaign, the Lost Mission, which just re-uses assets from the base game and Resurrection of Evil. It's probably the weakest part of the package. No new guns, enemies, or environments at all. It's also worth noting that none of the mods for the 2004 release work with this version.
I recommend this package because the games included are of high quality, but if you already own them separately it's not worth a second purchase.

Doom 3: BFG Edition is Doom 3 with updated graphics, it also includes the original Doom 1 and Doom 2. There is also all the expansions of Doom 3 such as Resurrection of Evil and The Lost Mission which is also remastered.
+ The story is detailed yet simple, Becasue its so simple you can choose if you want to collect all the logs and videos which has lots more information about the story. For a FPS the story is well thought out.
+ The graphics are alot better whan before since they updated the textures, shadows, lighting and lots more. This makes the game feel new. They only done this like Doom 3 and the expansions.
+ Controls are spot on. They are very simple and you will quickly learn them. Only weird/bad thing about them is that right click is jump, but you can just change that since you can re-map the controls.
+ Doom 3 is different from most first person shooters becasue the game can seem scary at first but then feel like a FPS, but also can feel like a Sci-fi story/adventure. It has alot more to Offer you.
+ Having Doom 3, Resurrection of Evil, Lost Mission, Doom 1 and Doom 2 is great since there is so much entertainment to be had.
+ Once you have completed the games there is still more to do such as multi-player, leaderboards and Steam achievements. This gives you a few more hours gameplay. The multi-player is a bit hard to start becasue not so many people play it. But if you try then you can create a match.
+ The PC port runs very well and you should be able to max the game out easily. I used to play Doom 3 on my old computer witch only had a i3... No grathics card and I could run it on medium 900p.
+ The environments are very detailed and change from time to time which works well becasue once it starts to get boring the game changes by allowing you to go into space or old parts of the space ship.
- As I just said that the environment changes, the one problem with that is the massive build up. You visit hell towards the end which is great! But its very short which leaves you wanting more. But every other environment is fine.
- The gametime is around 10 to 15 hours. Thats good but you find that its get a bit repetitive towards the end of the game because you just end up shooting then walking, then shooting and again, again and again. It fun but not arfter a while. Thats only a small issue with it.
Overall I think that Doom 3: BFG Edition is a fun game which has lots of thing to offer. I would say its worth the money and if you like first person shooters then you should get this game. I am going to rate it 8.5 out of 10. Almost a 9 but only because there should be more gametime spent in hell which was so fun while is lasted that short amount of time. A great game which I would recommend.

I've been playing the Fallout series since the original launched in 1997 and I can confidently say that Fallout 4 is both a great game in its own right and also a great Fallout game with a story that is worthy of the franchise.
But you'd never know this if you went solely by the echochamber of lonely internet neckbeards whose sole hobby in life is to spend their time on message boards steeping themselves in their own gaming dogma instead of, you know, actually playing games for fun.
The truth is that, while these fat-fingered NEET armchair developers sit at home cursing at Bethesda through their monitors, Bethesda has successfully developed a unique formula that combines rich, open-world exploration with action RPG mechanics and memorable storytelling which they have honed over the last two decades; a formula stretching as far back as Arena, Daggerfall and Morrowind, neither of which were ever as complex or as deep as many of the TSR-based RPGs that Bethesda aped with their action-rpg titles (but this is something fanboys will never tell you).
Fallout is no different. If you're an
you will never - ever - accept the changes Bethesda makes, just as Sunni Jihadis will never accept a Shiite's mufti teachings.
If you've enjoyed Bethesda's other titles particularly Skyrim or Fallout 3, chances are Fallout 4 is almost sure to please.
Fallout 4 adopts many of Skyrim's gameplay mechanics (skill/perks trees, crafting, home-building) while improving upon many of Fallout 3's shortcomings like poor shooting mechanics,  a lack of faction variety and renewable quests.
Storywise, Fallout 4 is a remarkable adventure that explores the future by way of the past, how our memories make us who we are and, with regards to Synths (synthetic humans made by the shadowy Institute), how they even make us human.
By game's end you aren't just going to decide humanity's fate, you will define what humanity
. Anyone who says that Fallout 4's story is poorly written either hasn't played it, is lying, or simply doesn't understand it.
By comparison,  New Vegas' two primary factions squabbling over the Hoover Dam and the Vegas Strip out of a lust for power and influence is about as fascinating as the nutritional information on a box of oatmeal. Not to mention how the lead writer literally copy/pastes the college textbook definition of "dialectical materialism" into his dialogue and the fanboys fall over themselves as if the words were divinely inspired.
Fallout 4 isn't perfect, there are areas that Bethesda could have improved upon, but as games go it is a fully featured, post-apocalyptic romp that will keep you coming back for hundreds of hours (my hours alone attest to that). It's smart but it doesn't pretend to be some great philosophical work but then it doesn't need to be; it does what all good games set out to be: a fun, memorable experience.
If Fallout 4 were a food it would be a juicy cheeseburger with a heaping side of fries. New Vegas, by comparison, is a tall glass of pureed wheat grass. New Vegans will loudly insist (over and over) that the latter is better and tastier than the former but the truth is out there for all to see; a truth they have blinded themselves to out of pure envy and spite. It's sad really.
As for Creation Club, the hyperbole and panic that exists around it is overblown, it is completely optional content that no one is required to buy. It allows the community to contribute to mod developers in a curated experience you cannot get in the free mod scene. Anyone who says that CC will kill mods or that it is a pretext to end modding is, like the other haters, lying in order to spread FUD but what can one expect from gaming extremists?

I'm going to start out by saying that I'm a huge fan of Tower Defense games, and a lot of them fall drastically short when it comes to enjoyment.  I'll also point out that If it wasn't for the free weekend, I probably never would have played Sanctum 2.  That said, I'm glad I did.
My first impressions of Sanctum 2 were a little clouded by the graphics I saw on the menus and loading screens.  I'm not one for the cartoonish-style drawings of characters who have rediculous proportions to them, like a character's hand that's almost bigger than their entire body.  Thankfully those only seem to be present in the loading screens and menus, while in-game it seems the characters have a much more "realistic" proportions to them.
Multiplayer in this game is fairly tricky because it doesn't let you know a few things.  First, when you start a game it's default settings are online and open to the public.  So as I was playing the game I found it a little shocking to suddenly have someone I didn't know start typing a bunch of things only an immature 12 year old would type.  I had to deal with the nonsense during an assault wave, but shortly after I completed the wave I was able to quickly locate the ban option in the menu and rid myself of the immature jack-off.  I also quickly located the settings to drop my public game to "friends only".  I've got to say, if I wasn't familiar with multiplayer games this sudden appearance of an immature flamer, while I assumed I was playing single player, would quickly see me deleting said game.  Not a smart move by the developers to put "public" as the default setting without warning the player.  On the other hand, It's kind of a cool ability that your friends can just pop into your game whenever you're playing and not need an invite.
The multiplayer snafoo aside, I found Sanctum 2 to be an extremely enjoyable game.  There is a story mode, challenge mode, and even sandbox modes for you to dabble in.  Sandbox mode even has settings so you can increase (or decrease) things like how much money you get from kills, how much money you recover from tower removal, the strength and feriousity of enemies, etc.  This brings a VERY high replayability to the game.
I know I downplayed mutliplayer due to my initial experience, but in reality this is where Sanctum 2 really shines the most.  Sure, single player is great and really enjoyable, but multiplayer is absolutely awesome.  Picture this...  You're placing towers and baricades.  You launch the next wave.  It gets past your first towers, and the second.  You start to feel overwhelmed as you fall back, firing and firing.  Oh no, you have to reload!  Suddenly 3 others jump in and start blasting the hell out of the enemies before they can stomp you to bits.  That's right, your friends are laying down a bunch of whoop♥♥♥♥♥  You join back into the fray with a new found sense of joy.  THIS is what co-op is all about!
Sound is pretty well done in the game.  Any text you type into the chat is relayed both visually in a chat window and via audio.  That's right, it plays AUDIO to say in your character's voice what you typed in the chat.  Doesn't get any better than that... Oh wait, it does!  This game also includes voice chat, for those who have microphones and aren't afraid to use them.
I have to say, I didn't think Sanctum 2 would be as good as it was hyping itself but in reality, after sorting out the multiplayer settings, this game has really shown me how great tower defense can be with a little FPS tossed in.  How good is it?  Well, let's just say I didn't know anyone who played it so I purchased a few 4-pack's and tossed copies at my friends like Santa Clause.

Sanctum 2 doesn't offer much in the way of tutorial for new players, starting your right in the action. The most essential elements of gameplay are explained in mouseover tooltips, and after that it's just you and your strategy versus wave after wave of very hostile aliens.
Campaign storyline progress is provided in a comic book page style on each level's loading screen, and the levels start out pretty empty - it's up to you to decide how best to deploy your defenses based on what's coming next from the enemy direction.
Gameplay is balanced such that your towers don't quite dispatch all of the oncoming hostiles on their own - you'll need to go toe to toe with some heavy hitting bosses to keep your core safe.
Multiple gameplay modes and difficulties make this game challenging enough to be satisfying without being too hard to enjoy. This game has the distinction of being one of the few I've ever played where death isn't ruinously frustrating - if you die, you wait ten seconds to respawn and you jump blazing back into the action. I'd place my FPS skills at "below average" on a good day, and I was still able to finish the campaign on my own in a few days.
Overall, this game is an outstanding value, and a lot of fun!

AvP 2010 really lets you feel like you're a Xenomorph or a Predator. The story is throwaway, but decently executed. The graphics still hold up well, along with the sound. All the little touches (acid/blood on the Predator's blades) and great sound effects make the game pretty immersive.
What's not so great? The Marine campaign is noticeably weaker than either the Xenomorph or Predator, with goofy voice acting and limited scare value. Max graphics still require a decently powerful videocard to pull off (especially the DX11 effects) at high res (1080p+) at 60fps. Almost no one plays multiplayer anymore.
Don't pick this game up expecting amazing writing. This game excels at giving you a sweet Alien/Predator experience, and an okay Marine one. If you are at all an Alien/Predator fan, definitely worth picking this up.

This game is for the ultimate AvP fans, and that only.
You can choose between 3 species, the Aliens, the Predators, and the Marines (Humans). They each get their own single player campaign, which are all interesting in their own way. The Alien gets you to sneak in the shadows, silently taking out their prey. The Predator gets you in the open, with your cloak, you can sneak up on people and collect their heads as trophies. The Marine is when you really are screwed. You are almost always in dark areas with a pistol or a pulse rifle with Aliens that could be anywhere.
But... you don't get much replayibility out of it unless you're a hardcore AvP fan, or an Alien or Predator fan. Like me, I could pick this up and play it, but for others, it is really boring to play through another time.
Would you buy this game?

After putting almost 200 hours into this game I think it is only fair to write a positive review here. At the point of writing Season 1 is finished and the game has become way better than it was at the start 9 months ago. Street Fighter games in general seem to be very polarizing games. Some people really dislike (and love) some iterations of this classic Fighter. For me the all time favorite will always be Alpha 3. In retrospect, despite playing it a lot I can't stand IV anymore. For me V was a breath of fresh air as compared to the predecessor.
The animations look great, the soundtrack is superb, the gameplay is amazing. The weekly missions feature keeps me playing online and in terms of matchmaking, for me it is better than IV. The 3f buffer for simpler combos and using the V-System instead of Focus Attacks is a huge plus in my opinion.
Generally speaking, this is the current flagship of the fighting game community and it seems it is here to stay. If you prefer single player content you might want to wait and see if an Arcade mode gets released in Season 2. For everyone else out there who likes these kinds of games there really is no way to avoid this one. This is more true if you do not have a PS4 at home.

It can often be surprisingly entertaining, refreshing even, to download and start an almost randomly chosen game obtained in some bundle, often a game which could linger in those large Steam libraties forever.
Sadly, this game is not one of those. It promises to be a classic action-rpg with focus on combat, loot and character development. And although the interface is extremely big, the controls wonky and the dialogues rather uninteresting (and not voice-acted), I felt a certain urge to explare the outerspace world, kill those pesky aliens and find awesome loot. Sadly, the combat turned out to be very, very repetitive and boring, and - even worse - unbalanced. Since energy cells are not only the local currency but also the ammunition for your energy-powered weapons, I tried to rely on melee weapons to save ammo, but due to a lack of armour during the earliest stages of the game this didn't work out well. Since leveling proved to be extremely slow (and thus promising an endless grind-fest), I decided to quit this one, and look for another unknown game in my library.

Town of Salem is a multiplayer strategy role-playing game with a simple design yet very engaging gameplay. There are a lot of reasons to love this game, and there is no reason you shouldn't play it as there is a free browser version available. The only reason I use the Steam version is for better accessibility, and the only benefit is that you get five dollars worth of town points.
Pros
-Huge variety of roles to explore
-Many different game modes to play
-A ranked mode for competitive and experience players (like me)
-Can play with up to 14 other players
-Very easy-to-use and simple interface
-Ability to chat about your info (or lie about it)
-Multiple phases of gameplay
-Ability to have friends
-Great background music
-Very well balanced
Cons
-Can be easy to get screwed by events out of your control
-Somewhat steep learning curve
-Sometimes your arguments won't work despite them being true
Overall, this game does have minor issues, but they are GREATLY outweighed by the good parts. This game gets a 10/10 from me and I would definitely recommend this game to you. Just don't spend your money on the Steam version and play it for free on your browser. (I only did it for better access.)

The classic that tried to reboot a classic franchise. Some say it was a success, others a failure.
Regardless, it developed a cult following.
DOOM 3: BIG ♥♥♥♥ING GUN EDITION is the same game you enjoy from 2004, except with a few tweaks.
This game has always been a Western take on the Eastern "Survival Horror" genre. It being Western-developed at the time meant more action oriented than what you were used to in a "Survival Horror" like, say, Resident Evil.
When this game was originally developed they tried to separate it from the rest of the franchise by making it more visceral and scary. This edition still retains all of the same atmosphere and tension you remember, but they revamped the gameplay to make it like they actually wanted it the first time around: like Doom I and II. The game has more ammo drops and the gun locations have been somewhat changed making them a little easier to find. The textures have all been redone and upgraded, as well as the lighting. This is another spot that makes it different from it's initial release. Upon comparison you will notice the original 2004 was noticeably darker. That being said, they didn't have as great of an engine to show off back then, either. The AI have been upgraded to be more responsive and ferocious as well.
This game comes filled with extra content. Not only does it come with DOOM 3, it comes with DOOM 3: Resurrection of Evil, an all new expasion pack - DOOM 3: The Lost Mission, as well as the original DOOM I and II!
This is the definitive collection of DOOM, I highly recommend it.

A well done and imaginative adventure game.
I can use this as a counterpoint to Broken Age.  While Double-Fine had nearly limitless funding to produce an adventure game, they spent it all on the first half, rushed the second half and ended up with a good looking but still mediocre adventure game.  Fran Bow had nearly no resources and stretched its budget as far as it could go and came out as a fantastic adventure game.
The low budget in development shows, the graphical quality of the backgrounds and characters are poor, the inventory can be a trudge to navigate through as you have to click on use, look, and combine on the junk you carry around like this is an adventure game from the late '80s.  In fact, the design sees no evolution in Adventure Game development aside from the mini-games between chapters which are an unwelcome change in gameplay and are skippable with no impact on the play through.  However, it does not need to evolve because it does what it does well with what the developers were given to work with.  The art style works well to make the protagonist come off as insane and projects the nightmares she sees all the time into the world.  The rest of the game is well done enough with a story and design that hooks you so well it doesn't need any innovation to keep you playing it.
The story revolves around a child at a mental institution named Fran Bow and her search for her "talking" cat.  Along the way you see and discover the messed up circumstances around her lack of sanity and how she copes with what happened to land her in the mental institution in the first place.  Much of the game takes place in what may or may not be the nightmares and hallucinations of this little girl.  The art style, sound, music, and some of the jarring transitions between reality and unreality help present the story and the world she lives in.
This is a classical adventure game so there are inventory puzzles where you have to rub the right thing in your inventory against the right object to advance the story.  There are also puzzles where you have to figure out how to use environmental objects or machinery with little instructions to open new paths.  They are on the harder side of the puzzles you find in adventure gaming, but I wouldn't call their difficulty frustrating or insurmountable.
In all, a wonderful adventure game I'd recommend.

I'm somewhat on the fence about this game, but I think I can say I recommend it with reservations.
The real-time approach is often a mistake in making a 4X game; StarDrive manages to avoid most of the big problems that other recent attempts (most notably the terribly disappointing Armada 2526) have had. The mechanics make sense, and the player can make informed choices to wring out advantages to actually win battles, wars, and the game. Custom ship designs are a key part of the value proposition of the game, and the implementation here is meaty and satisfying.
Those good things said, the game has some big flaws in usability/playability. There is often only one way to perform an action  (scrap/refit a ship, scroll the map) when there should be several; information displays like the known-planets list and ships list are missing key features. Also, while the ship design module is a lot of fun early in the tech tree, as ships get larger the lack of any automated support makes filling in all the boxes of a design tedious instead of fun.
I picked StarDrive up as part of the holiday sale, and I can say it was worth the discounted price to me, but I'm not sure it would be worth full price.

Burnout Paradise is the game Hot Wheels wishes it could make. For me, it lived up to the trailer. I've spent hours and hours playing the game; unlocking all the cars, finding and re-finding all the secrets, generally exploring Paradise City and cruising, or wreaking havoc everywhere. The game really pulls off a very, very awesome style (the soundtrack, the cars, the radio host, the city itself) that no other racing game that I've played matches.
THE BAD:
- This game is 7 years old at this point, which is basically ancient history in the eyes of EA. And that means...
- The console DLC never came to the PC, and it never, ever will, even though I'd buy it in a heartbeat. EA thinks you're a loser for still playing this.
- THERE'S NO WAY TO TURN OFF THE TRAFFIC. This nearly killed any fun I had in this game. There are so, so many areas that are perfect for awesome stunts, huge drifts and pure racing, but you'll never unlock that full potential because some random hatchback or city bus is in the way.
- The AI cheats. Yes, this game is an example where having the fastest car doesn't actually matter, at least in the Marked Man events. The AI can and will always be on your tail.
I listed several dealbreakers above that would have probably deterred me from buying the game originally, but if I actually had to do it all again, I would over and over. Paradise is just too much fun despite its faults.

This is quite a nice game. The lack of a nicely paced tutorial and some of the controls being not so intuitive (but once you learnt it, either by google or the game's wiki, it's not a problem no more) might put off some, but in my opinion, this game is a gem.
A typical 4X turn-based game can more often than not turn into a flutter of clicks while you wait, or at times, there's just so much info and decisions to go through, that sometimes each turn can take a whole lot of time. The "real-time" concept in this game is a good balance. You can speed up, slow down and pause, in other words, you dictate the pacing of the game.
Space battles are cool and there's quite a bit of getting used to here... meaning to say, there's some interesting tactics... like making your ships charge and come around at slower ships... allows a more maneuverable but less powerful ship to bring down a slower brute... or a swarm of light ships can do more damage to one or a few powerful capital class ships...
Of course, there are things to be improved... research can be painstakingly slow, but perhaps it's because there are not that many things to research... or that it's one way to stretch the game, I don't know. I would be happy to have some mods or DLCs with new techs...
I'd say, if you liked MOO 1 and 2... and after getting Sins of a Solar empire, and you feel you want something in between of these games... Definitely go for StarDrive...
Cheers!

This game is cancer.
It's as close as you can get to a game giving you brain cancer.
It's not cancer through sucking, although I wasn't exactly pleased with the game either. It's cancer because it's aimed at teaching you schizophrenia.
Not teaching you ABOUT schizophrenia. It's aimed at driving you - the player - insane.
Keep this game away from people under the age of 17. I'm serious. If kids play this game, and start eating baking soda, or feces, or jump off cliffs thinking they'll survive, then you've now been warned.
I bought this game thinking that it would be about a girl struggling with schizophrenia, or some similar mental disease. ...but the thing is that she's not really struggling. Instead schizophrenia gives her super powers, like the ability to actually turn invisible, or time travel, or not die, by "going into other dimensions", her psychosis being actually real.
The game follows pretty closely how a schizophrenic person would reason, using compelling rhetorics to try to overpower skepticism in the player, turning words on their heads, with the end goal to try to convince the player that imagination is just you seeing other forms of reality.
This game scares me in the same way that Waldorf schools scare me: Kids who play these games may actually develop schizophrenia from it, and already insane people wouldn't exactly go saner from it.
There are plenty of dialogue choices in this game: You're always given two dialogue options. These options doesn't seem to affect the game beyond some additional dialogue - there's no "good ending" or "bad ending".
As usual with point and click games, you will get stuck time and again, trying to find the thing to use on the thing to get the thing. Sometimes this involves picking up a thing from a huge pile of various rubble, sometimes it means picking up a certain plank from something made out of planks, sometimes it means using objects to combine properties in unreal and un-advicable ways, and sometimes it means clicking on a small heap of rubble in a large area "when you need to". You will need to look up a walkthrough several times over, which leads to a kind of inception when the LPer in your walkthrough, in turn has to look up a walkthrough several times.
The plot itself is just the visualized ramblings of a madman, that leads up to a very overused plot twist. I won't spoil it - it's just that I'm sick of that particular type of twist, especially when the game itself spoils it continuously throughout the game.

I waited to write this review until I had beaten the game and got all of the achievements.
I didn't really expect much from this game. I'm not really into these action, kiddy looking, RPGs. I kind of just picked it at random from where it had been collecting dust in my library, but it won my heart. The voice acting is amazing and clever. Arguably, there is a deep philosophical lesson to this game. I won't give it away though. The music? Wow. I have never wanted to buy a game soundtrack, but I do now! At some point in the game, you get a radio, with which you can put whatever song you like on from the soundtrack.
The game has different endings. You beat the game once, and have the option to play the game again with all of your weapons, upgrades, and level intact. This is helpful to get a different ending and/or for achievements.
There is also a attack score mode, where you restart from the beginning, without your upgrades and from level one. In this mode, you can accumulate points and compete on the leaderboards.
There are some really tough achievements, but once you get them you have this huge feeling of accomplishment. They really test your skills as a player.
Buy this game. If you are on the fence, put it on your wishlist, and buy it when it goes on sale. I seriously doubt that you will be disappointed.

1. The start of the game is linear in every game, You have to build a woodcutters, you have to build a scout, and you have to build a house. Every single game. No clan has any variety, it would be nice if say, one clan never needed to build houses, or maybe had innate woodcutting with the scavenging, or villagers can scout.
2. The scout... the scout camp is a building that will never be upgraded. Why would anyone use koins/wood/stone to upgrade something as late as you can get it? Since you need a lvl 2 town center first. To fix the scout, either make normal vilagers do what scouts can do just need to be manually used, or let us upgrade the scout building early on, cept using the wood that would normally be used for the first house - so you can choose to scout 100% faster early on, or get the 10 pop max early on, be some decisions to mix up starting gameplay.
Houses are alright, wood cutting is alright..
3. Wood. You never have wood issues, in every hard game I play, I end with 3000 or something wood, but like 0 food. One forest, one woodcutters upgraded, and three woodcutters there is all you need for the entire game. Everything else goes up as you get more villagers, wood is still never an issue, even when there is a blizzard, only once have I ever had 0 wood. (and that's because lol rng blizard at the start)
4. THE RNG. Your start base needs to start with a food source. If you could build a food building there guarnteed every game, it would make SUCH a diference. reduce the rng of the map build, and really help every player, including the ai, in not dying from food loss forever.
Also, the rng of attacks. I've had some games in blizzards where I've been attacked in the same tile, 5 times from the wild. 3 wolves, then 3 druag, then 2 wolves, then wolves again, then draug. IT WAS INSANE. even early on when you have like just your starting tile I have been attacked by 3 wolves and almost lost the game 5mins in. Then attacked in another tile at the same time as soon as I took it right after this. Then in other games, not getting attacked once even with a tile surrounded by pve spawn camps. There needs to be some balance here. A tile should not be able to be pve attacked 3 times in the same month. - or right after colonisation.
Also also, the RNG OF WORLD EVENTS. had one game start with a rat infest - which noone had silo's yet so we all lost 80% of our food, then next event in winter was a blizzard... I saw 2 computers buildings on fire during the blizzard.. then they seem to defualt to just spawning vilagers out of there town center due to them losing everything from the blizzard.. I mean I had 8 sick villagers... and the computer faired worse. Blizzards are insane, esp compared to all the other events... like lol earthquakes? That's like never noticable at any time in the game, draug spawning? There is always like 3 spawning at most even when you have like 20 tiles.
4. The game elements are harder and hurt you more then pvp. The ai mroe often dies as well just from pve attacks then attacks from each other or you. Because of how reliant EVERYTHING in the game is with food, it makes it impossible for the ai to do anything if they also don't start nearby food. Blizzards, winter, just general food use, pve attacks, ect. All of that, is harder to beat then the ai is, where you can sometimes kill him entirely with one warrior, even on hard mode.
5. the ai needs work, One game I saw the same ai send his warchief to his Death 8 times against THE SAME TURRET. lol. No idea where he got all that coin to lose, but seeing the computer on hard attack in a one by one line, then get kited to death with a vilager and one turret.. is stupid.
6. Feasts need to be much better as the game progresses, I know only one clan makes them better, but they should get better over time for all clans. They start costing WAY to much food and don't relaly do anything later. either that or the cost for every feast in order needs ot be halved. (and then halve the fame gains)

What does it take to survive as an undercover cop who infiltrates one of Hong Kong's most ruthless criminal organizations? If Sleeping Dogs is any indication, it takes martial arts prowess, good marksmanship, driving skill, a reckless willingness to leap from one speeding vehicle to another, and the confidence to sing karaoke. None of the individual elements in Sleeping Dogs are best-in-class, but they're all thoroughly enjoyable, and the structured story missions have you switching from one type of action to another frequently enough that you're never tired of what you're doing at any given moment. Additionally, the fictionalized version of Hong Kong where Sleeping Dogs takes place is an exotic and atmospheric setting for this tale of conflicting loyalties; you probably wouldn't want to live amid the ruthless criminals who populate the game's cast, but this world sure is a nice place to visit.
I love Risk the board game, but this version was a disappointment. Extremely bare bones version with no extra game modes besides classic Risk and no online multiplayer makes for a hollow experience.

To start off, I have put almost 400 hours into this game.  I have dumped a comparable amount of time into Fallout 3 (before I got Steam) and I have dumped almost 1000 hours into New Vegas.  I think it's safe to say I have a good understanding of these three games.
Fallout 4 is an absolutely God-forsaken travesty of a Fallout game.
The branching dialogue paths that would allow for interesting character interaction have been reduced to Yes, No, Sarcastic Yes, and More Information.
The Skills that would allow for actual RPG gameplay have been removed entirely in favor of dumbing down the entire system.
The "infinite" quests are just a series of "go to this location and kill the things" busy work missions with no real impact of any kind.
The characters are uninteresting and completely forgettable.
The only interesting Companion has her entire character ruined by her own Loyalty Mission.
I could go on, but I don't want the bulk of this review to be just a list of things I dislike.
Even with all the myriad problems I've found in my time playing this game, I think the most telling thing I've discovered is my own reaction to these issues: indifference.  Indifference to the bugs, indifference to the plot, indifference to the characters, indifference to damn near everything.
I look at this game and I think to myself "there's nothing here.  This isn't worth any further thought."
I'm so bored with this game I can't even summon proper emotional responses.
After uninstalling this game, I booted up New Vegas and I was instantly excited to be back in Goodsprings again.
The very thought of playing Fallout 4 again bores me to sleep.
I think that's the best comparison I can make, honestly.
An older, clunkier spinoff game made by a different company is inherently more entertaining than a mainline big-budget release by the actual owner of the franchise.
This is the sign of a problem, Bethesda.
Now, if you'll excuse me, I got spurs that jingle jangle jingle as I go ridin' merrily along.

That's pretty much my answer to all questions regarding this.. visual novel. I'm a big fan of visual novels, and so I can judge fairly harsh. This is by no means a professional review, it's just my thoughts on the matter. But I'll give it in simple terms:
Pros:
- Decent character art.
- Decent background art.
- Decent music
Cons:
- Short (can be considered a pro if you hate it)
- Weak characters
- Weak plot
Basically, in my own opinion, this is a very bad visual novel. I can see effort was put into this, but.. it just doesn't hold up in the end.  I won't even go into the options.. or rather, the serious lack of them.
I may very well dislike this visual novel because I prefer long and in-depth stories, with a lot of character development. I think that's only natural. This just doesn't feel right, whatsoever. Ahh, opinions, don't we love 'em? Anyway, if you're going for all achievements, or just want to do all routes, you better start using the skip option. The story is identical except for a few different lines - regardless of the option you choose. After a few lines of "new" dialogue it goes right back onto the same story as if your choice didn't matter. The only significance your choices have are.. let's just say, you get a point for a girl if you choose the "correct" option. Whatever girl you have the most points with in the end, you'll end up with.
All that being said, it's all good if you like simple, short stories and yuri romance.
TL;DR: If you like a simple story with some romance and girl on (cat)girl action, give it a go. If not, stay away.

This game looks great and shows promise, but it has serious problems.  First the good parts.
The graphics are cool and the game shows a lot of potential.
Now the bad parts.  The game is not balanced and is often frustrating.  You cannot affect the rate at which you produce workers except late in the game.  You can't build any more buildings to generate workers ever, so the main mechanic of this game is to not let anyone die because it takes so long to replenish that worker.
The beginning of the game is unbearably slow.  Most RTS games have a slow start but they give you some kind of control (like two people working on a building, just for instance) over your progress.  This game is very static.  Get a new worker and decide what to do with him.
There is way too much randomness to your starter zone.  You may be bordered by a lot of land that has wolves and has to be cleared with warriors before you can even start.  Good luck with that.  At other times, you have lots of clear land with resources.  This inconsistency could be fun if managed correctly, but the game is not there yet.
So if you want to support this project, please do, but know that you will get very frustrated and even after playing many hours the game doesn't get much easier as there really isn't much depth to the game at the moment and that severly limits your gameplay options.
4/10 but still recommend for the fans of the genre.

is a really short - and not very well done - visual novel with a centering theme on female homosexuality. Yup, this is a Yuri title. I would really like to recommend this game, considering there aren't many otome visual novels that would even include same sex romance options and a game focusing on female homosexuality sounds like a concept to be supported - if only it would be better executed and accurately presented. Yet, the execution of the theme is really poor here, both with the boring narrative and non-existent character depth. It just is not a good game.
Here we have Ami, a shy and nerdy teenage girl who attends an all-female high school, alongside her best friend Ria. Her parents travel throughout the year to attend business meetings, so Ami has all the time and the space in the world to herself, and she is lonely. Stating a useful fact on the side: she is also gay and faces the fear of being judged if she were to come out of the closet. To keep herself busy, she decides to attend the Coding Club of the school and start working on a platform video game that they'd make with the senior club president, Lise. At some point, the designed protagonist of the game; a ninja cat girl named Starla comes alive, mostly to Ami's surprise and distress. How to handle this situation now?
Let's start with the display quality, shall we? There is an annoying inconsistency about the artworks and the CGs used for characters. Throughout my full playthrough, I've came across 4 different types of art works depicting the same characters ridiculously differently - none being appeasing or even anatomically correct. There has been some sorry attempts at presenting fan service, but no one should specifically prefer these ones for even that purpose. Environment designs are nothing remarkable or even remotely interesting, and the soundtrack is only forgettable. Oh, and there is no voice acting either.
I wouldn't care much for the art quality if only there were to be somewhat decent narrative and an intriguing storyline. Well, there is none! The storyline doesn't carry any drama, mystery, insight, sentimental attachment or anything that would make Ami's story interesting. She - alongside four romance options - and her ordeal, her frustration is presented as shallow as it can be. There is no credible story progression, no real life solution to the subject matter or a character portrayal that would make us emphasize with Ami. Character interactions are downright boring, with superficial social exchanges playing on the idea of female sexuality. Whomever wrote that script, clearly had no idea about an actual female/female relationship. The developer only established a sorry setting to play on some fantasy here and earn some money from it while he is at it. Aside portraying wholly shallow characters, the narrative is full with grammatical errors and dialogues marked for wrong characters. Without any option to reread the dialogue once its passed, it becomes a problem to keep track of whomever said what, and without much you'd be curious about the story itself, you lose interest fast.
To top all the nonsense this game contains, save game function is completely broken. If it's a Win64, sorry people. You cannot save at all. Developers are trying to solve that problem at the moment, but it seems like a problem with the game engine itself, so... no near future solutions yet. At least there is a skip dialogue option to go for fast playthroughs to achievement hunt.
At the end of the day, you may prefer passing this one. There is nothing intriguing or esthetically pleasing here. Even people who'd buy this to take a glimpse on some girl on girl action could probably do with something else better. Sad story.

Space Hack Review - Raymond KT
Summary: Space Hack is a sci-fi Action/RPG title with Diablo-inspired gameplay mechanics, presented in real-time 3D graphics. The story puts gamers on a colony transport ship that suddenly gets trapped inside a Black Nebula, but thatâ??s only their first problem. While trapped, they get boarded by aliens that take over the ship and begin to kill and eat the colonists. Playing the role of a tough, gristled ex-military man, gamers will struggle to reach an emergency transport module at the far end of the ship to free the remaining colonists, hacking and slashing their way through hordes of alien creatures along the way.
In Space Hack, you must single-handedly rid a huge colony ship of an alien infestation, one mutant bug at a time. The game unashamedly cribs from Diablo, and we're talking the 1996 original more so than the 2000 sequel to Blizzard's popular action/role-playing hybrid. So, much like the name implies, Space Hack is a fairly simple game about killing lots and lots of aliens, finding better stuff, leveling up, and navigating lots of big, sparsely detailed levels. It's got a decent enough presentation, and it's a really long game despite the budget price, but bad pacing and a lack of variety drag the whole thing down.
You probably figured the title Space Hack was in direct reference to the action in the game, but it turns out that Hack is also the game's main character. A name like "Hack" doesn't necessarily inspire much confidence, but in this case, Hack is supposedly the most capable and versatile human fighter remaining on the doomed colony ship you'll need to fight through. He's part of a small band of surviving humans who've holed up in a little base, and without much rhyme or reason, he'll be sent off to battle the alien hordes all alone using whatever weapons he can get his hands on. The game's story is presented with poorly translated onscreen text, so it really doesn't do much to establish what you're supposed to be doing or why you should care. Of course, the premise of fighting back droves of aliens is a good enough motivating factor on its own.
A good first effort from Rebelmind Games that is worth every cent of the twenty bucks it will cost you - but not much more

After coming back from a two year hiatus, I can say that the community in a sense has grown. It is a great sense of nostalgia brough back by the lack of frames and the odd mouse issue, the later of issue would be nice if fixed. Many are saying that progression is slow, but personally I am fine with it. It may have to do with the fact that my account had a fairly high power level, but I may have dedicated more time.
However, after the two years of being gone, the only pro is the nostalgia. It is awesome to see that some updates have added SOME content, but its not much. Its as if they have forgotten who their audience is. In my case when I began my Trovian adventures, I was a low budget gamer with a low budget computer. I had little money to spend on games and so my journey to find a free to play game had been blown into full force. I can tell you I had gone through a fair amount of awful MMO's. Fortunately I am not in that state anymore. The easiest way to progress is to have a high leveled friend to tag around with.
The charm however, it remains. It's something about that era of "blocks" that has a certain charm to it. Yes, it is odd to say that you shoud download the game for the looks, but that is what I am saying.
Try it.

Game is too easy for classic grand strategy (4X) genre in every aspect. You can learn all the tricks in mere minutes and there's not much to do after that.
Most annoying is the tech tree: it is just too shallow and all-visible at start (well, there's something like 1-6 upgrades in 1-3 tech trees in each of five tiers plus one 'hidden' tier). Upgrades are completely evolutional, improving just main characteristic of shield/armor/weapon/etc.
Space combat is really nasty too: no matter how much time you spend designing your ships combat result is mostly determined by ability to sustain DPS and hit the target (like a not-so-large pack of cheapest fighters with ammo-less lasers easily destroy something like cruiser). Moreover ships in fleet do not keep formation during combat thus there's no such thing concentrated fire or support ships staying in safe position delivering ammo/repairs to the hot zone.
As for diplomacy, well there's none out there. First Civilization had as much diplomatic choices as we have here and it is not the simplicity you want.
To be honest there's a couple of things that are good: it is ship designer (however you cannot fit your design with latest weapons/armors just developed by your techs, you need to do it manually) and 'turnless' strategic mode, however there're many space strategies which include these pros and doesn't have so much cons. If you want a good game, go for endless space (easy to learn) or something like space empires V or distant worlds (much harder thingies)

Overall it is a fun game to play with friends that I would recommend, but I would say maybe hold off until more content comes out.

I was given Bastion as a gift, and man, what a fantastic gift it was.  This is a gorgeous action game featuring a charming art style and dynamic animation, and it follows your character, known simply as "the Kid", as he investigates a calamity that ruined civilization and pieces together the remnants of the mysterious Bastion with a handful of other survivors.
Gameplay is very much level-based, featuring short maps where the world materializes under your feet as you fend off a variety of enemies and search for fragements of the Bastion, which serves as your home base.  After each mission, you return to base, where you can swap loadouts, purchase upgrades, and repair the facilities.  The addictive nature of these improvements is sure to keep you moving along at a good clip and leave you constantly wanting more.
Special mention must be given to the weapon system, which is superior.  As the player, you have a large selection of weaponry at your disposal, from carbine to flamethrower to machete.  Each weapon handles very differently, and has a number of possible upgrades, and it's impressive how the developers managed to balance the system so that you can be viable with nearly any combination.  Need practice with one of the weapons?  Try the proving grounds, fun custom-made obstacle courses designed around each weapon, hard enough to be tantalizingly out-of-reach with few upgrades, but with time and practice, offer awesome unlockable special skills.
All in all, this game is an absolute blast.   You could probabally blast through the story in just a few hours, but for a challenge, there's a pagan shrine, and activating the various idols found therein will give enemies serious buffs in exchange for extra combat rewards.  In my opinion, there's plenty here to add replay value; a special unlockable provided in the second playthrough is worth the price of admission alone.
This brings me to the best part of the game, which is the Narrator, played by Logan Cunningham.  Cool and wistful, he keeps a running commentary of your gameplay, adding color, providing exposition, telling stories.  I could not have loved that aspect of the game any more.
If you're into pure fun, don't hesitate to check this one out.  Totally recommended.

Worms Clan Wars is another game at the famous franchise Worms. Like its predecessors, you'll create your team of worms and battle against other teams with an arsenal of weapons. However, this game has some changes from the previous versions and that's why is worth a shot.
The graphics didn't change too much from the previous games. Th enviroment and the characters and colorful and lively, being nice to the eyes.
The gameplay is the same of previous Worms: each player has your own turn and you choose one of your worms to do the action. You can move with the directional buttons, choose a weapon through your mouse or keyboard shortcuts and press the spacebar key to use the weapon. Depending of the weapon you choose, the effects at the opponent (and yourself) will be different, so you need to be cautious to not blown yourself up when you use the weapon. This is one of the many great things about the worms games, because a wrong use of a weapon can lead to very funny moments and even make you lose, instead of your opponent. When you use a weapon, your turn is over and it's your opponent turn. You win when every worm of your opponent is dead. If every worm, even yours, die, it will be a draw.
Also, you can also use some items which help you to fight or get a better position to knock out your enemy and, different of when you use a weapon, you won't finish your turn when using it. For example, with the ninja rope, your worm can reach high places and even shoot at your opponent while escaping for your own safety. For example, you can use the ninja rope to go higher and throw a dinamite at your opponent and, before the dynamite blows (you have only a couple of seconds), you can reach another safe place and watch your opponent getting blasted. Your opponent will be damaged by the explosion and be throw at the air because of the explosion and even can fall at the water, losing all its hp. By the way, there's water and you lose your worm if you fall there. Oops, didn't I say that before?
Anyway, it's really nice the huge variety of weapons for you to use at Worms Clan Wars. Plus, some of them are funny, like the powerful "Concrete Donkey", which, when used, a giant concrete donkey falls from the sky and go stomping every place at a vertical line, while doing a funny donkey sound.
By the way, I said before this game has some changes from its previous games. Well, this time, your worms are not equal. At previous games, every worm is exactly the same, changing only its name, but at this game, there are 4 types of worms, which can add some deep to your strategy. For example, there is the tiny worm, called "Scout", which can be faster and jump higher, but they are weaker than the another ones. In another hand, there's the "Heavy", which is the totally opposite of the Scout: it is fat and heavy, so it'll be slow and jump really low, but it's more powerful than the other ones.
There's not many musics here, but the few remaining are nice to hear. But the Audio and sound effects are great! They are nice and funny, specially the many voices you can use as your worms voice. You can laugh a lot with these.
Worms usually has no fixed storyline, except this one has a campaign mode about some worms hunting some rare artifacts. But you don't need to do the campaign, if you prefer only fighting to the death against your friends or the AI or both.
It's another amazing Worms game, with some good improvements, but keeping the old and good formula of success that made Worms a loved franchise. If you love Worms games, don't miss this one. And if you never played a worms game, try this one! It's lovely and I think you will enjoy!

This game looks great and shows promise, but it has serious problems.  First the good parts.
The graphics are cool and the game shows a lot of potential.
Now the bad parts.  The game is not balanced and is often frustrating.  You cannot affect the rate at which you produce workers except late in the game.  You can't build any more buildings to generate workers ever, so the main mechanic of this game is to not let anyone die because it takes so long to replenish that worker.
The beginning of the game is unbearably slow.  Most RTS games have a slow start but they give you some kind of control (like two people working on a building, just for instance) over your progress.  This game is very static.  Get a new worker and decide what to do with him.
There is way too much randomness to your starter zone.  You may be bordered by a lot of land that has wolves and has to be cleared with warriors before you can even start.  Good luck with that.  At other times, you have lots of clear land with resources.  This inconsistency could be fun if managed correctly, but the game is not there yet.
So if you want to support this project, please do, but know that you will get very frustrated and even after playing many hours the game doesn't get much easier as there really isn't much depth to the game at the moment and that severly limits your gameplay options.
4/10 but still recommend for the fans of the genre.

You know, one of the greatest video game gimmicks that ever was devised is that of the toy figure that can interact with your games. Skylanders started it, and then Nintendo went and made the Amiibo figures that work with lots of different games like Super Smash Bros. Wii, and others. Then Disney got it and just ran with it- now you can find pretty much every Disney property in its own game, Infinity. Why, one of these days, you'll be able to buy a 3D printer program and RFID chip and just make your own. ...though what would you do if the RFID chip decided to not work, but even crazier, it suddenly changed into the very catgirl ninja you were coding into the game? Such is the idea behind A Wild Catgirl Appears .
You play as Ami, a high-school student in a Japanese girls school who's suddenly faced with a bit of a problem- the student council has handed down a decision- this year, every student has to join a club. This presents a bit of a problem- Ami's not that much of an athlete, and not that popular, so well... she ends up joining the school's coding club. There, she meets another person- another girl by the name of Lise, and they start working on a game, one that stars a catgirl ninja, named Starla. One day, Lise gets the idea to make an Amiibo-style figure of Starla. The figure doesn't work, but... the next day, Ami finds a surprise in her bed- one catgirl ninja who has no idea how she got there... yeah, that's pretty much the story.
I'll say it right now- this is a VN with a yuri twist to it. Ami has the chance to end up with one of four different girls- Ria (the best friend), Lise (the coding club president), Starla (the catgirl ninja), and Eiko (another catgirl that just... appeared somehow).
The story, well... it leaves a lot to be desired. There are many errors in spelling and grammar that need to be corrected that ought to have been caught with a quick spellcheck and a read-through. Not to mention, the introduction of Eiko is handled really poorly- she just shows up out of nowhere with no major event or anything. It just sticks out that she's just there- she just shows up and is just there to be another possible love interest. Why not flesh them out a bit? It needs to be polished up, and there needs to be a reason as to why Eiko shows up other than "Oh, have some free DLC!"
The art is good- I just wish there was more of it. Almost every character picture is the exact same pose- and 90% of them are the same but with just the facial expressions changed. The backgrounds look nice, but more are needed- you can't pass off a pool locker room as a clothing store changing room, for example. Throw in some variety, throw in some new poses, and suddenly you have more variety and better understanding of the characters. There is a bit of skin, and it does imply a lot of stuff, but... I think this is another of those that ended up having material cut to get itself on Steam.
However, there is one big, glaring error in this game- there are four different endings, and you can get any of them. However, once you get one, you need to close and re-launch the game to clear the event flags in order to get a different ending- if you play through the game a second time, you still get the first ending you got. I am rather surprised this wasn't addressed in the re-release. It's a glaring error that ought to have been smashed out somehow.
Let's get down to brass tacks, here: I want to like this game. I think it has plenty of potential, and it could honestly benefit from plenty of TLC from its artists, writers and programmers. But until the game has at least the whole ending problem hammered out, I can't recommend this game. A bunch of smaller problems are building up into one big reason as to why you shouldn't pick this up. If a new edition of this comes out, I'll give it a look and write a new review. But until then? I can't justify anything higher.
Steam wants three G-bucks for it, and I think that's mostly fair- though on sale would be even better. It's nice, but... it's unpolished. If I could call this a neutral review, I could- it's got problems, but it also has potential.

I think my biggest problem with A Wild Catgirl Appears! is that the art styles are so vastly different at points that it throws me for a loop. Or maybe it's the dialogue? Or maybe it's the story line...
Either way, I got this game in a bundle for under a buck and I still feel as though it wasn't a particularly good use of my time. It took me two hours to get all the achievements (only because I did read through one path in totality before giving up and using the oh-so-helpful skip button) and two hours for the rest of the card drops. After that, I'll never boot this game up again--why would I?
Let's break this attempt at a visual novel down, shall we?
.Characters.
Japanese school girls who attend an all-girls school and have very little parental supervision for one reason or another. That about sums them up. One is moe, one is shy, one is a ninja, and one is a ninja student. And then there's you, the loner main character. The cast is very generic to the genre.
.Story.
You and a classmate are creating a game in a coding club after school. An after school club that has no members yet somehow has the funding to make RIF figures for a fully-functioning game that you create in a couple of sittings. Right. Your main character, Ami, takes the newly-made figure home and, lo-and-behold, you have a living, breathing cat girl and her cat girl friend that inexplicably accompanies her right in the comfort of your room. Ta-dah! And, for our next trick, the game makes these catgirls fit into society just like everyone else while your main character struggles to figure out which classmate or catgirl she'd like to date most.
The time frame of the game is very slippery. It feels as though the events, particularly the conclusion, just sort of bluster by as though the devs don't want you to think too hard about the logictics behind them.
"Inexplicable" is the key word for this game. There's a lot that doesn't get adequately described, but you're just kind of expected to accept things--much in the way that the characters do. No one questions the appearance of the titular "wild catgirl" and no one even seems to care that a half-naked girl wearing cat ears is wandering around among the general public. Ah, Japan.
But back to the story: the catgirl, Starla (which, I'm sorry, is such an ugly name), infiltrates your life and you guys have fun together and school and clubs and yuri undertones.The four girls you meet are all romance options and the ending you get is based heavily on the rare A or B options you get at points in dialogue
Which brings us to our next point.
.Voice acting and dialogue.
Most of it was irritating. Abrasive, even. I could forgive the voice acting if the things the voices said were at al interesting, but... Yeah, no. Not in the slightest. In fact, some of it felt stilted and/or forced coming from the mouth of a teenager or ninja catgirl.
.Art style.
I didn't play the game before the big patch that apparently changed the art style, but it feels as though bits of the old art style, which can be seen in the achievements, have been left over. In fact, the art style varies on a scene to scene basis. What was that saying about too many chefs in the kitchen? Point being that the hodgepodge of graphical styles, some good and some... atrocious, did nothing for the game.
.Bottom line.
If you're a card and achievement collector, sure. Buy this on sale. If you're looking for the next greatest visual novel, steer clear.

Positive review.
The game is neatly done.
Good music, nice animations and graphics in general, gameplay a bit new, between a 4X and settlers.
Though, I doubt the balance of the game at the minute.
I enjoyed playing the solo game (the skirmish version as the campaign is not available yet).
I lost my first game with a trading victory from the AI while I was trying the military victory so I'll focus more on the balance of the military aspect of this game.
Before that, let's talk about the gameplay first.
You settle on a zone that allows you to have 4 buildings to start with. Choose wisely !
If you go straight to military then you will slow down your production and growth by lack of wood, food and happyness.. .so, maybe plan ahead and start with the basics.
Then, with your explorers, find the neighbouring zones and spend a bit of food to settle in.
This zone will have its own perk therefore, every map is different and specific.
The more you expand, the more food you need to expand and this makes the game slower and slower if you're trying to conquer the whole island, therefore, this was quite a disappointment when I played.
There is no way I can win first with a military approach.
All zones are defended more or less and that's probably where your army is useful. I guess trying to eradicate the other player is most probably a lost cause unless you deactivated the other winning conditions.
Some neat features are there too.
- Reallocating very quickly your villagers from one task to another.
- kind of research tree and prestige points that can be ignored or not depending on your own goals
- rare resources that will allow you to enhance a few buildings only.
- ruins and derelics to explore to get a bonus.
- Trading amongst the other players and neutral factions even leading to alliance with AI to use their special units.
- Healer that heals accross the map
- sending villagers to do some raids and bring back money and fame
the Cons:
- Military victory (eradication) seems to be very difficult, military units pretty weak
- not a huge feeling of interaction with other players
So it's a rather positive game though I wouldn't say it is thrilling either.

Aliens, Predators and Humans.
Review of Aliens vs Predator for PC (2010). Compared with ACM (2013).
Made by Rebellion
Released in 2010
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Spoilers ahead.
Aliens vs Predator is the latest AvP title from Rebellion. The first game was AVP (1999).
The second was developed by Monolith and realised in 2001. The first version was improved (AvP gold) and can be purchased at steam. AvP 3 was released on february 19, 2010 in Europe and features three distinct story lines. You can play as Alien, Predator or Marine. It has no connection to the AvP films other that it features three characters and some familiar organisations like Weyland - Yutani.
(tip: before you play this game, you should have seen the Alien films and/or played other Alien related games)
Story and gameplay
The story is mediocre. But it offers unique perspectives on the Alien and Predator franchises. Weyland - Yutani is the main 'villain' in this game. This game let you play as Alien, Predator or Human.
- Compared with the story off ACM, this story is not quite as good. Because it has no connection to the films. ACM is better in this regard.
The Alien is nicknamed 'Number 6' and you will try to escape the facility and return to your queen. In the end you must fight the Predator.
The Predator is nicknamed 'Dark' and you will try to obtain a weapon that the marines captured. In the end you must fight the Predalien.
The Marine is nicknamed 'Rookie' and you will try to unravel the secrets of Weyland - Yutani and fight deadly Aliens. In the end you fight with Mr. Weyland.
The Alien campaign is the shortest. Crawling against walls and objects can be a bit difficult. You have no longe range weapons. You are the weapon. You can perform fatality moves with the 'E' button just like the Predator. You see with a 'fish - eye' perspective. The Alien can crawl into vents and airducts.
The Predator campaign offers high - tech weaponary and is quite entertaining. You can perform fatality moves just like the Alien. You cannot crawl but you jump from tree to tree. You have the ability to cloak yourself. With your helmet you can view in three 'modes'.
The Marine or human campaign is the longest. It is the standard FPS genre. You have weapons and you have a flaslight to illuminate dark areas. You are the 'soft' character, compared to Alien and Predator.
- Compared with ACM, the campaigns are original and fresh. You can play different characters. AVP is better in singleplayer aspect. ACM does offer co - op campaign unlike AVP.
Artifical Intelligence
The A.I. of the game is very good. You can set your difficulty and the enemies will become tougher. If you play on the highest setting: only for die hards.
- Compared with ACM, its a tie (difficulty settings).
Multiplayer
If you play multiplayer, you will play team deathmatch. It offers the three main characters in a brutal war against each other. You can also play other modes like survival in which you fight waves of enemies. Just like other games (Left for Dead for example).
- Compared with ACM, multiplayer is quite the same. It offers less modes but you can play as more characters.
In-game bugs and screen tearing in singleplayer and multiplayer.
There are no bugs - except the Aliens themselves - in this game.
- Compared with ACM, there are no bugs or screen tearing. AVP is better.
Graphics
The graphics of this game are really good. If you compare this game to A:CM, AVP offers much more detail. With DX11 you will enjoy high end graphics. If you have a good pc you can play this game with maximum settings. Humans, Aliens and Predators look very good. Facial expressions are good. Lightning effects and environments are exceptional detailed. AVP is the best looking Alien game until now.
- The graphics of AVP are much better then ACM graphics if you focus on detail. But ACM offers an 80's setting. If you like detail go for AVP. If you like 'old school' style and resemblance to Aliens (1986), go for ACM. All in all, AVP offers superb graphics.
Sound
The sound of this game is really good. The Alien and Predator sounds are very good. But if you compare the sound of the weapons in this game with the weapons in Alien,  Predator or AVP movies, they are not the same. ACM offers better sounds.
- If you compare the sound of this game to ACM, both are quite good. Although I prefer the sound of ACM weaponary. The sounds of the Alien in AVP are very good. Sounds of both games are good.
Replayability
Replayability of the game is high because of the three distinct campaigns and the multiplayer options. It offers no co - op mode like ACM.
- Both AVP and ACM offer high replayability if you are Alien fan like me. ACM offers co - op unlike AVP and more multiplayer modes. ACM wins.
Conclusion
AVP 3 from 2010 is a game that delivers the AVP universe in a fresh setting. Because it offers unique campaigns, you will play this game again. The graphics of this game are unique. Much better then ACM graphics. They are not so good like Crysis 3 for example, but they are still very good. The story of the game is mediocre. The latest installment of the AVP series offers superb graphics and animations, a mediocre story, good sounds, three distinct playable characters and fun multiplayer modes.
AVP has better graphics then ACM, three campaigns with different characters and fun multiplayer modes. It is not movie related but it offers a decent story.
All in all, AVP is not as good as ACM. Co - op, upgradable weapons and better multiplayer modes and DLC belong to ACM.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The good
* Based on a existing franchise;
* Very good graphics;
* Three distinct stories;
* Multiplayer and survival mode are very good;
* Fresh and innovative gameplay.
The bad
* No co - op modes;
* No upgradable weapons;
* Less multiplayer modes compared to ACM.
* No canon story.
FINAL VERDICT: 7.5 out of 10.

Doom 3 is, frankly, not very good. The core problem here is the level design; the levels are cramped and bland, the solutions to several mandatory puzzles are painfully obtuse, and overall simply figuring which way is "out" is an exercise in both tedium and frustration.
Heck, even the actual gameflow that made the first two Doom games the timeless classics that they are is completely butchered. Your nameless marine stumbles around at a pace that makes a Call of Duty protagonist look like Usain Bolt, most enemies take way longer to kill than they reasonably should, and any sense of weapon balance is thrown right out the window. And for what, exactly? Dark rooms (countered by a flashlight that runs on a rapidly recharging battery) and jump scares. Yes, you'll often be ambushed by enemies who literally spawn in right behind you, leading to an ungodly amount of insanely dull firefights.
It's particularly jarring since the BFG Edition comes packaged with the first two Doom games, which play entirely differently, and are, for that matter, infinitely better in almost every respect. Heck, they're both so darn good that I would recommend buying BFG for them alone-- except that they're on sale on Steam in other capacities, and much cheaper to boot.
How the mighty have fallen.

This is one of those games with a lot of potential, and also one of those games that never quite lived up to it.
The premise is simple. The game takes place on a 2d plane. Your ships can be customized and designed very similar to Gratuitous Space Battles. Any wacky ship design you want, you can build. The game is also highly mod friendly, which is a huge plus in my book.
You colonize planets, design ships, build fleets, and conquer the galaxy. Simple enough.
Problem is that the game is highly buggy, full of memory leaks and other instabilities. This is a real shame considering how brilliant the game design is. There is just no polish and little to no bug fixing that was done. Be prepared to have your game either slow down to an unplayable crawl and/or crash to desktop continually.
Lots of potential but poor execution. Avoid this game unless you like frustration.
